(2) Add `_fun_grad_cap(h, delta)` mirroring `_num_and_dq`/`_backprop`: Lf = [0, conv(h,h), 0]; c = (1-delta)*max(Lf); w_j = 1 where Lf_j < c, 0 above, with a linear ramp of width 0.1*delta*c across the boundary; val = -log(sum_j w_j*Lf_j) + 2*log(sum h); dLf_j = -w_j/(sum_j w_j*Lf_j) (plus nothing on the max term), then grad = _backprop(dLf, h) + 2/sum h. (3) Run 5 stages delta in {0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.002, 0.001}, each ~120 L-BFGS iterations in log coordinates (reuse `_lbfgs_log` with fg = lambda hh: _fun_grad_cap(hh, delta)), rescale after each, keep the best by exact R. (4) Diversity: repeat the whole delta schedule from 3 log-normal perturbations of the coarse record (sigma=0.10 on log h applied to a random 30% of cells), ~4 s each, keep the global best coarse array. A step function on a NON-UNIFORM grid with free breakpoints can place arbitrarily fine steps exactly at the two ramps and coarse ones across the plateau; it contains the uniform construction as a special case, and being only 2K+1 parameters it is not trapped by the saturated, million-dimensional gradient that blocks the record.

Parameterise u_i=log h_i and v_i=log(b_{i+1}-b_i) so ordering is free; optimise log R with L-BFGS-B and forward finite differences (step 1e-6, 2K+1 params), clipping gaps to [1e-4,1]. Schedule: 30 random multistarts at K=10 (log-uniform heights in [1e-2,1e2], Dirichlet(1) gaps) run ~80 iterations each, keep the best 5; then continuation K -> 20 -> 40 -> 80 -> 128 by splitting every step in half (which preserves f exactly) and re-optimising ~60 iterations per level; print R at every K. Finally rasterise the best f onto a uniform grid N=32768 by exact cell-overlap averaging and spend the last 20 s on the standard uniform machinery (beta ladder 1e3..1e7 plus peak-window polish) so the two parameterisations are directly comparable.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has absorbed ~170 failed moves; every first-order/mass/coarse-restart idea returns the start, so a further gain there needs a different *operator*, not a different perturbation. Exact R's gradient sees only the argmax knot, yet 42.8% of knots are within 5% of max and only 18.2% within 0.1% — there is a smooth, second-order-flavoured residual ('flatten the near-max knots') whose Jacobian is the convolution operator. I bet slot 1 on a damped Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt solve of that residual. T52's free-breakpoint idea died on an O(K^4) evaluator and 85 s CPU, not on its premise; the exact trapezoid-jump representation makes it O(K^2 log K), so slot 2 re-tests it properly. L9 is the only line compounding (~1e-3/cycle after the 65536 lift), so slot 3 simply continues that ladder with betas scaled to the finer grid and time reserved for 131072.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a critical point of exact R because R's gradient is carried by the single argmax knot; the many knots 0.1%-5% below max contribute only through ||g||_2^2, so no first-order direction can flatten them (F604's capped-sum gradient and F598's coarse restarts both stalled). But the residual r_j = Lmax - L_j over the top window is a smooth function of h with Jacobian A = 2*(delta * h) (a convolution), which is far better conditioned than dR/dh. A damped Gauss-Newton step on ||A delta - r||^2 can therefore move mass in a direction the exact-R gradient cannot express; a line search on exact R keeps only genuine gains.
experiments.change: From p0670 (N=169984): (1) rescale, print R. (2) Build the top window W = indices j with L_j >= 0.70*Lmax on the knot array from _knots (print |W| and the quantiles of r_j = Lmax - L_j on W). (3) Implement the Jacobian operator exactly: matvec(d) = 2*fftconvolve(d, h)[1:N] restricted to W, and its adjoint matvecT(w) at i = 2*sum_j h_{j-i} w_j (use fftconvolve with h reversed, as in _backprop), with delta restricted to cells where h > 1e-6*max(h). (4) Run 25 CG iterations on (A^T A + lam*I) delta = A^T r with lam = 1e-6*||A^T r||/||delta|| scale, then normalise delta so max|delta| = 0.05*max(h). (5) Line search s in {1,1/2,...,1/256}: h_s = clip(h + s*delta, 0, None), rescale, compute exact R; take the best s with R > R_best + 1e-13 and print R at each s. (6) On acceptance run one beta=0 L-BFGS restricted to a peak window of frac 0.05 (100 iters) plus one full beta=0 pass (100 iters); if no s improves, shrink the window to 0.85*Lmax and repeat step 2-5. Loop inside the deadline with per-stage time caps (each CG+line search <= 8 s), always keeping the best exact R; leave >= 2 s for a final sharp polish and return the best array.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941450 (beat 0.941243). Diagnostics: the printed |W|, and the RMS / 90th-percentile of r_j before and after each accepted step - a falling residual together with rising exact R means the top really was the binding deficit; a residual that cannot fall, or an R that falls whenever the residual falls, says the loss is in the f*f ramps/tails and the next main-line bet must attack edge steepness instead.

experiments.hypothesis: p0694's premise (a non-uniform breakpoint step function can put arbitrarily fine steps exactly at the two f*f ramps, which the uniform grid cannot) was never tested: it died because _eval_fg looped over ~K^2 knots building a K x K overlap matrix at each, i.e. O(K^4) time and memory, and finite differences over 2K+1 parameters made that hopeless. f*f of a step function is exactly piecewise linear with knots at b_i+b_j, and its derivative is a sum of K^2 box functions, so g and all of its knot values can be built exactly in O(K^2 log K) by accumulating +-h_i h_j jumps at b_i+b_j, b_i+b_j+min(w_i,w_j), b_i+b_j+max(w_i,w_j), b_i+b_j+w_i+w_j and prefix-summing. With that evaluator the free-breakpoint search is cheap enough to actually run its K ladder.
experiments.change: Start from Code Zero; write a new module from scratch (do not reuse p0694). (1) Exact evaluator: given breakpoints b (K+1) and heights h (K), set a=b_i+b_j, m=min(w_i,w_j), M=max(w_i,w_j) for all K^2 pairs (vectorised outer sums), accumulate jumps +h_i h_j at a and at a+M, -h_i h_j at a+m and at a+m+M into a single sorted unique breakpoint array via np.add.at, prefix-sum to get g, then ||g||_2^2 by exact trapezoid sums, ||g||inf = max of g at knots (or 0 at the ends), ||g||_1 = (sum h_i w_i)^2. Verify on 3 random K=6 examples that this matches R computed by rasterising f onto N=20000 and np.convolve to 1e-6; print the check and abort to a plain uniform start if it fails. (2) Optimise log R over (log h, log gaps) with L-BFGS-B and forward differences; ladder K = 8 -> 16 -> 32 -> 64 -> 128 by splitting each step in half (exactly preserves f, so R is unchanged at the split), ~60 iterations per level, 12 random multistarts at K=8 including at least 4 with spiky heights (3-5 large values, rest 1e-2) and Dirichlet(0.3) gaps so a few cells can become very narrow. (3) Enforce time: check time.process_time() before every multistart and every ladder level; if < 15 s remain stop the ladder. (4) Rasterise the best f onto N=32768 by exact cell-overlap averaging (vectorised via np.add.at on cumulative-mass, no Python double loop), then spend the remaining time on the standard machinery: beta ladder {1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7} global log L-BFGS + peak-window block polish, keeping best exact R. Print R at every K, the three smallest gaps, and the positions of the 8 narrowest cells relative to the f*f argmax.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a critical point of exact R because R's gradient is carried by the single argmax knot; the many knots 0.1%-5% below max contribute only through ||g||_2^2, so no first-order direction can flatten them (F604's capped-sum gradient and F598's coarse restarts both stalled). But the residual r_j = Lmax - L_j over the top window is a smooth function of h with Jacobian A = 2*(delta * h) (a convolution), which is far better conditioned than dR/dh. A damped Gauss-Newton step on ||A delta - r||^2 can therefore move mass in a direction the exact-R gradient cannot express; a line search on exact R keeps only genuine gains.

experiments.hypothesis: p0694's premise (a non-uniform breakpoint step function can put arbitrarily fine steps exactly at the two f*f ramps, which the uniform grid cannot) was never tested: it died because _eval_fg looped over ~K^2 knots building a K x K overlap matrix at each, i.e. O(K^4) time and memory, and finite differences over 2K+1 parameters made that hopeless. f*f of a step function is exactly piecewise linear with knots at b_i+b_j, and its derivative is a sum of K^2 box functions, so g and all of its knot values can be built exactly in O(K^2 log K) by accumulating +-h_i h_j jumps at b_i+b_j, b_i+b_j+min(w_i,w_j), b_i+b_j+max(w_i,w_j), b_i+b_j+w_i+w_j and prefix-summing. plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has resisted 100+ distinct local moves (GN, coarse ladders, warps, soft-max, flooding, block refits), so the record family is a strong attractor for smooth perturbations. Only two facts still look exploitable: (i) all record-preserving optimisers work on a *fixed discretisation*, and the discrete R depends on where the stair-function grid sits relative to the smooth shape — a DOF that has produced real gains on L3 (F470) and L8 (F602) but was never systematically scanned on the record; (ii) the ramp of f*f near the support ends is the main remaining loss (57% of knots are >5% below max), and an analytic x^-p edge term is the classical way to flatten that ramp — the parametric edge family reached 0.882 from scratch but has never been added on top of the 0.9412 construction. I bet on those two, plus one structured-perturbation robustness test of the record that also tells us whether to keep spending on it. L9 and T53 are both stalled at 0-gain steps, so I keep the main slot on the record.

experiments.hypothesis: The record resists single-cell and peak-window perturbations, but no one has tested *block-structured* multiplicative perturbations spanning a range of scales (from 1/64 to 1/512 of the support) with a strong beta continuation. Such moves relocate mass at the scale where the plateau shape is decided, and the high-beta polish then redistributes it; if any of them lands in a slightly better configuration the subsequent sharp polish will keep it.

Print per-round: block size, a, pre-polish R, post-polish R, and whether accepted. Keep the best over the whole run and return it.

If every round returns exactly 0.941243 with identical knot statistics (18.24/34.55/42.77), the basin is closed to block-scale perturbation up to 3% and the main line should be moved to a fresh basin; any accepted round with a different argmax/plateau fraction is the real signal.

experiments.hypothesis: R is computed from the stair-function f, so the *discretisation phase* of the grid relative to the underlying smooth shape is a genuine degree of freedom that all record optimisers have held fixed. Fractional-shift resampling gave real gains on L3 (F470) and L8 (F602). T53's warp failed because it distorted the shape; a pure sub-cell shift does not distort, it only re-rasterises the same mass on a different grid, and the best discrete R over shifts can exceed the current one and then be polished further.

experiments.hypothesis: The remaining loss in R is the two ramps of f*f near the support ends (only 42.8% of knots are within 5% of max). plan.analysis: The record is a genuine critical point of exact R at every resolution (F288: 103 failures, F429/F615/F616/F617/F621/F622 all zero). Local refinement is dead: single-cell, block, peak-window, edge-term, warp, and GN-on-top-knots moves all return 0.941243. So the three slots should not refine locally. (1) I bet on basin-hopping that is allowed to travel downhill at coarse N and only then escalated — every prior escape was greedy. (2) T54's edge-mass premise is refuted (F622), so I pivot to the one objective that is flatness-aware over ALL knots rather than just the max: a normalized deficit sum with full global gradient, then screened by exact R. (3) Bold: a genuinely different search — alternating-projection / flat-target deconvolution, which never uses R's gradient at all and aims directly at the theoretical optimum f*f = const.

experiments.hypothesis: Every escape from 0.941243 has been greedy (accept only improvements), so the search can never cross the shallow ridge around the critical point. At coarse N the ridge is wider and cheap to cross; a Metropolis walk there that accepts worse shapes, then re-escalated, may land on a coarse shape whose escalated version beats the record.
experiments.change: Replace p0703's GN/coarsen front end with a simulated-annealing basin-hop ladder. (a) Resample p0703 to N0=2048 by mass-conserving cumulative-mass interpolation (np.interp on cumsum, then diff, clip>=0, _rescale). (b) At the current level, loop until 40% of the CPU budget: propose a perturbation = pick 1-3 contiguous windows whose length is drawn log-uniform from [N/64, N/8]; multiply each window's heights by exp(U(-a,a)) with a drawn from {0.03, 0.10, 0.30}, or (1 time in 3) replace a window by its own mean times exp(U(-0.25,0.25)); then run _lbfgs_log(h, 150 iters, cap+1.5 s, beta=0) and _rescale. Compute exact R; accept if dR>0 else with probability exp(dR/T), T annealed geometrically 3e-4 -> 3e-6 over the level's iterations. Keep best-in-level separately from current. (c) Escalate best-in-level by mass-conserving interpolation x2, run _lbfgs_log(300, 2 s) + _peak_window block polish, and repeat up to N=84992; finish with _polish and return max(exact R, base R). Print, for each level, best-in-level R and the record's own resampled R at that level.
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.941250. Decisive diagnostic: whether best-in-level R at N=2048-8192 climbs at least +2e-4 above p0703's own resampled R at that level (that would be the first coarse-level escape ever seen here) and survives escalation; if every level stays within 1e-5 of the resampled record, the record's basin is genuinely coarse-stable and the ramp loss is structural.

experiments.hypothesis: T54's edge-mass idea is dead (F622: the record's edges are already optimal), so the leftover deficit must be attacked where the exact-R gradient is blind: over the whole knot profile. The normalized flatness deficit G(h)=sum_j (L_j/Lmax - 1)^2 over ALL 2N+1 knots has a real gradient on every knot (including the ramps and the plateau shoulders), unlike R whose gradient sees only the argmax knot, and unlike F615's GN which used only knots above 0.7*Lmax.
experiments.change: Add to p0713's module a function _flat(h) returning G and its gradient: with L=_knots(h), M=L.max(), m=int(np.argmax(L)), S2=sum_j (L_j/M-1)*(L_j/M), set gL[k] = 2*(L[k]-M)/M^2 for all k, then subtract 2*S2/M from gL[m]; h-gradient = _backprop(np.concatenate(([0],gL,[0])) , h). Drive it with the existing _lbfgs_log(h, 400, cap, fg=_flat) from p0713, then evaluate exact R and, only if R improved by >1e-9, run _polish. Loop until deadline over variants: (i) all knots, (ii) only knots with L_j > 0.5*M, (iii) G blended as G - 0.02*log R, each with 1-2 random restarts produced by multiplying a random 10% window by exp(U(-0.05,0.05)) first. Print G(start), G(end), and exact R for every variant, and keep the best exact R.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941260 on T54's own best. experiments.hypothesis: R=1 iff f*f is constant on its support, but every program so far optimizes R or a smoothed max. Alternating projection toward a flat target uses no R gradient at all: repeatedly flatten the current f*f (a gamma-compression of its knot values), refit h to that target by least squares on the exact autoconvolution, and anneal gamma toward 0. This is a different kind of search and should produce a construction with a genuinely different structure (low max/mean, no zeros) rather than a local variant of the record.
experiments.change: From Code Zero, work on a ladder N = 512 -> 2048 -> 8192 -> 32768 -> 84992. At each N: start from the escalated previous h (at N=512 start from h = ones(512)). Loop until 80% of the budget: compute g = fftconvolve(h,h) (length 2N-1), M = g.max(); form the target t_j = M * (g_j/M)^gamma with gamma drawn from {0.8,0.5,0.25,0.1} (annealing lower as iterations succeed), then rescale t so that sum(t) equals sum(g) (mass matching); fit h to t by L-BFGS on log-heights (only cells above 1e-12*max) minimizing ||conv(h,h) - s*t||^2/s^2 with s = (sum(conv*h))/sum(t) recomputed analytically each evaluation, gradient via 4*fftconvolve(residual, h[::-1], 'valid')[:N]; cap each fit at 30 iterations or 1.5 s. After each fit compute the exact R_of(h); track the best exact R and its h; every 10 successful fits, also run _lbfgs_log(best, 100, cap, beta=0) as a keeper step. Escalate the best-exact-R h to the next N by mass-conserving cumulative interpolation and _rescale. At N=84992 finish with _polish and return the best. Print the target residual, the exact R, zero fraction and max/mean at each level.

plan.analysis: Every local move on p0703 is exhausted (~200 held failures), and the record is an *exact 2x staircase*: since R is invariant to x-scaling, every dyadic coarsen/lift ladder is literally the identity on the shape, which explains a whole class of no-op failures (F429/F571/F598/F617). Two levers remain untried. (1) Spectral/nonlocal: R's loss is the shape of g=f*f versus flat, so correct |F| toward the spectrum of a prescribed trapezoid target, keeping F's phase — a move no gradient of R can make. (2) Alternating projection in the g-domain: T55's real failure was mechanical (np.convolve at N>=2048 is O(N^2), so its ladder never left N=512) plus the constant being an exact fixed point of gamma-compression; both are fixable. Slot 3 attacks the staircase degeneracy with non-dyadic resampling before a beta-homotopy.

experiments.hypothesis: R is determined by how flat g=f*f is, and g must die at both ends; the record's |F|^2 spectrum is far from the sinc-like spectrum of a flat/trapezoid g. Pointwise reshaping of |F| toward the target spectrum (phase kept, so f stays roughly the same non-negative shape) is a nonlocal move that is invisible to the exact-R gradient and has never been tried on the record.
experiments.change: In p0703's module add a stage before the existing polish. (a) Coarsen the start exactly by pairwise mean to M=42496 (it is an exact 2x staircase, so this is lossless); work there. (b) For ramp fraction rho in {0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20}: build target g_t on the same 2M-1 length as conv(h,h): plateau of height (max(conv)/1.0) on [rho*S, (1-rho)*S], linear ramps to 0 at both ends (S = support length in samples), then rescale g_t so sum(g_t)=sum(conv(h,h)) and so max(g_t)=max(conv(h,h)). (c) nfft = next_fast_len(4*M); F = np.fft.rfft(h, nfft); T = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(g_t, nfft)); for alpha in {0.05,0.10,0.20,0.35,0.5}: Fn = (np.abs(F)**(1-alpha)) * (T**alpha) * np.exp(1j*np.angle(F)); hn = np.fft.irfft(Fn, nfft)[:M]; hn = np.clip(hn,0,None); if hn.sum()<=0 skip; hn=_rescale(hn); rn=R_of(hn); if rn > bestR: keep. (d) After each accepted alpha, run the existing _short_polish (2 s cap) at M, then prolongate the best back to 84992 (cumulative-mass interp) and run _polish to the deadline. Loop over rho/alpha with alpha halved each outer round until 90% of budget. Print, each round: corr = dot(|F|^2, T^2)/norms, alpha, rho, raw R before polish and after. Use fftconvolve everywhere; never np.convolve at M>=1500.

Replace the self-referential compression by a prescribed trapezoid target (rectangle's triangle != trapezoid, so the constant is not a fixed point) and fix the convolution cost.
experiments.change: Keep p0722's ladder but change three things. (1) Replace every np.convolve(h,h) and np.convolve(h,d) with fftconvolve (nfft via scipy.fft.next_fast_len >= 4N) in _R_of, _fit's fg and _polish; keep the analytic gradient formula but compute the correlation with fftconvolve(grad_g, h[::-1], mode='valid')[:N]. (2) Seed N=512 with a non-constant profile: 16 log-uniform random block heights (rng seed 0..3, each block width 8-40 cells) passed through _rescale, not ones(512); also keep ones(512) as one candidate only. (3) Replace the gamma target: for rho in {0.30,0.20,0.15,0.10,0.05} build the trapezoid on the length-2N-1 grid (plateau height chosen so sum(target)=sum(conv(h,h)), max(target)=max(conv(h,h))), fit h to it with the existing log-height L-BFGS (mass-matched, <=200 iters, <=2 s), evaluate exact R, and keep the best h over all rho; then apply one keeper L-BFGS on exact R (beta=0) for 1 s. Escalate the best-R h by cumulative-mass interpolation to 2048, 8192, 32768, 84992 (cap 20% of remaining budget per level), finish with _polish and return the best exact-R h. Print at each level: rho, residual ||conv(h,h)-g_t||/||g_t||, exact R, zero fraction, max/mean.

Prolongate back to 169984 and polish once. Print each accepted warp's amplitudes and the raw R it attains before polish.

plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record has resisted every local move at its own construction (GN, soft-max, warps, edges, upsampling), so it is a local optimum in shape space. Two bets remain: (a) the same moves on a different near-record basin can work — p0293 is only 1.3e-5 lower but has f*f argmax 0.171 vs 0.573, so its geometry differs; (b) T57's warp test was mechanically broken (raw R printed negative, Nelder-Mead never left zero), so the warp hypothesis is untested. For a genuinely new direction, I bet a sparse spike-mixture from scratch finds a basin the dense optimizers cannot reach.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's near-max plateau is too flat and symmetric for Gauss-Newton to improve, but p0293's f*f is one-sided (argmax 0.171) with a smaller near-max set; a damped GN step on all knots within kappa of max, with residual weighting that does not penalize the far flank, can flatten p0293's top and surpass 0.941243.
experiments.change: Load p0293 (N=42496, R=0.941230). Implement a damped Gauss-Newton step on residuals L_j - Lmax for all knots with L_j >= kappa*Lmax, Jacobian J[j,i] = h[j-1-i] + h[j+1-i], solving (J^T J + lam I)d = -J^T r by 60 CG iterations. Sweep kappa in {0.05,0.02,0.01}, lam in {1e-6,1e-4,1e-2}. Accept h+d only if exact R increases (backtracking). plan.analysis: 60+ generations have failed to move 0.941243, and every failure was a *global* move on that construction: fine-grid lifts, global warps, rigid sub-cell shifts, prescribed g-targets, Gauss-Newton on the plateau, SA. What has never been varied is the *local* fine structure at the two ends of f, where g must jump from 0 to its max. The record's max/mean of 147.28 means its toe is a single cell of height 147 at N=84992 — g therefore rises quadratically (slope 0) off both ends, which is exactly where the 5.9% gap lives. A toe that is 3x taller/narrower (a cell-average x^-1/2 profile) converts that quadratic rise into a near-jump, and that needs ~10x the resolution plus a *targeted* initialization, not a full-array L-BFGS prolongation which drowns the ~3 toe coordinates among 1e6. Slot 3 tests the complementary local degree of freedom (non-rigid, per-block sub-cell shifts) that the failed global warps and rigid shifts never covered.

experiments.hypothesis: R's remaining deficit is concentrated in the two ramps of f*f, which start with zero slope because each toe of f is one finite cell wide (max/mean 147.28). At ~10x the resolution the toe can be made ~3x taller and narrower, which turns the quadratic ramp into a near-jump and should raise R; earlier 'upsample + full L-BFGS' attempts (F429/F523) failed only because the toe is a handful of coordinates among 1e6, so initialize the toe analytically and freeze the interior.
experiments.change: Load start (N=84992, exact 2x staircase). Measure one exact-R eval at N=340k and choose k in {11,8,6,4} as the largest with k*84992 <= 1e6 and one R eval (fftconvolve, next_fast_len>=4N) under ~0.15 s. Build h by mass-conserving cumulative interpolation to N=k*84992. Let K=4096. For p in {0.30,0.40,0.50,0.60}: overwrite the first K cells with the cell averages of x^-p, h_new[j]=A*((j+1)^(1-p)-j^(1-p)), A chosen so the K-cell mass equals the original first-K mass; do the same independently at the right end with its own mass (so the two ends are allowed to differ); also try a capped variant A=min(A,cap) for cap in {2x,5x} times the old toe height, renormalizing mass. Print raw exact R for every (p,cap,sideness) candidate before any optimization. Take the best raw candidate (and the unchanged start as a control) and run L-BFGS on log-heights restricted to the first K and last K cells only (all other cells frozen; use the program's existing exact-R value/gradient in log coordinates, ftol 1e-20, active-set on heights > 1e-13*max) with a 10 s cap each; accept only if exact R improves. With the remaining time (deadline 0.90*budget, checked every iteration) re-run the block L-BFGS with K doubled, then one full-array L-BFGS polish (<=6 s) and a peak-window polish on the winner; return the best exact-R construction.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941260-0.941320. Diagnostic: (i) the raw (pre-optimization) power-law toe must already beat 0.941243 for some p near 0.5, otherwise the ramp is not toe-limited; (ii) the accepted result should show max/mean > 147.28 and >18.24% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max; (iii) if raw R drops for every p but the block L-BFGS climbs back to exactly 0.941243, the record's toe is optimal at its own scale and the limit is elsewhere.

experiments.hypothesis: T58's premise (a sparse few-spike + low-background profile can give a flat-topped f*f) was never actually tested: p0740 spent the whole budget in differential evolution at N=2048, was killed at 85 s, and only reported 0.5876. A vectorized random search over a cheap capped-block family with exact-R scoring at N=1024, then Nelder-Mead and a normal escalation+polish, is affordable within 60 s and will establish whether the family contains any basin above 0.85.
experiments.change: Start from p0001 (trivial). Do NOT call differential_evolution. At N=1024 evaluate exact R with fftconvolve (next_fast_len>=4N) on the family h(x)=B+sum_{k=1..4} A_k*1{|x-c_k|<w_k} rasterized by cell-overlap (12 parameters: log B, log A_k, c_k, log w_k; log-uniform A_k in [1,300], w_k in [0.005,0.15], c_k uniform in [0,1], B log-uniform in [0.01,3]). Draw 400 random parameter vectors in one vectorized batch (each eval ~1 ms at N=1024; assert the batch takes <5 s or shrink it), print the best R and the number of blocks with A_k>2B. Take the top 5 through Nelder-Mead on exact R (maxiter 400, xatol 1e-6). Rasterize the winner at N=8192, prolongate by cumulative mass to 32768, then run log-height L-BFGS on exact R (maxiter 300), then beta-softmax homotopy betas 1e2,1e3,1e4 (150 iters each), then 3 peak-window block polishes (frac 0.05,0.10,0.20). Check time.process_time() after every stage against deadline=0.90*budget and stop staging early rather than being killed; print R, zero fraction, max/mean and the f*f argmax fraction after each stage; return the best exact-R array (never the raw start).
experiments.prediction: Hard target: a valid program beating the track's 0.666667 (the first random batch should do that in seconds); aim 0.85-0.88 after escalation. Diagnostic: if the winning family member keeps A_k>2B for only one block, the spike+background premise collapses to a single spike and the track should be redirected to a block-profile family; if several blocks survive with a broad flat top, the track has a real basin worth refining next generation.

experiments.hypothesis: F621's fractional sub-cell shift failed on the record because a *global* shift of a 2x-staircase shape is a rigid motion (R-invariant up to endpoints) — the same reason global coordinate warps (F640/F645) died. The identical cumulative-mass remap applied *independently inside many blocks* is non-rigid: it can sharpen or re-stack features at sub-coarse-cell scale while conserving each block's mass, a degree of freedom no previous experiment on this construction exercised.
experiments.change: Load p0703 (N=84992, exact 2x staircase). Coarsen losslessly by pairing to M=42496 and verify exact R matches the start to 1e-12 (print both). Split into 166 contiguous blocks of B=256 coarse cells. For a per-block shift vector delta in [-0.5,0.5]^166, rebuild h' with block-local cumulative-mass interpolation: within block [a,b), with F the block's own cumulative mass extended by F(x<a)=0, F(x>=b)=block mass, set h'_j = F(j+1+delta_b) - F(j+delta_b) for a<=j<b (this conserves the block mass exactly and leaves other blocks untouched); clip at 0, rescale. Stage A: single-block raw-R scan, for each block try delta_b in {-0.4,-0.2,+0.2,+0.4} and record max |dR| (print the 5 best blocks and the max). Stage B: 300 random delta vectors (Gaussian sigma 0.15, and a second batch sigma 0.35), keep the best. Stage C: coordinate descent over blocks in random order with 3-point line search delta_b in {-0.3,0,+0.3}, 3 sweeps, keeping any improvement (exact R only, no gradient). Stage D: decoarsen the winner back to N=84992 by cell duplication and spend the remaining time (deadline 0.90*budget, checked each sweep) on 2 short full L-BFGS polishes (<=5 s each) plus a peak-window polish at frac 0.05; return the best exact-R array. Print R after every stage.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941260. Diagnostic: if Stage A shows max single-block |dR| < 1e-7 for every block and Stages B/C never beat 0.941243 by more than the noise floor, the record is stationary under non-rigid sub-cell rearrangement as well — a much stronger statement than the failed global warps, and it tells the search to attack the shape at a scale coarser than these blocks (or abandon this construction). If instead a handful of blocks (likely near the two toes or the f*f argmax at 0.573 of support) carry the gain, report their positions and sizes.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has resisted ~200 tests; it is an exact 2x staircase, stationary under global warps, block shifts (F650, only 10 s used), GN, resampling and higher-N duplication (F288). Two leads remain unexploited: F651's power-law toe overwrite at ~4x resolution never actually ran (ImportError on next_fast_len), and F650's own diagnostic says to test rearrangement at a COARSER block scale than its 256 cells. Meanwhile T58's p0749 (0.794099) is a genuinely different smooth basin that overran its budget (82 s) and never got the standard beta/peak-window escalation. I bet slot 1 on the unexecuted toe test, slot 2 on the coarse-scale block stationarity follow-up, slot 3 on properly escalating the T58 basin.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's remaining deficit sits in the two f*f ramps, which start with zero slope because each toe of f is a single finite cell (max/mean 147.28, 6.9% zeros, argmax at 0.573). At 4x resolution a power-law toe can reshape the ramp while conserving mass, raising ||f*f||_2^2 without raising the max. This exact test has never been executed: F651 died on an ImportError before running.
experiments.change: Use `from scipy.fft import next_fast_len` (NOT scipy.signal) everywhere. Load start (N=84992), rescale to Lmax=1. Duplicate each cell k=4 times to N=339968 (exact same step function); verify exact R matches the start to 1e-9 and print both. Toe surgery: left window of W cells and right window of W cells, W in {256, 1024, 4096} fine cells counted from each support end; inside a window replace heights by A*((i+0.5)/W)**p for p in {0.5,1,1.5,2,3} (mirror with an independent exponent on the right), with A set so the window's total mass is unchanged (clip at 0, rescale); also try a capped variant min(A, c*((i+0.5)/W)**p). Score every variant with exact R (fftconvolve, nfft=next_fast_len(4N)) and print a table. Take the best variant, then run bounded log-height L-BFGS restricted to the two toe windows (maxiter 200, deadline-guarded), then a full-array log L-BFGS on exact R (maxiter 150) plus a beta ladder (1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5) and a peak-window polish at frac 0.05/0.10; always keep the best exact-R array. Loop surgery+polish with new p values until time.process_time() > 0.88*budget; never return the raw start. Print R after each stage and the final N.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941255-0.941300. Diagnostic: if no raw (pre-optimisation) power-law toe beats 0.941243 - 1e-5 at k=4 for any p and W, and polishing never recovers it, then the ramp deficit is not a resolution/toe-width artefact and this construction is settled; if one variant already wins raw, report the winning p, W and side.

experiments.hypothesis: F650 only tested rearrangement inside fixed 256-cell blocks and quit at 10 s of a 60 s budget. Its own diagnostic calls for attacking at a scale coarser than those blocks. If the record is stationary under 8- and 16-block mass-conserving rearrangement and per-block mass scaling as well, a much stronger statement holds; if a few large blocks carry gain, we learn where the record is rigid.
experiments.change: Load p0703 (N=84992), pair-coarsen to M=42496, verify exact R equals the start to 1e-12 (print both). Partition into K blocks with K in {8, 16} (B = M/K coarse cells). Stage A: for each partition, per-block cumulative-mass remap h'_j = F(j+1+delta_b)-F(j+delta_b) inside block b (block mass conserved), delta grid {-0.5,-0.35,-0.2,0,0.2,0.35,0.5}, single-block raw-R scan; print the 5 best blocks and their positions. Stage B: coordinate descent over blocks in random order, 3-value line search, 3 sweeps per partition, accepting only exact-R improvements above 1e-9. Stage C: per-block multiplicative scaling m_b in {0.98,0.99,1.0,1.01,1.02} by coordinate descent, 2 sweeps (mass-changing degree of freedom). Repeat partitions A-C in a loop with fresh random orders until 55% of budget, always keeping the best exact R. Then decoarsen the winner to N=84992 and spend ALL remaining time (deadline 0.90*budget) alternating full log L-BFGS on exact R (120 iters, 4 s caps) with peak-window block polish at frac 0.05 and 0.10 and a beta pass at 1e4. Never return the raw start; print R, delta and block index after every stage and the final best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941248-0.941260; judged against the track's 0.941243. Diagnostic: if every single-block |dR| < 1e-7 in Stage A for both partitions and no stage beats the noise floor, the record is stationary under coarse-scale non-rigid rearrangement, and the main line should abandon this construction rather than keep perturbing it. If a few large blocks (expect near 0.57 of support or near a toe) carry the gain, report their indices and shift sizes.

experiments.hypothesis: p0749's spike+block+background basin reached 0.794099 but consumed 82.7 s of CPU (killed late) and never got the standard beta-homotopy / peak-window escalation at high N. With hard deadline guards and a proper resolution ladder this basin should climb into the 0.86-0.89 range that L9-type basins reach, telling us whether this family is a real competitor or a dead end.
experiments.change: Start from p0749's array (N=8192). Rewrite every stage with a hard `if time.process_time() > cap: break` guard so CPU never exceeds 0.88*budget; print elapsed after each stage. Ladder: for N in (8192, 16384, 32768, 65536) (cumulative-mass prolongation between levels), at each level run: (1) log-height L-BFGS on exact R with analytic gradient (fftconvolve, next_fast_len>=4N), maxiter 200; (2) beta-softmax homotopy beta in (1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5), 120 iters each; (3) peak-window block L-BFGS at fracs 0.05, 0.10, 0.20 and also a window centred on the left and right ramps of f*f (where L is between 0.1 and 0.9 of max); always keep the best exact-R array. If time remains after the ladder, repeat levels 32768/65536 with a fresh beta ladder. Report after every stage: N, R, zero fraction, max/mean, frac of f*f knots within 0.1%/1% of max, and f*f argmax fraction.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.86-0.88 (hard minimum: strictly beat the track's 0.794099). Diagnostic: if max/mean stays below ~10 and the fraction within 0.1% of max stays under ~1% even after the beta ladder at N=65536, this family tops out as a smooth craggy basin and T58 should be retired; if max/mean starts rising with sparse spikes appearing, the basin is morphing toward the record's structure and deserves another generation.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 is a proven-hard local optimum: 109 documented failures of resampling, toe surgery, warps, softmax, GN, DOF-splitting. Everything tried attacks the *max* of f*f. But R's numerator is a sum of squares over ALL knots while the denominator is only the max — so the untapped reserve is the shoulder band (5–40% below max, 57% of knots), not the top plateau. New: (a) target a shoulder-lifting objective instead of smoothing the max; (b) note that at an exactly-equal 2x/4x split the antisymmetric sub-cell direction has zero gradient by symmetry, which explains F659's null result — randomising the split breaks that saddle; (c) a spectral (Wiener) square-root family f = IFFT(sqrt(FFT(g_target))) gives a principled, untested from-scratch construction. Betting main line on shoulder-lifting, exploration on symmetry-breaking at 4x, bold on spectral square root.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's deficit is in the shoulders of f*f (only 42.8% of knots lie within 5% of max), not in its top. The exact-R gradient devotes almost nothing to them because the max term dominates. Directly maximising the numerator's contribution from a band just below the max, with the max itself hinge-penalised, should raise ||f*f||_2^2 at fixed ||f*f||_inf.
experiments.change: Keep p0751's file but replace the main loop with a band-target phase. On the record (N=84992, rescaled so max knot=1), for bands B = [[0.50,0.90],[0.70,0.95],[0.80,0.98],[0.90,0.995]]: build weight w_k = 1 on knots with B0*Lmax <= L_k <= B1*Lmax and a cosine taper of 5% of the band at each edge; define objective F(h) = -sum_k w_k L_k^2 / num0 + 30.0*max(0, Lmax(h)/Lmax0 - 1.0)^2 (Lmax0 = start max, num0 = start numerator). Its gradient w.r.t. L is gL = -2 w_k L_k / num0 plus the hinge term on the argmax knot, backpropped with the existing _backprop and folded into log-height L-BFGS (existing _lbfgs_log plumbing, 250 iters, band recomputed from the current h every cycle). Accept the result only if exact R_of improves over the incumbent (use p0751's R_of); after every accepted step run 60 iters of exact-R log-L-BFGS to settle. Cycle bands until 0.88*budget, then a final exact-R polish. Print per band: numerator, Lmax, number of knots above 0.9*Lmax, exact R, elapsed. Hard-deadline every stage.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941270. Diagnostic: whether any band raises the numerator at fixed Lmax; if all bands return unchanged, the shoulder is convolved-locked and the record's deficit really is structural.

experiments.hypothesis: F659 split each cell into two equal halves and polished with plain L-BFGS and saw nothing — but at a perfectly equal split the antisymmetric sub-cell direction is an exact symmetry point, so its first derivative vanishes and no gradient method can ever leave it. Randomising a 4-way mass-preserving split removes that saddle and exposes sub-cell shape at the ramps and toes, which is the only remaining degree of freedom the 1x grid cannot represent.
experiments.change: Base p0707 (N=339968 = 4x staircase of the record). Stage A (raw scan, no polish): for alpha in {1.0, 4.0, 20.0} and 40 seeds, split every group of 4 cells by w ~ Dirichlet(alpha,alpha,alpha,alpha) with weights multiplied by the group's mass (mass-preserving); evaluate exact R of each raw split with fftconvolve; print the best raw R and how many splits beat the start (expect raw R to drop ~1e-4, that is fine). Stage B: take the top 5 raw splits, polish each at native N=339968 with exact-R log-height L-BFGS restricted to the free mask = cells whose group's f*f knots are within 5% of max OR within the first/last 4096 cells (mask everything else as bounds=(0,0)/excluded indices), 150 iters each, cap 4 s per polish; then a beta-homotopy settle (1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 60 iters each) on the same mask. Stage C: full-array exact-R L-BFGS on the best candidate, 150 iters. Accept only if final R > start R; keep and return the best. All stages guarded at 0.88*budget; print R, max/mean and the fraction of knots within 0.1% of max after each stage.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941248-0.941260 on this track. Diagnostic: if raw split R never recovers above start-1e-6 after Stage B, the 4x sub-cell redundancy is genuinely inert (F659 confirmed structurally, not just numerically); if one split recovers and beats start, sub-cell phase is live at the ramps.

experiments.hypothesis: R is maximised when f*f is as close to an indicator as possible; the deficit is exactly the mass in g's two ramps. Instead of fitting f parametrically and hoping, prescribe the target g (plateau + power-law ramps of tunable exponent q and width w) and invert the convolution spectrally: f = IFFT(sqrt(max(Re FFT(g),0))). This yields a spiky-toed f of exactly the kind the record has (max/mean ~150) without any local search, and the family is 7-dimensional so Nelder-Mead is enough to find its best member.
experiments.change: From Code Zero. Build g_target on M=2048 uniform knots over [0,2]: g = 1 between xL and xR; on [0,xL] g = min(1,((xL-x)/wL)^qL) and mirrored on the right; params (xL, xR, log wL, log wR, log qL, log qR, log base) with base a small floor added. G = np.fft.rfft(g); neg = G.real < 0; G.real = np.maximum(G.real, 0); G.imag = 0; f = np.fft.irfft(np.sqrt(G.real.astype(complex)), n=M2) on M2=2048 cells over [0,1] (rescale index-wise so total length matches), then h = np.abs(f) + 0.02*max|f|; rasterise by cell-average at N=1024, score by exact R (fftconvolve, existing R_of style). Random-search 800 parameter draws (vectorised), take the top 5 through Nelder-Mead on exact R (maxiter 400). Escalate the winner by cumulative-mass prolongation to N=8192, then log-height exact-R L-BFGS (300 iters), beta homotopy betas 1e2/1e3/1e4/1e5 (150 iters each), then 4 peak-window block polishes (fracs 0.05/0.1/0.2/0.35), then to N=32768 with the same ladder. Print R, zero fraction, max/mean, f*f argmax fraction, and knots within 0.1/1/5% of max after each stage. Deadline guard: stop staging at 0.88*budget and return the best array found (never the raw start).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.88-0.92, hard floor 0.80 (must beat track T58's 0.794099). Diagnostic: max/mean of the final f (expect 10-150 if the spectral square root produces the right spike-toed shape) and the within-0.1% knot fraction (expect markedly above p0749's 0.35%); if max/mean stays near 4 the family collapses to a smooth blob and should be redirected.

plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record has survived ~40 generations of every gradient-based move: beta/softmax homotopy, Gauss-Newton plateau passes, prolongation, step-splitting (F659), randomised sub-cell splits (F663), band/shoulder targets (F662), multiplicative envelopes. So the deficit is not a magnitude problem but a barrier problem: every accepted move has been a nonneg, greedy, derivative-based step. Two genuinely untried escape mechanisms remain for the record: (a) leaving the nonneg cone (signed heights) so the argmax term stops pinning the landscape, and (b) derivative-free optimization restricted to the far toes, where f*f's ramps are set. T61's spectral sqrt is refuted (F664: max/mean 1.13, flat blob); the fix is least-squares inversion of the same target, which historically reaches 0.79-0.80.

experiments.hypothesis: Every escape attempt on the record has been a nonnegative, gradient-based step, and the exact-max gradient is pinned by the single argmax knot, so no move in the nonneg cone can pass the plateau barrier. Allowing heights to go temporarily negative keeps L=convolve(h,h) exactly valid, loosens the max term (no knot dominates), and lets L-BFGS travel through the barrier; rectifying afterwards can land in a basin unreachable from the record by any nonneg path.
experiments.change: Keep p0751's helpers (R_of, _knots, _num_and_dq, _backprop, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window). Replace the main loop with a signed-excursion loop. With h=rescale(start), R0: repeat until 0.85*budget. (a) Choose a contiguous band of width w in {256,1024,4096} cells at a random position, 60% of the time overlapping the f*f peak window, else anywhere nonzero. (b) Fix a sign vector sigma = +1 everywhere except that band where sigma = -1, restrict to the active set {h>1e-13*h.max()}, write h_i = sigma_i*exp(u_i), and run 80-iter L-BFGS-B on u in [-30,30] with the soft-max objective _fun_grad_beta(beta=1e3) evaluated on the signed array (guard sum(h)>1e-12; if the optimizer drives the sum negative, abort that draw). (c) h' = clip(h,-) then rescale; compute exact R; accept only if R>R0+1e-15. (d) After an accept, settle with _lbfgs_log(beta=0, 100 iters) plus one _peak_window block polish (frac 0.05). (e) Every third draw instead add negative bumps: h + sum of 3-8 triangular bumps of amplitude -alpha*local h, alpha in {0.02,0.05,0.1}, at random positions, then run (b)-(d). Print each accepted R with band width/position and the sign fraction. Track the best rectified array and return only it.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941248-0.941270 (>+5e-6 over the record). Diagnostic: if after >=200 signed draws the best rectified R never exceeds R0 by 1e-6, the record is a local optimum even in the signed relaxation, which is strong evidence that the remaining 5.9% needs a different construction family rather than any local move on this one.

experiments.hypothesis: T60 established that sub-cell degrees of freedom at the ramps are inert (raw splits drop to 0.92 and polish cannot recover; F663 agrees). The one region never optimized freely is the extreme toes, where f*f's ramps begin and where T38 only tested 2-3-parameter power laws with gradient polish. Reviving the toes is possible only additively (the record has 6.9% exact zeros, so multiplicative profiles do nothing there), and a 32-coefficient smooth additive toe profile optimized derivative-free is immune to the argmax gradient that has blocked every local move.
experiments.change: Base p0761 (N=339968). Stage A: mass-preserving coarsen by cumulative mass to N=42496; assert R matches the record to 1e-9 and print it. Stage B: on the 42496 array, let the outer K=1024 cells on each side be h_i = h_base_i + exp(v_i)*m, where m = mean of the nonzero interior heights and v_i is a cubic-spline interpolation of 16 free coefficients per side (32 params), interior cells fixed. Maximize exact R with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='Nelder-Mead', options maxfev=4000, xatol=1e-6, fatol=1e-12), initial simplex step 0.05 per coefficient, hard cap 20 s via a callback TimeoutError; start from v=log(clip(h_base_i,1e-6*m)) so the initial point reproduces the base exactly. Stage C: prolongate the best 42496 profile back to 339968 by cumulative mass, then run _lbfgs_log(beta=0, 150 iters), beta in {1e4,1e5} at 100 iters each, and _lbfgs_block peak windows at fracs 0.05 and 0.10. Accept only if the final R > start R; print coarse R after A, after B, and each toe coefficient's mass added (sum of exp(v)*m over each toe) so a zero result is unambiguous. Guard everything at 0.88*budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941245-0.941255 on this track (any gain above 1e-6 counts). Diagnostic: the printed toe mass added — if Nelder-Mead drives the toe additions to ~0 and coarse R is flat, the toe values are already optimal and T60 should be closed; if toe mass grows but R does not, the ramp is geometrically locked by the plateau.

experiments.hypothesis: T61's premise (prescribe the target g = plateau + power ramps, then invert) is sound, but the spectral square root is mathematically wrong: IFFT(sqrt(max(Re FFT(g),0))) is not an autocorrelation inverse, which is why F664 got a flat blob (max/mean 1.13, 0% zeros). Inverting the same 7-parameter target family by direct least squares on f>=0 restores the family, and that route is known to reach 0.79-0.80 from trivial starts.
experiments.change: Rewrite p0760's inversion only; keep build_g and the parameters. New fit(g): at N=1024, minimize ||f*f - g/||g||_inf||_2^2 over log-heights f=exp(u) (cell averages, fftconvolve, analytic gradient via _backprop-style correlation) with L-BFGS-B, 200 iters, u in [-25,25], initial u = log(0.5 + 2*IFFT-style bump) or log(ones); then rescale and return exact R. Stage 1: Nelder-Mead over the 7 params with objective = exact R of the least-squares fit (maxfev 400, xatol 1e-4), starting from the p0760 params, at N=1024; keep the top 3 param sets (restart NM twice from perturbed copies). Stage 2: prolongate the best fit by cumulative mass to N=8192, run _lbfgs_log(beta=0, 300 iters), beta ladder {1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5} 150 iters each, and peak-window block polishes at fracs 0.05/0.1/0.2/0.35; repeat Stage 2 at N=32768 if time remains. Print R, zero fraction, max/mean and the within-0.1/1/5% knot fractions after every stage. Hard deadline at 0.88*budget; always return the best nonnegative array found.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.79-0.82 on this track (track best is 0.693904, so a large gain). Diagnostic: max/mean should rise well above 1.13 (expect 10-60) and the within-1% knot fraction above 2%; if the least-squares fit still returns max/mean ~1, the target family itself is unreachable by nonnegative f and the track should switch to a free-form f parameterization.

plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record has survived every local, geometric, block-rearrangement, toe and target-fitting attack, so the main bet is to change the representation: a memory-safe coarse smooth basis that solves directly for mass moves flattening the near-max f*f plateau, rather than following the exact single-knot gradient. I also bet that p0751's beta ladder is mistuned (starts at 1, stops at 1000), so a much wider F537-style homotopy may still move global mass, and that p0622's finer 169984-step construction can exploit a capped near-max surrogate at full resolution where p0691 only used a coarsened grid.

experiments.hypothesis: R is limited by the near-max shoulders of f*f; the exact-max gradient only moves the single argmax knot, but a low-dimensional smooth additive basis can transfer mass globally to raise those shoulders. A coarse-basis linearized least-squares correction avoids the 12 GiB Gauss-Newton failure while still targeting flatness.
experiments.change: Keep p0751 helpers. Coarsen p0751 to M=42496 by pairwise means. Build K=256 overlapping cubic B-spline basis functions on the whole support plus 16 edge hats. For eps in {0.002,0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05}: let A be knots with L >= (1-eps)*Lmax, target c=mean(L_A), residual r=c-L_A. Form J_k = 2*conv(h,B_k)[A]. Solve the K-dimensional damped normal equations (J^T J + lambda*diag(J^T J)) d = J^T r for lambda in {1e-6,1e-4,1e-2,1e-1}, clip h+B d >=0, rescale, and line-search alpha in {1,1/2,1/4,...} on exact R. Accept only exact-R improvements, then alternate with p0751's peak-window L-BFGS and hard-max polish. Use the whole budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim for 0.941250-0.941260. Diagnostic: print predicted residual drop and the actual exact-R gain for each eps/lambda. If predicted drop is large but exact R never rises, the plateau is not reachable by smooth whole-support mass moves; if one eps gives a gain, continue that eps to convergence.

experiments.hypothesis: p0751's smooth-max homotopy starts at beta=1 and stops at beta=1000, so it never explores the very low-beta global smoothing that can move mass across the whole support, nor the high-beta sharpening that F537 found useful. Extending the ladder and interleaving peak-window block polish should let the same construction move before sharpening.
experiments.change: Replace p0751's beta list with [1e-3,3e-3,1e-2,3e-2,0.1,0.3,1,3,10,30,100,300,1e3,3e3,1e4,3e4,1e5,1e6,1e7]. For each beta run log-height L-BFGS for up to 150 iterations or 2 s, then run peak-window block L-BFGS on fracs {0.02,0.05,0.10,0.20} with exact R, keeping only improvements. Repeat the full ladder for several cycles until budget end, then do a final hard-max exact-R L-BFGS polish. Print R after every beta and block stage.

plan.analysis: 0.941243 is a genuine KKT point of the equal-width discrete problem: ~230 findings show that every gradient, surrogate (soft-max, capped-sum, flatness-deficit, shoulder-band, spline-basis), sub-cell split, resampling and annealing move returns it unchanged, and extra degrees of freedom at 2x/4x resolution are inert. So no local method at the fixed grid can gain; only (i) genuinely new degrees of freedom, (ii) an algorithmically different search on a losslessly coarsened grid where iterations are 4-8x cheaper and lifting back is exact, or (iii) a decisive measurement of how strict the local maximum is. Note the record's own history: its gains came from structural perturbations plus polishing, never from surrogate objectives. Non-uniform cell widths were only tried with <=16 warp parameters and Nelder-Mead alone, never with many warp degrees of freedom alternated with full height re-optimization.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is stationary only within the equal-width-cell class. All its cells have identical width and it is an exact 2x staircase, which is what an equal-width constraint produces at convergence. Giving the cell boundaries genuine freedom (a many-parameter monotone moving mesh) creates new variables whose stationarity condition differs, so R can increase; earlier warp attempts used <=16 parameters optimised by Nelder-Mead without re-optimising heights, which cannot exploit this.
experiments.change: Keep p0751's helpers (R_of, _knots, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _peak_window, _rescale). Add a moving-mesh stage. (1) Coarsen p0751 exactly by 8 (mass-average of 8 consecutive cells) to M=10624 cells, h0, boundaries X_i=i uniform; print R of the rasterised-back array to confirm it reproduces 0.941243011. (2) Parametrise log-widths w_i = 0 + sum_{k=1..48} c_k*cos(pi*k*(i+0.5)/M) added to a uniform log-width base, widths = M*softmax(w), boundaries X = cumsum(widths); bounds |c_k| <= 1.0. (3) rasterise(h, X) onto a uniform grid of N_out cells by exact cell-overlap (np.add.at of h_i*overlap), N_out=21248 during warp search and 84992 for scoring/polish; R is evaluated on the rasterised array (that is what gets scored). (4) Alternate until budget: (a) L-BFGS-B on log h at fixed X using p0751's analytic gradient, chained through the rasterisation (dh_fine/dh_i = overlap weights) so the height gradient is exact; (b) L-BFGS-B on the 48 warp coefficients c with a forward-difference gradient (49 rasterise+R evaluations per gradient, step 2e-3), accepting only exact-R improvements. (5) Every 2 cycles re-rasterise the best mesh at the next finer N_out (21248 -> 42496 -> 84992) and polish heights there; keep the best equal-width array of length <=84992 ever seen and return it. Never return an array with N > 1e6; spend >=95% of the budget, printing R after every warp and height stage.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941270. Diagnostic: if the warp gradient norms are nonzero but R never rises past 0.941243011 after height re-polish, the equal-width partition is not the binding constraint and the moving-mesh direction is closed; if R rises at M=10624 and survives rasterisation to 84992, the mesh was binding and the same stage should be re-run at M=21248.

experiments.hypothesis: T62's smooth-max ladder is dead on this construction (F675), but the track's real question - can mass be moved globally at all - was never answered by a direct measurement. If the record is a strict local maximum, every mass-transfer move must have negative second-order response, and measuring the size of that negative response tells us how far a perturbation must go before it can help; if instead some two-window transfer is positive, it is an immediate escape that the local gradient cannot see.
experiments.change: Use p0773 as base and keep its helpers. Replace the beta-homotopy main loop with a global two-window mass-transfer scan. Define a move by a pair of windows [a1,b1), [a2,b2) on the 84992 grid, with widths in {256,1024,4096,16384} and start positions on a stride of 1024 covering the whole support (cap the pair list at ~400 pairs, including pairs on opposite sides of the f*f argmax and pairs with one window on the near-max plateau and one in a tail). Move: h[a1:b1] *= (1+alpha), h[a2:b2] *= (1 - alpha*m1/m2) with m1,m2 the window masses so total mass is preserved; exact 1-D maximisation of R over alpha in [-0.45,0.45] by 24 golden-section steps (R_of only, no gradients). Record per-move delta_R, apply the single best improving move if any, then polish (peak-window L-BFGS at fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10 plus one full exact-R log-height L-BFGS), and repeat the scan from the improved point until budget end. Also try, per window alone, the flattening move h_win <- (1-alpha)*h_win + alpha*mean(h) with an exact alpha search. Print, for the base point, the best positive delta_R over all moves and the distribution of non-positive ones (min, median, max) and the number of moves within 1e-7 of zero. Spend >=95% of the budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941245-0.941250 if any global transfer is positive. The informative result either way is the strictness profile: if the maximum delta_R over all ~400 two-window transfers is <= +1e-8 and the median is around -1e-4, the record is a strict local maximum in this class and greedy/global-transfer escapes should be abandoned; a few near-zero moves identify the directions (windows) along which a larger, non-infinitesimal perturbation should be attempted next generation.

experiments.hypothesis: At N=169984 each R evaluation is a large FFT and every program burns its budget on a handful of long L-BFGS runs; the record is an exact 4x staircase, so the 42496 grid carries the identical function (R invariant, lifting back is exact). Running an algorithmically different, cheap-per-iteration search there - block coordinate descent with exact 1-D line searches, which handles the max kink exactly instead of differentiating through it - gets many more accepted/rejected moves, and any gain lifts losslessly to 169984.
experiments.change: Base p0772 (N=169984). First verify it is an exact staircase and coarsen by 4 with mass-average to M=42496; print R there (must be 0.941243011) and work on that grid. Loop until budget: (1) compute the full exact-R log-height gradient once (one backward pass), then sweep blocks of B=1024 cells in a random permutation: for each block take d = gradient restricted to the block (log-coordinates) and do an exact 1-D maximisation of R along h_block*exp(alpha*d), alpha in [0, 0.5], by 18 golden-section steps; recompute R only by R_of; accept if R improves (accept zero-change alpha=0 otherwise). (2) Per block also try two non-gradient moves with exact alpha in [0,1]: h_block <- (1-alpha)*h_block + alpha*mean(h_block), and h_block <- (1-alpha)*h_block + alpha*mean(h). Accept only improvements. (3) After each full sweep run peak-window L-BFGS (frac 0.05) and, every 3rd sweep, a full exact-R log-height L-BFGS with p0772's own _lbfgs_log. Print R and the largest single-block gain after every sweep. If the best 42496 R exceeds the start by more than 1e-9, lift exactly (each cell repeated 4x to 169984), run a short softmax beta ladder [1,10,100,1000] then hard exact-R polish, and return the better of that and the start; otherwise return the start. Keep total per-block R evaluations modest so that at least 8 full sweeps plus the final polish fit in the budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941246-0.941255. info.open_why: Need p0751's exact code/state, the two side-track programs' full plans and results, and the findings F490/F537/F604 that the side tracks revive, to design distinct follow-ups that don't repeat failed surrogates.

plan.analysis: The record is a strict local maximum under essentially every tried parametrization: heights (exact gradient, log-heights, block polish), mass transfer (cell, window, golden-section), warps (sine, PL, cosine, moving mesh), grid changes (2x/4x/8x staircase, non-dyadic resample), surrogates (logsumexp beta 1e-3..1e7, p-norm, windowed max, shoulder bands, spectral reshaping), and global stochastic escapes (SA, signed excursions). p0778's own scan gave max delta +1.1e-16 with 184/184 moves at zero: the record is a discrete and continuous local optimum. So I bet on the two things never isolated: (a) large-scale surgery (a wide new zero gap) whose re-optimization must pass through a smooth flat-target L2 objective rather than R's one-knot gradient, and (b) a from-scratch alternating-projection/gamma-compressed flat-target construction, which is a different objective, not a different descent. Slot 3 revives the smooth-min homotopy on a coarsened grid where the max-knot structure differs.

experiments.hypothesis: Every escape so far perturbs the record on a small scale and R's exact gradient (which sees only one argmax knot) drags it straight back. A wide, non-infinitesimal structural change (a new contiguous zero gap) cannot be undone by local descent, so it genuinely relocates the basin; the smooth flat-target L2 residual sum_j w_j (g_j - c)^2 with w_j = g_j^2 has a gradient spread over the whole near-max band and can rebuild a good plateau from a damaged start, where the exact-R gradient cannot.
experiments.change: Keep R_of/_knots/_backprop/_lbfgs_log/_peak_window/_rescale. Step 0: verify p0778 is an exact 2x staircase by coarsening with mass-average (h2[i]=(h[2i]+h[2i+1])/2) to M=42496 and printing R (must be 0.941243011); work on the M grid. Step 1: implement smooth objective F(h) = log(sum_j w_j (g_j - c)^2 / sum_j w_j) with g = knots(h), c = g.max(), w_j = g_j^2 + eps; gradient via existing _backprop with gLf = 2 w_j (g_j - c)/den plus the w_j-derivative term dropped (report that it is dropped), in log-height coordinates, L-BFGS 200 iters. Step 2: for each surgery variant S in {zero [0.10M,0.40M), zero [0.30M,0.60M), zero [0.45M,0.75M), multiply [0.15M,0.35M) by 0.3, multiply [0.40M,0.65M) by 0.3}: apply S, run 5 s of F-descent, then exact-R polish (peak-window L-BFGS at fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10 + one full exact-R log L-BFGS), record raw-after-surgery R, R-after-F, R-after-polish; keep the global best h and if it beats the base, prolongate back to N=84992 by exact doubling and re-polish. Step 3: repeat the whole variant list with random block positions/scale factors (fixed RNG seed) until >=95% of the budget is used. Print one line per variant with the three R values.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941245-0.941250. The informative result either way: if every variant's R-after-F rises steadily while R-after-polish returns to <=0.941243011, a wide gap is recoverable but not beneficial, and the flat-target objective is confirmed to share the record's basin; if R-after-polish lands above the base for any variant, the basin escape worked and gives a new direction to exploit. Also informative: whether F-descent's optimum differs from the exact-R optimum (report the L1 distance between the two height vectors).

experiments.hypothesis: R=1 needs f*f flat; the exact-R objective rewards only the top knots and is a poor guide when starting far away. A genuinely different search - alternating projections that impose a gamma-compressed flat target on g in real space and then re-fit f by least squares - optimizes the thing that actually matters (the whole residual g - c), and it is a mechanism no prior from-zero run used.
experiments.change: Build from scratch (start=None). Use fftconvolve everywhere. Init at N=2048 with two deterministic starts: (A) capped singular f_i = min(cap, ((i+0.5)/N)^-0.5) with cap in {1.0, 3.0, 10.0}; (B) plateau [1.0 for i<N] plus a spike of height sqrt(N) in cell 0. Algorithm, one outer round: (1) g = knots(h), c = max(g); (2) target g_t = c * (g/c)**gamma with gamma in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} (a flat-target projection, preserves g's zeros and support); (3) re-fit f by L-BFGS on log-heights minimizing sum_j (g_j - g_t_j)^2 / sum_j g_t_j^2 (exact gradient by backprop), 60 iters, clamp to [0, None], _rescale; (4) exact-R polish (peak-window L-BFGS fracs 0.05/0.10 + one full exact-R log L-BFGS, 1.5 s); (5) keep the best R seen. Run gamma values round-robin for ~12 s at each N, then double N by exact staircase prolongation (2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768) and continue, until >=95% of the budget is used. Print per (N, gamma, init) the R before and after the exact-R polish.
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.90 at N=16384-32768, ideally above the 0.88 best-from-zero baseline; a hit above 0.941243 would be a new record. Diagnostic: does the flat-target projection raise R monotonically with N, and does gamma<1 (stronger compression) beat plain exact-R descent from the same init? If all gammas end below the plain-R descent at equal N, the flat-target projection is not a useful surrogate and should be dropped as a line.

experiments.hypothesis: F583's smooth-min p-norm on the L-infinity term (as opposed to logsumexp) changes which knots the gradient spreads over and worked 3/3 on L9. On the record the exact max sits on a staircase plateau where whole pairs of knots are tied, so the effective max structure at M=42496 (after exact halving) differs from the N=84992 grid; running the same homotopy on both grids gives two chances at a different near-max configuration, and F583's doubling step supplies the transfer between them.
experiments.change: Keep p0778's helpers. Implement _fun_grad_pnorm(h, p): num, dq, Lf as in _num_and_dq; S = sum(Lf**p); val = -log(num) + 2*log(sum(h)) + log(S)/p; gLf = -dq/num + (Lf**(p-1))/S; grad = _backprop(gLf, h) + 2/sum(h). Run ladder p in {4, 8, 12, 24, 48}: each stage L-BFGS in log-height coords 150 iters, then peak-window block polish at fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10, then print exact R and the argmax knot index. Do the full ladder twice, once at N=84992 and once at M=42496 (exact mass-average halving), and after the M run prolongate back to N=84992 by exact doubling. Finally polish the better of the two with the exact-R full log L-BFGS. Loop the whole procedure (M and N ladders alternating) until >=95% of the budget is used; print per-stage R, argmax index and whether it beats the base.

plan.analysis: 75+ generations of local escapes on the 0.941243 record have all returned it unchanged. The measured deficit is in the shoulders: only 18.24% of f*f knots are within 0.1% of max and 42.77% within 5%, while the exact-R gradient sees exactly one argmax knot. So I bet on two ways to spread gradient over *all* near-max knots: (1) a max-constrained (penalty/augmented-Lagrangian) formulation on the record, where the L_inf term becomes a constraint set instead of one non-smooth knot, and (2) a smooth low-dimensional log-spline parametrisation that can move large-scale shoulder slope, which no full-grid descent can. T64's from-zero flat-target basin is genuinely different (42% of knots within 0.1% of max) but burned only 17.7 s of its 60 s budget, so slot 3 gives it the whole budget and harder projection.

experiments.hypothesis: Every surrogate so far (logsumexp, p-norm, softmax, softmin, Gauss-Newton) keeps R's single-argmax geometry in some form and returns exactly 0.941243011. Writing R as max num/s^2 s.t. L_j <= 1 for all j and solving it with an L2 penalty on the violations gives gradient to *every* knot that exceeds the level, linearly (not exponentially) in the violation, which is precisely the shoulder-raising signal needed; rho -> infinity recovers exact R, and the exact-R polish at each stage keeps real gains.

Add _fun_grad_pen(h, rho): num,dq,Lf = _num_and_dq(h); F = -log(num) + 2*log(h.sum()) + rho*sum(max(0, Lf-1)**2); gLf = -dq/num + 2*rho*max(0, Lf-1.0); grad = _backprop(gLf,h) + 2/h.sum(); return F,grad. Stage: rescale h so max(Lf)=1 exactly (h/=sqrt(maxLf)), run _lbfgs_log(h, 250 iters, fg=lambda hh: _fun_grad_pen(hh,rho)), print rho, num/s^2, maxLf, count(Lf>1), count(Lf>0.99*max), then exact-R polish (peak-window block L-BFGS at fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10, 1.5 s each, then full exact-R log L-BFGS 3 s) and keep best-by-exact-R. Ladder rho in [1e0,1e1,1e2,1e3,1e4,1e6,1e8]; alternate the whole ladder between N=84992 and the exact mass-average halving M=42496 (doubling M results back with _double), restarting from the current best each cycle and looping until 95% of the budget is used. Never return anything with exact R below the base 0.941243011.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941262. The result shows whether exact R rises monotonically with rho while the count of knots within 1% of max grows (shoulders genuinely raised) - if every stage's exact R stays exactly 0.941243011 and the >1-knot count collapses to 1 as rho grows, the constrained geometry is exhausted on this construction and the shoulders are pinned by the convolution structure, not by the surrogate.

experiments.hypothesis: T65's p-norm ladder is exhausted: it returned exactly 0.941243010 with an argmax invariant at knot 97392 (N) / 48696 (M), i.e. the max structure is stable under both grids. What has never been varied is the *function class*: the record's R deficit is a large-scale shoulder/ramp feature, but every attempt has been full-grid descent that cannot move shoulder slope without moving 84992 coupled heights. Restricting to a smooth low-dimensional log-spline and climbing K upward tests, and can improve, the large-scale shape directly; the R(K) curve is also the cleanest available measurement of how much of the 0.941 is carried by fine-scale structure.
experiments.change: Keep p0786's helpers. Add a geometric log-spline parametrisation: for K in {129,257,513,1025,2049,4097,8193,16385}, with u = (arange(N)+0.5)/N * (K-1), i0=floor(u), w=u-i0, h = exp((1-w)*c[i0] + w*c[i0+1]) evaluated in O(N) (no dense design matrix). Gradient: from exact-R log objective g_h via the existing _fun_grad(h) (val,grad), then g_c[i0] += g_h*h*(1-w), g_c[i0+1] += g_h*h*w using np.add.at. Init c at each K by least squares on log(record heights + 1e-9) (np.linalg.lstsq on the same two-point interpolation); then L-BFGS over c (bounds [-25,25], 250 iters, exact-R objective). Ladder K upward starting from K=129, two rounds per K, printing R, max/mean and count of knots within 1%/5% of max at each K. Keep the best rasterised h by exact R; after each full ladder apply the standard exact-R polish (peak-window block L-BFGS fracs 0.02/0.05/0.1 plus one full log L-BFGS 3 s), then loop the ladder from the current best with a random sigma=0.02 perturbation of c until 95% of the budget is used. Return the best exact-R construction found.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250+; minimum useful outcome is the curve R(K). If R at K=2049-8193 is still >= 0.9400 the record's large-scale shape has real slack and refining K back to 16385-84992 with polish should beat 0.941243011; if R collapses below 0.93 by K=1025 and no K-level optimisation recovers it, the record's R is carried by fine-scale structure and the smooth-basis line should be dropped.

experiments.hypothesis: p0783 is the strongest genuinely different basin (0.878326 with 42.13% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max - much flatter than the record's 18.24%) but it stopped at N=32768 using only 17.7 s of 60 s, ran one gamma per branch, used an absolute-error target fit dominated by the peak, and never escalated resolution. plan.analysis: The record 0.941243011 is saturated: ~30 generations of surrogates (logsumexp, p-norm, softmin, penalty-constrained, GN, log-spline, upsampling ladders) all return it unchanged, and the many upsampling runs failed for a structural reason — the record at N=169984 is the exact staircase of the N=42496 function, i.e. literally the same step function, so N-ladders add nothing. The one lever never tried on it is to remove the sparse max-gradient from the step direction entirely and instead *project* onto the max=1 manifold every evaluation, ascending log(||g||_2^2/s^2) alone. Meanwhile T64's 0.878 basin is a genuine flat core (43% of knots within 0.1% of max) whose whole deficit is ramp mass (R = 1 - (r/3)/(w+r) for a trapezoid), so shortening the ramps with end spikes is the correct fix there. Slot 3 pushes the under-explored 0.941123 alternative p0702 with the record's proven polish machinery.

experiments.hypothesis: R = num/(s^2 * max) and every failure has come from the max term: its gradient lives on one knot, so the true gradient direction is dominated by a single cell and L-BFGS/logsumexp/p-norm all get stuck in the same place. If instead we fix the gauge max(g)=1 by projection (h -> h/sqrt(max)) at every objective evaluation and ascend only log(num/s^2), the direction is the exact gradient of R restricted to the max=1 manifold, with no degenerate sparse term; it can therefore move the shoulders (where the whole deficit is: only 18.24% of knots within 0.1% of max) that the sparse term hides.
experiments.change: Keep p0778's helpers (_knots/_conv, R_of, _num_and_dq, _backprop, _rescale, _lbfgs_log, _peak_window) unchanged. Add _rho(h) = h / sqrt(max(knots(h))) (guard max<=0). Add objective _fun_grad_proj(h): hp = _rho(h); num, dq, Lf = _num_and_dq(hp); s = hp.sum(); val = -log(num) + 2*log(s)  (NO log(max) term); gLf = -dq/num; g_hp = _backprop(gLf, hp) + 2.0/s; then chain through rho: with M = Lf.max() and dM/dh computed from the max knot index m as dM/dh[a] = 2*hp[m-1-a] for valid a (as in _lbfgs_log's _peak-window code), grad_h = g_hp/sqrt(M) - (g_hp . hp) * (dM/dh) / (2 * M**1.5). Run L-BFGS-B in log-height coordinates with only the active (nonzero) cells free, bounds (-30,30), ftol 1e-20. Schedule: (a) 6-8 projected-L-BFGS runs of 150 iters each, each seeded from the current best after a different deterministic kick (multiply the block around the f*f argmax by 1+-0.02; renormalise; also one run from the untweaked best); (b) after each run, one exact-R peak-window block L-BFGS (fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10) to confirm in the true objective; keep a result only if R_of improves on the current best by >1e-14. Repeat the (projected ascent + exact polish) cycle until 95% of budget; print R and the count of knots within 1% of max after every cycle.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941250-0.941262. Diagnostic: if R rises above 0.941243011 at all in any cycle, the sparse max-gradient was the blocker and the projected direction is the right main line; if every cycle returns exactly the record with a vanishing projected gradient, R is a true projected local optimum and the main line must move to a different basin. Also report whether the within-1%-of-max fraction climbs above 34.55%.

experiments.hypothesis: T64's basin already has an almost perfectly flat core (43.38% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max) yet only R=0.878, and for a trapezoidal g the entire deficit is the ramp mass, R = 1 - (r/3)/(w+r). p0789's ramps are therefore the target, and its own log shows the projection machinery is exhausted (relative-error refits at N=65536 collapse, gamma 0.30 leaves w1%=0.000). What it never had is a *short-ramp* mechanism: tall narrow capped spikes at the two ends of f (the record's f has max/mean 147 and 6.9% zeros precisely for this reason), which is what makes g rise steeply off zero.
experiments.change: Build on p0789 (keep _knots/_R/_prolong/_fit_target/_exact_polish, fftconvolve everywhere). Steps: (1) start from p0789's h at N=32768; (2) seed construction: form h_new by taking h and replacing the first and last L cells (L in {64,256,1024}) with a capped spike profile A*min(cap, ((i+0.5)/L)**-0.5) for the left and mirrored for the right, A chosen so the spike mass is q in {0.05,0.10,0.20} of the total mass, cap in {3,10,30}*mean(h); keep the interior; _rescale; (3) exact-R polish of each seed with the existing peak-window + full log L-BFGS (2-3 s), keep the best by exact R; (4) from the best seed, alternate: prescribed trapezoid target fit (build g_t on the knot grid as c on the central w fraction, linear ramp of width r to 0 at both ends, with w in {0.5,0.6,0.7} and r in {0.01,0.02,0.05}; refit log-heights by L-BFGS on absolute error ||L-g_t||^2/norm — NOT the relative weighting that broke at N=65536 — 60 iters) then exact-R polish, 1 iteration per (w,r) pair, keep best by exact R; (5) staircase-prolong the best to N=65536 and 131072 and repeat (4) there. Use >=95% of budget; print per (L,q,cap) and per (w,r,N) the R before/after and the within-1% fraction.
