info.open_why: T77's revive hinges on F637 target relocation, and I need to see p0883's actual implementation plus F490/F724 (the record's gradient-flatness facts) and the two backtrack candidates' approaches to pick a genuinely untried direction.

plan.analysis: The record is a saturated discrete local optimum at N=84992: ~290 documented failures on it, and the last generation added four more (F782 ceiling homotopy, F783 shoulder-weighted numerator, F777/F784 trapezoid target relocation). F783 is the informative one: the shoulder-weighted surrogate did move h hard (R fell to 0.8957) but could never be polished back, so either the direction is wrong or the objective lost the peak instead of pinning it. I bet on the latter being fixable by projection rather than by a log-max term. For the main slot I avoid objectives entirely and attack the one thing never varied on the record: the cell/knot alignment of the representation itself (F602's fractional-shift result, never tried at 0.9412). The bold slot bets that the from-scratch ceiling (~0.912) is a greedy-escalation artefact and uses a beam over refinement paths.

experiments.hypothesis: Every move on p0828 has varied heights inside a fixed N-cell grid whose knots land at fixed offsets; the objective is exact for that grid, so the record is only a critical point of that particular discretisation. Re-representing the same shape as a step function on a grid shifted by a fraction of a cell gives a genuinely different piecewise-constant function (and a different knot lattice for f*f) at the same N; F602 found fractional-shift re-alignment before refinement gained on a 0.9114 basin, and it has never been applied at 0.9412. Resampling can score slightly higher or lower on its own, and from there the existing exact-R polish has a different local geometry to descend.
experiments.change: Keep all of p0828's machinery (R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _polish, Q-sweep, dict return). Insert one new first stage. Define F(t) = cumulative mass of the base step function, F(t)=0 for t<=0, F(t)=M for t>=N, computed by np.interp(t, np.arange(N+1), np.concatenate(([0],np.cumsum(h)))). For each delta in [0.5, 0.25, 0.75, 0.1, 0.9]: build h_d with N cells covering [delta-1, delta+N-1], h_d[j] = F(delta+j+1) - F(delta+j), j=0..N-1; clip at 0; print R_of(h_d) BEFORE any optimisation (diagnostic). Then rescale (h_d/sqrt(max knots)) and run, per delta, exact-R log L-BFGS (~150 iters, <=2.5 s) followed by _polish (fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10) capped at ~2 s, keeping the global best only if exact R_of improves by >1e-13 (print R after resample / after log polish / after window polish for every delta). After the delta sweep (~25 s), if nothing beat the record, continue with the base's own Q-sweep + polish on the unchanged record for the remaining time so the run still uses the full budget; if a delta did win, run the Q-sweep and _polish on that winner instead. Return {'best': best, 'alternative': start} exactly as p0828 does, and never return anything with R below the base's.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941255 (record + 1.2e-5); realistically +1e-5 if the shape is representation-limited and 0.000000 if not. Diagnostic: the printed R_of(h_d) before optimisation for each delta tells us immediately whether the record's R depends on knot alignment at the 1e-5 level (some delta scores above 0.941243) or is alignment-independent (all below, all polishes return to 0.941243011). If all deltas polish back to 0.941243, the construction is a genuine critical point across discretisations and the remaining search must be structural, not representational.

experiments.hypothesis: T78's premise (the 0.0588 deficit lives on knots with g in ~(0.4,0.99), not on the argmax knot) is untested, because T78's implementation kept the log(Linf) term while down-weighting the very knots that carry the max, so the surrogate's minimum sat at a different peak height: R collapsed to 0.8957 and no polish recovered. The mechanical fix is to fix the gauge by projection instead of by a log term: pin max(g) to its current value after every micro-step (R is scale-invariant, so this is legitimate) and ascend the objective -log(num)+2log(s) alone, optionally with a mild down-weight of the top band. If the deficit really is shoulder-dominated, moving mass up into the band at fixed peak must raise num/max.
experiments.change: Build on p0888, keep its helpers, dict return and time handling. Add M0 = knots(base).max() and fg_pin(h) = value -log(num)+2log(s), grad _backprop(-dq/num, h)+2/s (NO log Lm term, reuse _num_and_dq). Add fg_band(h,c,beta) identical but with dq multiplied by w[:-1]/w[1:] using w = 1-sigmoid(beta*(Lf - c*M0)) exactly as p0888 already does, still no log Lm term. Outer loop until ~2 s before budget: (1) take h, run _lbfgs_log with the current fg for a SHORT run (maxiter 40, cap 1.0 s) so it cannot run away; (2) rescale the returned h by sqrt(M0/_knots(h).max()) to pin the peak; (3) compute exact R_of; accept h only if R beats the current best by >1e-14, else discard and shrink the step (multiply a global step-scale used to cap maxiter: 40 -> 30 -> 20); (4) every 5th micro-step run _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(best,0.05) with _fun_grad plus _polish, accepting only exact-R gains. Run stage A with fg_pin, then stage B with (c=0.98, beta=30), then stage C with (c=0.95, beta=100), then repeat the best-scoring stage for the rest of the budget. Print per micro-step: stage, num, max knots (must stay ~M0), exact R, accepted/rejected, and the fraction of knots within 1% and 5% of max.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250. Diagnostic: the max-knots column must stay at ~0.967353 in every accepted step (if it drifts, the projection is wrong); success looks like num/max rising together with the within-1% fraction rising from 34.55% while ||f*f||_inf stays fixed. If every micro-step is rejected in all three stages and the within-1% fraction never leaves 34.55%, then lifting the intermediate band at a pinned peak is not reachable in h-space and the whole shoulder-targeting family (T78, F783, F723, F782) is closed on this construction.

experiments.hypothesis: Every from-scratch line tops out at 0.88-0.91 (F715 0.882, F291 0.912) and every one of them escalates a single greedy path: coarse start, double N on the single best construction, re-polish. F721's own note is that all escapes have been greedy. A beam search over refinement paths - keep the top K constructions at each resolution, generate several dithered children per parent, and only prune on exact R at that resolution - searches the parts of the coarse landscape that greedy escalation discards, and the analytic capped two-sided inverse-sqrt family (F715/F474) gives a far better coarse seed than Code Zero.
experiments.change: From Code Zero, no dependence on p0001's shape beyond N=1. Define a rasteriser: for a parameter vector (log cap, log AL, log AR, pL, pR, log epsL, log epsR, log base) build h_i = min(cap, base + AL*cellavg_L + AR*cellavg_R) with cellavg_L = 2*(sqrt((i+1+epsL))-sqrt(i+epsL)) type exact cell integrals for exponent 1/2, and for general p use ((t+eps)^(1-p) difference)/(1-p) per cell; exponents p in [0.2,0.6] via the same formula clipped. Seed 16 parameter vectors by random log-uniform sampling around (cap=10..100, AL/AR=1..30, pL=pR=0.5, eps=1e-4..1e-2, base=0..1), rasterise at N=64, exact-R polish (log L-BFGS, 100 iters) each, keep the top K=6 by R_of. Then for level = 64,128,...,32768 (and up to 65536 if time allows): for each of the K parents, make 3 children = exact staircase double (h[2i]=h[2i+1]=h[i]) plus independent multiplicative dithers of 2% and 10% on random contiguous windows of width N/8; polish each child with exact-R log L-BFGS (maxiter 100, cap ~min(3 s, remaining/K/3)), keep the top K=6 by exact R_of; print level, best R, mean R of the K, and spread. When the level ladder ends or ~15 s remain, run _polish (log + peak-window block fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10/0.20) on the global best with the remaining budget and return the best array (heights only, length = its N).
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.900 at 65536 steps, beating T76's 0.796 and, if the beam helps, F715's 0.882; it will not reach 0.9412, and it is not supposed to. Diagnostic: the gap between the best of the K and the mean of the K at each level - if the beam's diversity keeps the mean close to the best, greedy escalation loses nothing and the 0.88-0.91 from-scratch ceiling is a property of the family, not of the search; if the beam's best systematically exceeds the greedy single-path result at the same level, diversity is worth carrying, and the same beam should be run on a record-derived coarse seed in a later slot.

Re-representing the same shape as a step function on a grid shifted by a fraction of a cell gives a genuinely different piecewise-constant function (and a different knot lattice for f*f) at the same N; F602 found fractional-shift re-alignment before refinement gained on a 0.9114 basin, and it has never been applied at 0.9412. Resampling can score slightly higher or lower on its own, and from there the existing exact-R polish has a different local geometry to descend.
experiments.change: Keep all of p0828's machinery (R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _polish, Q-sweep, dict return). Insert one new first stage. Define F(t) = cumulative mass of the base step function, F(t)=0 for t<=0, F(t)=M for t>=N, computed by np.interp(t, np.arange(N+1), np.concatenate(([0],np.cumsum(h)))). For each delta in [0.5, 0.25, 0.75, 0.1, 0.9]: build h_d with N cells covering [delta-1, delta+N-1], h_d[j] = F(delta+j+1) - F(delta+j), j=0..N-1; clip at 0; print R_of(h_d) BEFORE any optimisation (diagnostic). Then rescale (h_d/sqrt(max knots)) and run, per delta, exact-R log L-BFGS (~150 iters, <=2.5 s) followed by _polish (fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10) capped at ~2 s, keeping the global best only if exact R_of improves by >1e-13 (print R after resample / after log polish / after window polish for every delta). After the delta sweep (~25 s), if nothing beat the record, continue with the base's own Q-sweep + polish on the unchanged record for the remaining time so the run still uses the full budget; if a delta did win, run the Q-sweep and _polish on that winner instead. Return {'best': best, 'alternative': start} exactly as p0828 does, and never return anything with R below the base's.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941255 (record + 1.2e-5); realistically +1e-5 if the shape is representation-limited and 0.000000 if not. Diagnostic: the printed R_of(h_d) before optimisation for each delta tells us immediately whether the record's R depends on knot alignment at the 1e-5 level (some delta scores above 0.941243) or is alignment-independent (all below, all polishes return to 0.941243011). If all deltas polish back to 0.941243, the construction is a genuine critical point across discretisations and the remaining search must be structural, not representational.

experiments.hypothesis: T78's premise (the 0.0588 deficit lives on knots with g in ~(0.4,0.99), not on the argmax knot) is untested, because T78's implementation kept the log(Linf) term while down-weighting the very knots that carry the max, so the surrogate's minimum sat at a different peak height: R collapsed to 0.8957 and no polish recovered. The mechanical fix is to fix the gauge by projection instead of by a log term: pin max(g) to its current value after every micro-step (R is scale-invariant, so this is legitimate) and ascend the objective -log(num)+2log(s) alone, optionally with a mild down-weight of the top band. If the deficit really is shoulder-dominated, moving mass up into the band at fixed peak must raise num/max.
experiments.change: Build on p0888, keep its helpers, dict return and time handling. Add M0 = knots(base).max() and fg_pin(h) = value -log(num)+2log(s), grad _backprop(-dq/num, h)+2/s (NO log Lm term, reuse _num_and_dq). Add fg_band(h,c,beta) identical but with dq multiplied by w[:-1]/w[1:] using w = 1-sigmoid(beta*(Lf - c*M0)) exactly as p0888 already does, still no log Lm term. Outer loop until ~2 s before budget: (1) take h, run _lbfgs_log with the current fg for a SHORT run (maxiter 40, cap 1.0 s) so it cannot run away; (2) rescale the returned h by sqrt(M0/_knots(h).max()) to pin the peak; (3) compute exact R_of; accept h only if R beats the current best by >1e-14, else discard and shrink the step (multiply a global step-scale used to cap maxiter: 40 -> 30 -> 20); (4) every 5th micro-step run _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(best,0.05) with _fun_grad plus _polish, accepting only exact-R gains. Run stage A with fg_pin, then stage B with (c=0.98, beta=30), then stage C with (c=0.95, beta=100), then repeat the best-scoring stage for the rest of the budget. Print per micro-step: stage, num, max knots (must stay ~M0), exact R, accepted/rejected, and the fraction of knots within 1% and 5% of max.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250. Diagnostic: the max-knots column must stay at ~0.967353 in every accepted step (if it drifts, the projection is wrong); success looks like num/max rising together with the within-1% fraction rising from 34.55% while ||f*f||_inf stays fixed. If every micro-step is rejected in all three stages and the within-1% fraction never leaves 34.55%, then lifting the intermediate band at a pinned peak is not reachable in h-space and the whole shoulder-targeting family (T78, F783, F723, F782) is closed on this construction.

experiments.hypothesis: Every from-scratch line tops out at 0.88-0.91 (F715 0.882, F291 0.912) and every one of them escalates a single greedy path: coarse start, double N on the single best construction, re-polish. F721's own note is that all escapes have been greedy. A beam search over refinement paths - keep the top K constructions at each resolution, generate several dithered children per parent, and only prune on exact R at that resolution - searches the parts of the coarse landscape that greedy escalation discards, and the analytic capped two-sided inverse-sqrt family (F715/F474) gives a far better coarse seed than Code Zero.
experiments.change: From Code Zero, no dependence on p0001's shape beyond N=1. Define a rasteriser: for a parameter vector (log cap, log AL, log AR, pL, pR, log epsL, log epsR, log base) build h_i = min(cap, base + AL*cellavg_L + AR*cellavg_R) with cellavg_L = 2*(sqrt((i+1+epsL))-sqrt(i+epsL)) type exact cell integrals for exponent 1/2, and for general p use ((t+eps)^(1-p) difference)/(1-p) per cell; exponents p in [0.2,0.6] via the same formula clipped. Seed 16 parameter vectors by random log-uniform sampling around (cap=10..100, AL/AR=1..30, pL=pR=0.5, eps=1e-4..1e-2, base=0..1), rasterise at N=64, exact-R polish (log L-BFGS, 100 iters) each, keep the top K=6 by R_of. Then for level = 64,128,...,32768 (and up to 65536 if time allows): for each of the K parents, make 3 children = exact staircase double (h[2i]=h[2i+1]=h[i]) plus independent multiplicative dithers of 2% and 10% on random contiguous windows of width N/8; polish each child with exact-R log L-BFGS (maxiter 100, cap ~min(3 s, remaining/K/3)), keep the top K=6 by exact R_of; print level, best R, mean R of the K, and spread. When the level ladder ends or ~15 s remain, run _polish (log + peak-window block fracs 0.02/0.05/0.10/0.20) on the global best with the remaining budget and return the best array (heights only, length = its N).

plan.analysis: The record p0828 is converged in its own 84992-cell grid: every local, spectral, surrogate, target-fit and coarse-to-fine move on it has returned it unchanged, and full-width perturbations (SA, GN, p-norm) also failed. The only untried axes are (a) changing the underlying discretisation so new sub-cell directions exist, (b) optimising inside a structurally different subspace (symmetric), and (c) using the finer beta-continuation/block-polish recipe that actually gained on L9 (F793) but has never been applied to the record. T79's beam failed because its K children collapsed to one point (spread 1e-4) and it never passed N=8192; it needs structural children and surrogate-based pruning to keep diversity.

experiments.hypothesis: The 0.941243 record is only a critical point of the 84992-cell grid; refining to a 2x grid that splits each cell in two creates sub-cell degrees of freedom that the record's own parameterisation cannot see. experiments.change: Keep p0828's helpers, R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _polish and dict return. New first stage: build h2 of length 169984 by exact 2x staircase of base. For each of ~8 trials, multiply the two children of cell i by (1 + a*s_k*v_i), k=0,1, with s=[1,-1] (and a run with s=[1,1]), a in {0.01,0.03,0.10}, v_i = sin(2*pi*f*i/N + phase) with f in {1,2,4,8} and random phase, plus a per-cell random uniform jitter of 1-3% on a random contiguous window of width N/8. Rescale each, score exact R_of, keep the best 2. Then run the existing Q-sweep on each with a finer grid c in {0.985,0.99,0.995,0.999}, beta in {1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7}, cap 2.5 s, and _polish after each beat. Finally _polish the best with all remaining budget; return the best array (length its own N).
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250 (record + 7e-6); a gain above 1e-6 shows the record was grid-limited. If every trial returns exactly 0.941243, the record is a genuine local optimum in the continuous shape and the main line must move to a different construction.

experiments.hypothesis: T79's beam collapsed because its children were only 2%/10% multiplicative dithers of an already-converged parent, so by level 4096 the mean-best spread was 1e-4 and pruning on exact R discarded all diversity; and it ran out of budget at N=8192 before the ladder did anything. experiments.change: Build on p0895, keep its rasteriser, R_of, _R_grad and _polish. At the seeding level N=64 keep K=10 (not 6). At each level make 4 children per parent: (i) exact staircase double; (ii) staircase double plus a 20-40% multiplicative dither on a random contiguous window of width N/6; (iii) a fresh rasterisation from a parameter vector drawn by perturbing the parent's 8 family parameters (log-uniform +-0.5 in pL,pR, +-0.3 in log cap/AL/AR, +-1 in log eps); (iv) a Gaussian-smoothed reconvolution of the parent followed by rescale. Score children by a smooth surrogate Q = sum_j L_j*sigmoid(beta*(L_j - 0.95*max L)) with beta=200 (not exact R) for pruning while N <= 2048, then by exact R for N >= 4096. Keep K=8. Cap each child's polish at min(1.5 s, remaining/(K*4)). Ladder 64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384,32768,65536 as time allows; print level, best R, mean R, spread, and the number of distinct surviving parents. Spend the last ~10 s on _polish of the global best.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.890 at 32768/65536, beating T79's 0.876384 and ideally F715's 0.882. Diagnostic: the best-mean spread should stay >= 1e-3 through N=1024; if it collapses again, the from-scratch ceiling is a property of the family, not of greedy escalation.

experiments.hypothesis: F793 gained +0.00043 on L9 purely by replacing a coarse beta schedule with a geometric continuation and adding coordinate-wise block polish on the full array; p0828's Q-sweep uses only five (c,beta) pairs and never polishes the full array block-by-block. experiments.change: Keep p0828's machinery. plan.analysis: Ninety generations and ~300 recorded attempts on the 0.941243 construction: every local, spectral, surrogate-max, target-fitting and 2x-refinement move returns it unchanged, so the record itself is mined out. The only mechanism that has ever gained near this level is coarse restriction / optimize / prolongation (F705/F710, +7.9e-5), and the only constructions still showing any life are T66's distinct 0.941205 basin (p0813) and the coarsened-then-upsampled record p0691. Slots 1 and 3 push that mechanism with things never tried on it (multi-factor and offset/shifted restrictions, generous coarse convergence). Slot 2 continues T80 by finishing the beta ladder and adding what F793 says was missing on L9: cyclic block-coordinate exact-R polish over the whole array, so mass can flow along the many near-null directions a few hundred cells at a time.

experiments.hypothesis: p0813 (0.941205, N=169984, 10.3% zeros, distinct non-staircase basin) is the only construction still gaining, and the one mechanism that gained on it was a coarse restriction/optimize/prolongation cycle (F705/F710). Restricting on several factors at once, each optimized to real convergence rather than a short burst, and prolongating mass-preservingly before a full-resolution polish should recover more than the single 2x cycle did.
experiments.change: Keep p0813's helpers (R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_log, _lbfgs_block, _polish, dict return). New first stage: for factor f in (2,3,4) build a restricted array hc of length ceil(N/f) by contiguous block sums divided by f (mass-preserving area average); run _lbfgs_log(hc, maxiter=600, fg=_fun_grad) with a generous cap (up to 12 s for f=2, 10 s for f=3, 8 s for f=4), then evaluate R. Take the best coarse result, prolongate back to N by mass-preserving linear interpolation of the *block sums* (each original cell gets the coarse value weighted by its overlap with the coarse cell), clip >=0, rescale, and polish with _lbfgs_log (300 iters) plus _polish(fracs=(0.02,0.05,0.10,0.20)). Accept only if R_of exceeds the current best; then, with all remaining time, repeat the best factor's cycle once more from the new best (coarse_optimize -> prolongate -> polish), always keeping the global best. Print, per factor, R before/after coarse optimize and after prolongation+polish.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.941250 (beats the record by >= 7e-6). Diagnostic: whether the coarse-optimized restriction has higher R than the direct full-resolution polish and whether the gain survives prolongation — a gain that appears at coarse N but vanishes after prolongation says the basin is resolution-limited, not shape-limited, and the same ladder should then be run on p0810/p0804 too.

experiments.hypothesis: T80's nested (c,beta) ladder stopped at beta=1e8 and selected c=0.98/1e2, so its Q surrogate was still far from the max and every step was rejected by exact R; F793 gained +4.3e-4 on L9 only when the beta continuation was pushed further AND coordinate-wise block polish was added on the full array. plan.analysis: The 0.941243 record is a saturated 2x-staircase at N=84992 (true dof 42496); ~300 local, coarse, spectral, annealing and target-fitting moves have died on it, and its f*f plateau (18% of knots within 0.1% of max, argmax at 0.573) says the remaining deficit is intrinsic and should need a *shape-rearranging*, not local, move. Every failure so far used either L-BFGS on the exact ratio (one-knot max gradient) or random perturbations. Untried: the KKT condition of max||f*f||_2^2 s.t. f*f<=1, ∫f=1, which says f*(f*f) must be constant on the unsaturated region — i.e. a purely multiplicative, projection-restored fixed point that touches all knots at once, is cheap (a few fftconvolves per iteration, thousands fit in budget) and keeps f*f<=1 exactly at every step. Bet: run that iteration at the record grid (slot 1) and on the fine 169984 grid to break the staircase (slot 3), plus revive F690's flat-target refit on the record (slot 2) to reshape the plateau through a worse-R intermediate.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact-R L-BFGS is stuck because the max term is carried by one knot, so no computed direction moves the whole plateau. The KKT condition for max ∫(f*f)^2 with ∫f=1 and f*f<=1 is that q = f*(f*f) is constant wherever f*f<1, so a multiplicative update h *= (q/qbar)^theta followed by the exact rescale h /= sqrt(max(L)) (which restores f*f<=1) is a projection-restored ascent using every knot's multiplier at once; this direction family has never been used on the record and is cheap enough to iterate thousands of times.
experiments.change: Start from p0828's h (N=84992). Add a routine _fp(h, theta, iters, deadline): (1) L = _knots(h) via fftconvolve, M = L.max(); (2) q = _backprop(pad(L/M), h) using the existing helper (this is 2*f*(f*f)/M on cells, i.e. the gradient of the numerator); (3) qbar = sum(q*h)/sum(h) (mass-weighted mean, computed only over positive cells), c = clip(q/qbar, 0.5, 2.0); (4) h = h * c**theta; (5) h = clip(h, 0, None); h = max(h, 1e-4*h.max()) inside cells that were positive (keep exact zeros only if they were zero for 2 consecutive iterations, otherwise re-seed them at 1e-4*h.max() with probability 0.05 per iteration) ; (6) rescale h /= sqrt(_knots(h).max()). Record R_of(h) every 10 iterations, keep the best. Outer loop until deadline: theta ladder (0.5, 0.25, 0.1, 0.05, 0.02), each with 200-600 iterations; after each ladder rung take the best h and run the existing _lbfgs_log + _polish for 2-3 s to consolidate, accept only if R_of improves. Print R after every ladder rung and the best R at the end. Return only finite non-negative heights.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.94130 (+6e-5), at minimum a first-ever monotone move off 0.941243. Diagnostic: print R after each pure fixed-point rung before any L-BFGS — if the pure multiplicative iteration raises R above 0.941243 the KKT/projection view is right and the record was a surrogate artefact; if R drops then rises only after polish, the projection is the useful part.

experiments.hypothesis: F690 showed that a prescribed flat target refit by log-height L-BFGS reshapes f*f substantially (0.878 from zero, 42% of knots within 0.1%). On the record, small-alpha spectral blends (F718) and shoulder-weighting surrogates (F783) never changed the shape; a full refit to a *hard* trapezoid target with a plateau fraction and ramp exponent different from the record's own is a genuinely different, shape-level move that is allowed to pass through a worse R.
experiments.change: Keep p0828's R_of/_knots/_backprop/_rescale/_lbfgs_log/_polish. New stage: from the record compute g = L/M on knots; find the plateau interval [k1,k2] as the first/last knot where g>=0.98 and the support ends [a,b] where g>0. For W in {0.28,0.34,0.42} and ramp exponent p in {1.0,1.5,2.0}: build target gt on knots = 0 outside support, 1 on [k1',k2'] (an interval of the record's support length fraction W, centred at the record argmax), and ramp_k = ((x-a)/w)^p (and mirrored) filling the two shoulder intervals, scaled so gt is continuous; minimize sum_k ((L_k - gt_k)/(gt_k + 0.1))^2 over log-heights of the positive cells with L-BFGS (analytic gradient via _backprop of 2*(L-gt)/(gt+0.1)^2, maxiter 200, deadline-capped), then run exact-R _lbfgs_log + _polish for 3 s and record R_of. Accept the best over all (W,p) if it beats 1e-14; then spend the remaining budget alternating fixed-point-free polish (_lbfgs_log full, then _lbfgs_block on peak windows frac 0.02/0.05/0.10) until the deadline. Return the best (or the start if nothing beats it) plus the start as alternative.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.94130; the informative result is the R right after the target refit and before exact-R polish (it will likely be below 0.94) and whether the polish then lands above 0.941243 — that distinguishes 'the record is in a shape trap' from 'the record is the optimum of its shape class'.

experiments.hypothesis: p0921 is the record on a 2x-refined grid (N=169984) and is an exact staircase, so it sits on a symmetry manifold that exact-R L-BFGS (one-knot max gradient) cannot leave; the multiplicative-projection iteration of slot 1 is grid-agnostic and, run at N=169984 from a dither-split start, can redistribute mass between each pair of twin cells — a direction that is invisible in the 84992 parameterisation and therefore was never searched by any of the ~300 failures on the record.
experiments.change: Build on p0921's h2 (N=169984). Seed: h2[2i] *= (1+d_i), h2[2i+1] *= (1-d_i) with d_i ~ Uniform(-0.03,0.03) (and a second seed with d_i ~ N(0,0.01)), rescale, print R. Then run slot 1's _fp fixed-point at N=169984 (same q = _backprop(pad(L/M), h), theta ladder 0.5..0.02, keep positive floors, rescale by sqrt(max L), R tracked every 10 iterations), alternating with the existing _lbfgs_log (full 169984 log-space, capped 2 s) and _polish on peak windows every ladder rung; accept improvements only. Use the whole budget, final report of best R and the odd/even cell-ratio spread (max/min of h[2i]/h[2i+1]) to show whether the staircase broke.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941243 has resisted ~300 local, spectral, target-refit, fixed-point, and upsampling moves; it is an exact 2x staircase and an exact-R local optimum. The promising untried directions are structural rather than local: (i) replace the outer ramp region with an analytic inverse-sqrt edge profile whose autoconvolution is flat on its inner half; (ii) break the staircase with large smooth odd/even modulation rather than small random dither; (iii) force a wider plateau by warping the record's own f*f target before refitting. experiments.hypothesis: The record's extreme max/mean and saturated ramp gradients suggest its outer edges are the limiting structure. plan.analysis: The record p0933 (0.941247) came from beta-softmax (log-sum-exp) peak-window polish, which unlike earlier sharp/p-norm polish actually moved a near-record basin (+6e-6) — and it did so while driving the zero fraction from 6.3% to 45.1%, i.e. the log-parameterised softmax polish is acting as a pruning operator, not just a smoothing one. Two facts stand out: p0933 used only 21 s of its 60 s budget (the loop ran one pass of the schedule and stopped), and the beta ladder was never extended past 1e7 in the window. So I bet on (1) iterating the now-effective polish to the deadline, (2) pushing beta much higher to sharpen the binding max, and (3) using the polish as the repair step inside a perturb-and-repolish hop, which failed before only because sharp polish could not repair the damage.

experiments.hypothesis: p0933's gain came from a single pass of the beta-softmax window schedule and it exited at 21 s of 60 s; the same operator applied repeatedly until the deadline should keep finding small improvements on this basin, since each pass changes the zero pattern (6.3% -> 45.1%) and re-opens room for the next pass.

plan.analysis: p0941 (0.941252, N=42496, 54.4% zeros, argmax at 0.986 of support) is the record; its gain came entirely from cycle 1 of the beta-softmax window schedule (F829), cycle 2 was flat, so the fixed schedule is exhausted. Its argmax now sits at the far right edge (p0933/p0940/p0942 had it at 0.17-0.19), so several knots are near-tied and the exact-max gradient is unstable. The zero fraction climbed 45%->54% during cycling, so pruning is an active mechanism worth making explicit. Three bets: (1) randomize/prune the cycling so successive passes hit new windows; (2) a new band-deficit surrogate that pushes mid-band knots (g in 0.5-0.99) toward the max, which is where the R deficit actually lives; (3) global low-frequency multiplicative reshaping plus beta-softmax repair to move large-scale mass that full-array L-BFGS cannot.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941252 (p0941, N=42496, 54.4% zeros, argmax at 0.986) came from cycling a fixed beta-softmax window schedule; randomizing it (F835), mid-band surrogates (F836), global low-frequency modes (F837) and multi-tolerance windows (F838) all failed on it. Two operators have direct precedent of working on basins with a similar zero fraction: coarse-grain restriction/optimize/prolongation (F803 gave +5.6e-4 on a 56.1%-zero basin; F705/F710 gave +8e-5 on another), and pushing the beta ladder to 1e9-1e10 (F830 gave +4e-6 on p0933, whose schedule stopped at 1e8). p0941's schedule caps at beta=1e8 and frac=0.40, so both are untried on it. Third bet: zero-revival (F183/p0204/p0229 worked on earlier constructions) is untried on p0941's 54% zeros. All three aim at 0.94127 (+2e-5).

experiments.hypothesis: p0941 has 54.4% exact zeros, and F803 showed that on a 56.1%-zero basin a coarse-grain -> optimize -> prolongation cycle added +5.6e-4 (F705/F710 added +8e-5 on another). info.open_why: The record lives on T27/H2 via p0941's beta-softmax window cycling; I need p0941's exact code and the findings F826/F829/F830 that produced its gains, plus F490's general statement, to design experiments that extend rather than repeat the fixed-window schedule.

plan.analysis: The record (0.941253, p0950) sits on H2, a near-staircase local optimum that has resisted every fixed-resolution, coarse-grain and high-beta-ladder escape (F836-F845). Two mechanisms did recently pay: repeated beta-softmax peak-window cycling (F829, +5e-6) and linear-space global L-BFGS where zeros stay zero (F846, +1e-6, zero fraction 54.4->58.4%). p0950 only ran the linear polish once, before the perturbation loop, so the two operators have never been interleaved. I bet on (1) alternating them cyclically to the deadline, (2) making the pruning explicit (rank-prune the smallest positives, then regrow in linear space, which the p0950 evidence says is the active mechanism), and (3) breaking the exact 2x-staircase symmetry with an antisymmetric sub-lattice split - a different map from the linear-interpolation doubling that failed (F844/F845).

experiments.hypothesis: p0950 spends its budget in one long perturbation sweep after a single global linear polish, whereas each cycle of {linear-space global L-BFGS, then beta-softmax peak-window ladder, then sharp full-array polish} changes the zero pattern and re-opens gradient room for the next cycle, as F829 showed for the window operator alone on p0933.
experiments.change: Keep p0950's helpers verbatim. Delete Phase C (the cosine perturbation grid sweep). After each sub-step accept into best only if R_of(ht) > bestR + 1e-13. Print per cycle: cycle index, R, zero fraction, argmax index/N. Final: two sharp full-array polishes before returning best.

Diagnostic: pruned cells returning positive in a different location with a rising R means mass relocation was the missing freedom (then push q larger); pruned cells staying at zero with unchanged R means 58% zeros is a genuine optimum of the support and the zero fraction should be left alone.

experiments.hypothesis: The record family is (near) an exact 2x staircase, i.e. a critical point of the staircase-preserving map; every resolution experiment so far used linear-interpolation doubling, which reproduces that symmetry exactly (F844/F845). An antisymmetric sub-lattice split breaks the symmetry and gives the two interleaved lattices independent degrees of freedom, which the sharp linear-space polish can then exploit.

info.open_why: Understand the exact mechanism of the recent +1e-5 gains on the record hill (p0933->p0941->p0950) and the beta-softmax window schedule, plus the coarse-grain cycle that worked on a similar 56%-zero basin, to design experiments that push past 0.941253.

plan.analysis: The record's last three gains (F846/F847/F848) all came from the same mechanism: linear-space L-BFGS that lets the zero pattern and the f*f argmax migrate (p0950 argmax 0.986 -> p0957 0.541, zero fraction 58% -> 11.5%), plus the beta-softmax peak ladder. Fixed-window beta ladders alone (F830/F842/F851) and multi-scale/antisymmetric perturbations (F844/F845/F849/F852) are dead. So I bet on (1) making the prune/regrow explicit inside p0957's cycle loop, (2) transferring the cycle loop to p0958, a sibling point on the same hill with a different zero pattern/argmax, and (3) a block-relocation sweep, since gains have tracked argmax migration. Targets are modest (+1e-5) because we are near the basin floor.

experiments.hypothesis: p0957's gains come from mass relocation via the zero pattern, but the regrowth of zeros is left entirely to L-BFGS-B's bound handling. F848's explicit prune-then-regrow added +2e-6 on p0950's 58%-zero basin; on p0957's 11.5%-zero basin, where argmax is at 0.541 and relocation is clearly the active mechanism, an explicit prune plus a gradient-directed reseed should open more relocation room per cycle than blind polishing alone.
experiments.change: Keep p0957 verbatim. Inside the cycle loop, after the (d) sharp log polish, add a prune/regrow sub-step: (i) take the positive entries, zero the smallest int(q*npos) of them for q cycling over [0.02, 0.05]; (ii) compute the objective gradient via _fun_grad on the pruned vector, take the flat zeros, and set the 3 zeros with the most negative gradient component to 0.01*max(h); (iii) call _rescale then _lbfgs_all_pos(..., 500 iters, beta=0.0), then one _window_polish_peak(frac=0.10, extra=128, beta=1e8). Accept into best only if R_of > bestR + 1e-13. Print per cycle: R, zero fraction, number of regrown cells that stayed positive, argmax index.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941265 (+9e-6 over 0.941256). Tell: if R rises while zero fraction swings by more than a few percent and the argmax index moves, relocation is still productive and more q values are worth cycling; if regrown cells all fall back to zero or R stays flat for 3+ cycles, the relocation channel is exhausted in this basin.

experiments.hypothesis: p0958 is a different point on the same hill: 21.4% zeros vs p0957's 11.5%, argmax at 0.282 vs 0.541, and it reached 0.941255 with prune-and-regrow but without p0957's repeated {global linear polish, softmax peak ladder, sharp log polish} cycles. F847 showed the cycle loop converts exactly this kind of alternative zero pattern into a gain on p0950; running p0957's cycle code on p0958's construction is a cheap, genuinely different local geometry.
experiments.change: Take p0957's code verbatim as the template but set the start to p0958's construction (the program's own `start` argument will be p0958). Do not add the prune/regrow sub-step of slot 1 here; keep the loop exactly as in p0957: (a) _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 800, beta=0.0), (b) _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 300, beta=1e7), (c) the four-entry window ladder (0.05/64/1e7, 0.10/64/1e8, 0.25/128/1e8, 0.40/256/1e8), (d) _lbfgs_log(best, 250, beta=0). Accept only improvements. Raise the final residual budget to two _lbfgs_all_pos polishes of 3000 and 2000 iters. Print per cycle: R, zero fraction, argmax index.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941265. Crucially, that densification happened only in the last two calls (global L-BFGS 4000 + 200 refine iterations) — the alternating cycle loop that produced most of the earlier gains never ran on the densified, de-staircased basin. So the strongest line has an unpolished basin at a genuinely new geometry (dense support, 3x more independent cells) plus a very weak inner optimizer (60 crude steepest-descent steps). I bet on three things: (a) re-running the cycle loop from the dense point, (b) replacing the crude knot descent with a proper step-controlled exact-gradient descent, (c) trying a higher resolution now that the array is no longer a degenerate 2x staircase (which is why F844/F845 were no-ops).

plan.analysis: The record (0.941267) is locally exhausted: the KKT test on its 67% zeros (F885), hundreds of random sub-block solves (F883) and 2x upsampling (F879/F887) all gave <=1e-6. Only support/grid changes ever produced 1-3e-6 (F862/F865/F867/F877), and those are used up at N~105k. p0995 vs p0996 is informative: identical max/mean (181.96) and identical f*f plateau stats, but 18.4% vs 67.0% zeros and near-tied argmaxes at 0.437 and 0.214. That means the same continuum f*f with a wide flat top, with the remaining loss in the ramps, and several representations of it at the same score. So I bet on three things that change the representation or the coarse shape rather than polish it: extension of the dense representation, coarse-level basin hopping, and mass-warp restarts.

experiments.hypothesis: p0995 hands back the SAME continuum f*f as the record (max/mean 181.96 in both, identical 14.91/27.97/34.62 plateaus) but on a dense 18.4%-zero representation with argmax 0.437. Support extension has only ever been applied to the sparse 67%-zero representation. On the dense array the added pad steps are genuinely new degrees of freedom unconnected to the existing zero pattern, so the extension+reoptimise mechanism (which gave +2e-6 twice, F862/F865, and +1e-6 on p0985, F877) has a fresh construction to work on.
experiments.change: Use p0995's construct() but gate OFF its 2x-upsample phase (it returns the pre-upsample length anyway) and, after its base cycle loop, run two support-extension rounds on the returned array: (i) pad = 12000 steps prepended and appended filled with 1e-3*best.mean(), then _rescale, print 'ext1 R=%.7f (N=%d) zeros=%.1f%%'; (ii) re-enter run_cycle up to 8 times, accepting only gains > 1e-13, until deadline-6.0; (iii) second round with pad = 6000, same fill, re-enter cycles likewise. Keep best = the best-R array over the un-extended start and all extended candidates. Finish with _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 800, beta=0), one peak-window _lbfgs_block(_peak_window(best, 0.25, 256), 250, beta=1e8) + sharp beta=0 polish, and _refine_knots(best, 400). Return best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941269-0.941270 (+2-3e-6). Tell: after round 1 R exceeds 0.9412670 within 3 cycles while the zero fraction rises from 18.4% toward 35-55% and argmax moves; if R stays 0.9412663 and zeros climb past 70%, the dense representation is the same continuum object and extension is exhausted at this support size.

experiments.hypothesis: Every local move on the 104992-sparse array is dead (F883: accepted=0 in hundreds of sub-block solves), so the only route is a different basin. At a 4x coarser resolution the landscape is different and each L-BFGS solve is ~16x cheaper, so ~15-20 noisy restarts can be afforded; F291 showed a progressive-N ladder can carry a coarse optimum up to a better fine point, and the record's own staircase structure (F920) means exact np.repeat prolongation introduces no interpolation error.

Then replace all tail phases (extension, closing polish) with: hc = 0.25*(h[4j]+h[4j+1]+h[4j+2]+h[4j+3]) (N=26248); print its coarse R_of(hc) as the baseline. While time < deadline-12: draw hc_r = hc * exp(N(0, 0.05)) on entries >0, and set a random 10% of hc's zeros to 1e-3*mean(hc); polish with _lbfgs_all_pos(hc_r, 300, deadline-12, beta=1e7) then _lbfgs_all_pos(..., 300, beta=0); print the coarse R; keep the best 3 distinct candidates. For each of the best 3, prolongate with np.repeat(h, 4) to N=104992, _rescale, run 2 full run_cycle passes, and keep any result beating 0.9412663. Finish with _refine_knots(best, 400) and one global _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 600, beta=0). Return best.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f has a wide flat top (two near-tied argmaxes at 0.214 and 0.437) and its remaining loss is concentrated in the ramps; the height profile is strongly asymmetric. A monotone mass warp (new cumulative mass at edge i = M((i/N)^gamma)) keeps the total mass and the sparsity pattern but moves mass between the plateau-forming bulk and the edge regions, i.e. it changes the ramp/plateau balance directly. This is a shape change, not a polish, and no 1-D mass warp has been tried on this hill (F831/F847 only used noise, sines and tilts).
experiments.change: Keep p0996's construct() and insert, before its base cycle loop, six warped restarts. For gamma in [0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 1.05, 1.10, 1.20]: build C = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(start)))/start.sum(); edges v = (np.arange(N+1)/N)**gamma; h_new = np.diff(np.interp(v, np.linspace(0, 1, N+1), C)); clip at 0, _rescale, print 'warp gamma=%.2f R0=%.7f'. Run one run_cycle on each with a per-candidate deadline of min(deadline-8, now + remaining/remaining_count) and keep the best-R result over all gammas and the unwarped start. Then run p0996's normal pipeline (extension rounds, closing polish, _refine_knots) on that best. Return the best array found.

info.open_why: Inspect the current record program p0992 and its two near-identical children p0997/p0996, plus the KKT/zero-revival failure F885 and the structural-gain findings F847/F862/F867 that produced the recent creep, to pick experiments that differ from the many failed local-polish variants.

plan.analysis: The record has plateaued at 0.941267 for ~10 generations across two representations (N=104992, 22% and 67% zeros give the same continuum), and every local move is dead: zero revival (F885), coarse basin-hopping (F890), 2x upsample (F887), many cheap sub-block solves (F883), cumulative-mass warps (F891), interior extensions with ε filler (F889). Since R = ∫g² for g=f*f normalized to max 1 and ∫g=1, the remaining 5.9% is pure continuum *shape*: area sitting in the ramps/tails. The one mechanism that theory says shortens ramps — making f's outer mass more singular — has only been tried as capped parametric families from scratch (F450/F474), never as a seed on the record, and always with useless ε-padding. I bet both main slots on that edge/ramp mechanism (decaying-tail pad growth; edge-concentration envelope), and flip D8 so polishing sees every near-max region rather than one contiguous argmax window.

experiments.hypothesis: All support extensions on this line used ε=1e-3*mean filler, which the optimizer immediately re-zeroes (F889, F878); a pad that instead *continues the profile* as a geometrically decaying tail from the current edge height gives the optimizer a real seed for a longer, more singular outer edge. Theory says such an edge makes f*f rise to its plateau faster (g(x) = c²∫dt/sqrt(t(x-t)) = const), i.e. it moves area out of the ramp into the top, which is exactly what R=∫g² rewards.
experiments.change: Start from p1003's module and reuse its helpers. DELETE p1003's six gamma-warp restarts and its 9 multi-zero KKT trials (both known dead: F891, F885) to free ~15 s. Keep one base call of run_cycle to get best (should be 0.9412670). Then, for pad in [8000, 16000] (one round each, each round given half the remaining budget via its own deadline): let act = np.flatnonzero(h > 1e-9*h.max()); hedgeL = mean of h[act[:32]], hedgeR = mean of h[act[-32:]]; rho = 0.05**(1.0/pad); build left pad vector hedgeL*rho**np.arange(pad,0,-1) and right pad vector hedgeR*rho**np.arange(1,pad+1); h_ext = concat(left, h, right); _rescale; print 'extpad pad=%d R0=%.7f N=%d' . Then re-enter p0970's run_cycle loop on h_ext until that round's deadline, accepting only gains >1e-13, stopping the round when a cycle gains <1e-9. Keep `best` = best-R array over everything (including the un-extended start). Finally run the peak ladder [(0.10,128,1e8),(0.25,256,1e8)] and one _lbfgs_all_pos(300, beta=0.0) on `best` with the leftover time and return it. Always leave 1.5 s margin.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941269-0.941271 (+2-4e-6 over 0.9412670). Tell: round 1 exceeds 0.9412670 within 2 cycles while f*f's 5%-band share falls below 34.6% (shorter ramps) and the outer cells stay finite but 10-100x larger than the ε-filler versions produced. If R never beats the start and the pad is re-zeroed again, the 'edge singularity' route to shorter ramps is closed at this support size and the next generation should invert it (soften the edges).

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f is spiky (max/mean 182) but its outer mass is not *concentrated* — a mass-preserving envelope that raises only the outermost few percent of the active support, then re-polishing, should lengthen and sharpen the top of f*f (higher 0.1%-band share, lower 5%-band share) and so raise ∫g². Previous restarts moved mass monotonically (gamma warps) or added tiny mass (ε extensions); none has ever re-weighted the *outer* cells of the incumbent in place.
experiments.change: Start from p1003's module, reuse its helpers, drop the gamma warps and the KKT multi-zero trials as in slot 1. Run one base run_cycle to get best (~0.9412670). Then for (alpha, tfrac) in [(0.5,0.01),(2,0.01),(8,0.01),(2,0.03),(8,0.03)]: act = np.flatnonzero(h > 1e-9*h.max()); d = np.minimum(np.arange(h.size)-act.min(), act.max()-np.arange(h.size)); tau = max(8.0, tfrac*h.size); w = 1.0 + alpha*np.exp(-np.clip(d,0,None)/tau); h_env = _rescale(h*w); print 'env alpha=%.1f tau=%.0f R0=%.7f' . Run one run_cycle on h_env with a per-candidate deadline = now + remaining/(#candidates left) (so all 5 are tried) and print 'env ... R=%.7f dR=%.2e zeros=%.1f%% amax=%.3f' . Keep the best over candidates and the un-enveloped start. Spend any leftover time in the run_cycle loop plus the peak ladder on the winner, and return the best-R array.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941269-0.941272. Tell: at least one envelope (expected alpha=2, tfrac=0.01) finishes its cycle above 0.9412670 with max/mean rising above 185 and the 5%-band share dropping below 34.6% while the 0.1%-band share rises above 14.91%. If all five lose >5e-6 and stay lost, the record already sits at the edge-concentration optimum and the next generation should test the opposite direction (mass diffusion away from the edges) on the record.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f has a wide flat top with two near-tied argmax knots (0.214 and 0.437 in different representations), and the exact-max and single-window softmax gradients both fixate on one contiguous window, so mass can only be traded inside that window; polishing *all* near-max regions jointly lets the optimizer shorten every ramp of the plateau at once instead of flickering the argmax between them.
experiments.change: Keep p1003's module and pipeline exactly as is, but replace _peak_window with a multi-region selector _peak_windows(h) that returns one sorted, deduped index array: take Lf = _knots(h), mx = Lf.max(); collect every knot index with Lf >= 0.999*mx, with Lf >= 0.99*mx, and with Lf >= 0.95*mx; split each collected set into contiguous runs, dilate every run by pad = max(64, int(0.02*h.size)) steps on both sides, clip to [0, h.size-1], union all runs. Pass this index set to every _lbfgs_block call in the beta ladder (same betas 1e7/1e8, maxiter 250) and in the sharp passes; add one final _lbfgs_all_pos with beta=1e8 on the full array at the end. Print, once per rung, 'multiwin nregions=%d nidx=%d R=%.7f dR=%.2e' plus the resulting 0.1%/1%/5%-band shares. Keep the accept-only-if-better rule and the whole rest of p1003 (cycle loop, extension, time guards) unchanged.

If R never beats the start and the pad is re-zeroed again, the 'edge singularity' route to shorter ramps is closed at this support size and the next generation should invert it (soften the edges).

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f is spiky (max/mean 182) but its outer mass is not *concentrated* — a mass-preserving envelope that raises only the outermost few percent of the active support, then re-polishing, should lengthen and sharpen the top of f*f (higher 0.1%-band share, lower 5%-band share) and so raise ∫g². Previous restarts moved mass monotonically (gamma warps) or added tiny mass (ε extensions); none has ever re-weighted the *outer* cells of the incumbent in place.

Keep the accept-only-if-better rule and the whole rest of p1003 (cycle loop, extension, time guards) unchanged.
experiments.prediction: Exploration judged on its own track: aim for R >= 0.941268 (+1e-6 or better on the record) and, more importantly, a *different* profile than the single-window version — if both near-tied argmaxes are inside the optimized set the argmax should stop flickering, the 1%-band share should rise, and the 5%-band share should fall. Tell of failure: the added regions just absorb mass, R drops and never recovers, and the profile stats come back identical to the single-window polish — then D8 is a dead flip on this hill and the plateau is genuinely single-region in the continuum limit.

info.open_why: Need the exact record program p0992/p0996 code and the KKT/zero-revival and support-extension findings that failed on it, to pick a genuinely different main-line move and a well-grounded D-flip.

plan.analysis: 0.941268 is a KKT point: zeros strictly inactive (F885), mass warps dead (F891), every max-surrogate dead (F490/F897/F899), support extension and envelope each worth only ~+1e-6. The one lever with an untested mechanism is grid refinement. Staircase prolongation is an exact symmetry point of the finer problem, so gradient methods provably cannot move off it — that, not the idea, is why F898 returned its start unchanged. Breaking sub-cell symmetry hands the optimizer genuine new degrees of freedom, and the finer grid's optimum is provably >= the coarser one. I bet on two refinements (2x, 4x) plus one compounding outer-edge loop.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a local optimum at N=104992 only because a staircase 2x prolongation is a symmetric stationary point: h[2i]=h[2i+1] implies equal gradients, so L-BFGS cannot move (this, not the idea, is why F898 returned its start). Breaking the pair symmetry with small antisymmetric tilts opens ~105k genuinely new sub-cell degrees of freedom, and the optimum over the finer grid is >= 0.941268, so a re-polish should strictly gain.
experiments.change: Start from p1008's module, keep all helpers. Delete the envelope loop (frees ~20 s). After start_best is computed (N=104992), build C = np.repeat(start_best, 2) (N2=209984, exact staircase, R unchanged) and run one UNTILTED control through run_cycle, printing its final R (expect exactly 0.9412680 — this tests the symmetry claim). Then for delta in [0.002, 0.01, 0.03]: draw e = delta * (2*np.random.rand(N)-1); set h2[2i] = C[2i]*(1+e[i]), h2[2i+1] = C[2i+1]*(1-e[i]); clip at 0, _rescale, print 'tilt delta=%.3f R0=%.7f'. Give each candidate a split deadline (now + remaining/remaining_candidates) and run: _lbfgs_all_pos(h2, 400, tdead) then p1008's run_cycle(h2, R_of(h2), tdead); keep the best over control + all deltas. Spend leftover time in _lbfgs_all_pos(1500) + _refine_knots(300) on the winner, and if >8 s remain do one more 2x refinement round (to 419968) with fresh antisymmetric tilts and maxiter halved. Return best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941271-0.941274. Tell: at least one delta finishes its cycle at >= 0.9412705 (+2.5e-6) while the untilted control sits at 0.9412680, and mean|h[2i]-h[2i+1]|/mean(h) after polish is > 1e-3 (asymmetry survived). If every tilt polishes back to 0.941268 with the asymmetry erased, the record's continuum is locally optimal in step-function space at every finer scale and refinement is closed for good.

experiments.hypothesis: The two outer-edge moves that each bought +1e-6 (geometric tail continuation, F895-line; mass-preserving outer envelope, F896-line) are complementary and cheap; run in alternating rounds with accept-only-if-better, and each round can re-open the edge region the other just changed, so the gains can compound instead of each snapping back on its own.
experiments.change: Keep p1010's helpers and its decaying-tail seeder and p1008's _envelope (paste both in). Replace the one-shot pad rounds with a 3-round loop, r=1..3: (a) pad both ends by 8000 steps with heights = edge_height * exp(-d/(0.10*N_active)) (continuation, not epsilon filler), (b) apply _envelope(h, alpha, 0.01) with alpha=2 on odd rounds, 8 on even, (c) _rescale, then run_cycle with deadline now + (deadline-4-now)/(4-r); accept only if R > bestR + 1e-9. After the loop: _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 3000) + _refine_knots(best, 300) under the closing deadline. Each round print (r, R, dR, zeros%, band01%) where band01 = fraction of _knots within 0.1% of max.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941270-0.941271. Tell: at least one round gains >= 1e-6 over 0.9412680 and the 0.1%-band fraction rises above 14.92%. If all three rounds return within 2e-7 of the base and the zero fraction snaps back to 66.5%, the record is stable under both outer-edge moves and only resolution changes (slots 1/3) remain viable on this hill.

experiments.hypothesis: The discretisation loss is not negligible: on a 4x finer grid the achievable R is strictly larger, but a plain 4x staircase is again a symmetric stationary point. Prolongating 4x, tilting sub-cells independently, and using a coarse-to-fine schedule (solve the 4x-block-averaged problem first for the large-scale moves, then re-prolongate with a smaller tilt and polish) lets the optimizer buy that discretisation head-room with a budget it can actually afford.

info.open_why: Need the exact record construction and its recent failed moves (p1003's plan/code, the zero-revival and warp findings) to pick experiments that differ from what already failed on this construction.

plan.analysis: The 0.941269 line is saturated under gradient polishing: the last six generations produced four +1e-6 moves and several identical-return results, all local. What still works on this hill is (a) changing the grid (F904's coarse-resample was the only fresh main-line gain) and (b) small structural re-weightings of the shape (F862/F877/F903 each bought 1-3e-6). All D1-D8 gradient machinery is stuck at the 0.94124-0.94127 hills, and F891/F895/F896/F901/F902 close monotone warps, tail pads, edge envelopes and staircase-prolongation on this construction. Betting on: a deeper multiscale round-trip (never run as a ladder, only one-shot), the interior mass shift that F896's own note recommends (opposite direction from the failed edge envelope), and large-amplitude basin hopping above the 2-10% window seen in F831.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's continuum f is unchanged by its 2x staircase, so all extra resolution is inert; the only way fine grids help is to first solve the *coarsened* problem to a genuinely different point and carry it back. F904's single one-shot round-trip bought +1e-6 on p1008; a full ladder (4x, 8x) with heavy optimisation at the coarse level and a symmetry-breaking dither on each refinement has never been run and should compound that.
experiments.change: Start from p1014's module, drop its pad/envelope rounds. Keep run_cycle and all helpers. After base best is set, for f in [4, 8] with N//f >= 8000: build coarse g[j] = mean(h[j*f:(j+1)*f]) (mass-preserving, same piecewise-constant f), _rescale, print 'coarse f=%d M=%d R0=%.7f'. Run run_cycle on g repeatedly until a cycle gains <1e-9 or a per-level deadline (half the remaining budget split between levels) hits. Then refine back: C = concat([0],cumsum(g)); u_new = linspace(0,1,len(g)+1); u_old = linspace(0,1,len(h)+1); h_up = diff(interp(u_new, u_old, C))*len(h)/len(g); _rescale; multiply by (1 + 0.01*(-1)**arange(len(h))) (alternating pair tilt, mass-neutral), _rescale, print 'refine f=%d R=%.7f'. Then run run_cycle on h_up with the remaining time; keep best over all candidates and the untouched start. Final: two peak-ladder rungs [(0.10,128,1e8),(0.25,256,1e8)] and one _lbfgs_all_pos(400, beta=0) on the winner. Leave 1.0 s margin.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941271-0.941274. Tell: at least one round-trip returns an array beating 0.9412690 by >1e-6 with the same zero fraction (66-68%) but a strictly larger 0.1%-band share than 14.93%. If both levels come back below the start, coarsening is closed on this construction and future work should stay at full N with shape moves only.

experiments.hypothesis: F896 showed that raising the outermost cells of the active support loses; its own note says the untested opposite is mass diffusion away from the edges. The record's f*f has a dip between two near-tied argmaxes (14.93% of knots within 0.1% of max but only 27.97% within 1%), i.e. the loss is in the mid-plateau valley, which is fed by pairs with large separation — the interior of f's support. info.open_why: Need the exact record program p1008/p1010 code and the findings on support extension and peak-window refinement to design three concrete main-line experiments that avoid repeating failed moves.

plan.analysis: The record is saturated on H2: every micro-move (pads, envelopes, interior sin^2 weights, fine-grid hops, 2x/4x tilt prolongation) returns within 1e-6, and the exact-max gradient only moves one knot. Two things did move the number in the last two generations and are not yet combined or pushed: the coarse-resample round-trip (F904 -> F907, +1e-6, only 4x/8x, one pass) and the observation that the loss lives in the mid-plateau valley, not at the peak or the edges. My bet: exploit the coarse grid as a genuinely cheaper, smoother search space (both for a deeper ladder and for real basin hopping there, since fine-grid kicks fail per F909/F910), and separately attack the plateau valley with a top-band-mass objective, which no hill has used (D1 alternatives are untouched: all programs still only soft-max the single argmax).

experiments.hypothesis: F907 showed a 4x/8x coarse round-trip gains +1e-6 in one pass; it was run once with only two rungs and never iterated, and never went to 16x where the coarse landscape is smoothest and the coarse optimiser gets many more effective sweeps per second. Iterating the ladder with accept-if-better and tilted re-prolongation should compound instead of snapping back.

info.open_why: Need the exact code and recent structural moves of the record line (p1019/p1014) plus the findings that drove the last gains and the coarse-resample/extension results to pick three non-redundant main-slot experiments.

plan.analysis: The record is a very strong local max on H2 at 0.941270: 30 generations of local moves (envelopes, warps, pads, coarse round-trips, band-mean objectives, random hops) gave 0 or +1e-6, and the f*f plateau statistics 14.94/27.97/34.62% have not budged. So the deficit is not in the peak value but in the mid-plateau valley, and first-order L-BFGS with an exact-max gradient cannot see it. The bet: (1) attack the valley with a new surrogate — maximize the L2 energy of the *clipped* profile min(f*f, c*max), which never rewards the peak and pushes every near-max knot up; (2) get past the gradient noise floor with curvature: Newton-CG using finite-difference Hessian-vector products of the existing analytic gradient; (3) if the point is a saddle rather than a max, escape along the most negative Lanczos curvature direction. All three are new mechanisms on this construction.

experiments.hypothesis: The loss is the valley between near-tied argmax knots (only 27.97% of knots within 1% of max). Every objective used so far rewards raising the argmax (exact max, logsumexp, top-band mean), which cannot push the 1-5% knots up without also raising the peak. Maximizing the L2 energy of the profile clipped at c*max (c slightly <1, annealed to 1) removes that trade-off: knots above c*max contribute nothing, so all gradient pressure goes to the valley.
experiments.change: Start from p1023's module, keep every helper and run_cycle. Add _fun_grad_clip(h, c, beta): compute num, dq, Lf exactly as _num_and_dq; form the soft max Mb = (1/beta)*log(sum(exp(clip(beta*(Lf-Lf.max()),-60,60)))) with weights w = softmax(beta*Lf); threshold t = c*Mb; u = np.minimum(Lf, t); num_c = sum(u[:-1]^2+u[:-1]*u[1:]+u[1:]^2)/3; dqc from u as in _num_and_dq; dLf = dqc*(Lf < t) + c*(sum(dqc[Lf >= t]))*w; grad = _backprop(dLf, h) + 2.0/h.sum(); val = -log(num_c) + 2*log(s) + log(Mb). Add _lbfgs_block_clip(h0, free, maxiter, deadline, c, beta) mirroring _lbfgs_block but with this fg (finite-difference-free, analytic). After the base best (~0.9412700), for (c, beta) in [(0.95,1e4),(0.97,1e4),(0.985,1e4),(0.995,1e5),(0.999,1e5)]: free = _peak_window(best, tol=0.999, pad_frac=0.25, extra=256); ht = _lbfgs_block_clip(best, free, 300, deadline-2.0, c, beta); ht = _rescale(ht); print 'clip c=%.3f beta=%.0e R=%.7f band1=%.4f'; accept only if R_of(ht) > bestR + 1e-13. After the ladder run one run_cycle(best, bestR, deadline-1.0), then a final _lbfgs_all_pos(400, beta=0). Leave 1.0 s margin.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941271-0.941273. Tell: at least one clip rung raises R above 0.9412701 by >1e-6 while the 1%-band share rises above 27.97% (and 0.1%-band above 14.94%). If the band shares stay pinned and R falls monotonically as c->1, the top profile is structurally fixed at this construction and the next test must be global, not a re-weighting.

experiments.hypothesis: Every hill uses L-BFGS-B, and the exact-R gradient here is dominated by the single argmax knot while the plateau is nearly flat over thousands of knots; residual curvature along the valley is far too large for a quasi-Newton diagonal-ish model, so L-BFGS stalls with a small but non-zero gradient and terrain it cannot follow. A genuine second-order step (Newton-CG with exact Hessian-vector products) should walk along that curved valley.
experiments.change: Start from p1023's module; keep helpers and run_cycle. Add _newton_window(h0, free, deadline, beta, maxiter): x = log(h_free + 1e-12*max); objective f(x) returns _fun_grad_beta(hh, beta)[0] and gradient g[free]; hessp(x, p) uses a central finite difference of the analytic gradient: eps chosen so that max|eps*p| = 1e-6, hessp = (g(x+eps*p) - g(x-eps*p))/(2*eps), where x+-eps*p -> h[free] = exp. Call scipy.optimize.minimize(f, x0, jac=True, hessp=hessp, method='trust-ncg', callback=_make_cb(deadline-0.2), options={'maxiter': maxiter, 'gtol': 1e-14}). Return the rescaled exp result. After base best, for beta in [1e6, 1e8]: free = _peak_window(best, tol=0.9995, pad_frac=0.10, extra=128), and if free.size > 6000 keep the 6000 indices of free with the largest h; ht = _newton_window(best, free, deadline-2.5, beta, 40); print 'newton beta=%.0e nfree=%d R=%.7f gnorm=%.2e' with the final gradient norm of the free block; accept if R_of(ht) > bestR + 1e-13. Then run run_cycle and a final _lbfgs_all_pos(400, beta=0). Leave 1.0 s margin.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941271-0.941272. plan.analysis: The p1032 hill is now saturated: three independent attempts in gen 305 (clipped-L2, trust-ncg Newton, Lanczos/saddle-move) all landed on exactly 0.941272 with identical band statistics (14.96/27.97/34.62), i.e. the optimizer is no longer the bottleneck — the construction's degrees of freedom are. F919's clip idea is the only objective that beat the wall (+2e-6) but was applied timidly (c near 1, then discarded). F867/F877 showed grid refinement + halo growth is the biggest structural lever on this lineage (+3e-6). So I bet on: (1) refine the grid + grow the halo on p1032 and re-polish; (2) push the clip anneal much harder (c down to 0.40, many slow rungs, long runs); (3) a new mixed objective that keeps sharp and clipped gradients active simultaneously instead of sequentially. info.open_why: Need p1032's full code and the clip-objective finding F919 plus F490/F915 (peak/valley objective facts) and F896 (outer-cell mass) to design three concrete main-slot experiments that build on the record's clipped-L2 direction.

plan.analysis: Ten generations on the 0.941273 record have bought +1e-6 each, and every re-weighting of the peak (clip, top-band, fused, Newton-CG, Lanczos, plain upsample) is exhausted on this construction — F919/F920/F921/F926/F927/F929 all land at 0.941273. What has not been tried: (a) a reparametrisation that can move the *global shape* with well-conditioned curvature instead of 100k ill-conditioned cell gradients (D2 flip, never used by any hill); (b) a long accept-only micro-hop portfolio, the only mechanism that has repeatedly produced the +1e-6 steps on this hill (F831/F847); (c) explicitly breaking the record's exact 2x staircase degeneracy, which is why every plain-interp upsample (F925/F929/p1038) snapped back to the same point. I bet on one of these three making a real (>1e-6) step, most likely the staircase break.

experiments.hypothesis: R is a continuous functional of the step shape, but the record has ~35k free cells and the exact-R gradient is dominated by one argmax knot, so L-BFGS on 105k cells has terrible curvature conditioning and cannot make global shape moves. Parametrising the profile by K coarse control points (D2 flip: spline/low-dimensional representation, never used by any hill) optimises the *same* function class in a well-conditioned coordinate system, so it can walk over the fine-grid valley barriers; the K ladder then recovers resolution.
experiments.change: Start from p1036's module (keep every helper, R_of, run_cycle, _lbfgs_all_pos, _lbfgs_block, _fun_grad_beta). Add _ctrl(h, K): positions xk = linspace(0, N-1, K); c = np.interp(np.arange(N), xk, h); return c. Add _raster(c, N): h = np.interp(np.arange(N), linspace(0,N-1,c.size), c); return h. Add _lbfgs_ctrl(c0, N, maxiter, deadline, beta): optimise x = log(c0 + 1e-9*max(c0)) with f(x) -> (val, W^T g) where h=_raster(exp(x),N), (val,gh)=_fun_grad_beta(h,beta), and W^T is the transpose of the linear-interp matrix computed with np.add.at over the two bracketing indices and weights of np.interp (multiplied by exp(x) for the log chain rule). L-BFGS-B with ftol 1e-20. After the base polish (run_cycle), for K in [384, 1536, 6144]: c0 = _ctrl(best, K) from the current best; c = _lbfgs_ctrl(c0, best.size, 400, deadline-6.0, beta=0.0); then beta=1e7 windowed pass at K=6144 only; h = _raster(c, best.size); h = _seed_zeros(h); run run_cycle(h) -> accept only if R_of > bestR + 1e-13, and print 'ctrl K=%d R=%.7f argmax=%.3f band01=%.2f%%'. Finish with _lbfgs_all_pos(400, beta=0). Leave 1.5 s margin.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941275-0.941278. Tell: the K=6144 stage followed by the full-grid polish beats 0.9412731 by more than 2e-6, and the log prints a changed argmax position and/or band01 > 15.0%. If instead every K snaps back to 0.941273 with identical band shares, the record's continuum is confirmed stationary and the parametrisation (not the point) was the issue.

experiments.hypothesis: On this hill the only mechanism that has repeatedly produced gains is a portfolio of tiny, cheap, accept-only hops (F831: 4 of 6 gained; F847/F848), while every single large structural move reverts. One 60 s polish cannot collect these; a loop of ~25 short hops, each repaired by a window beta-polish and a short sharp polish, can accumulate several +1e-6 steps.
experiments.change: Start from p1036's module unchanged, keep run_cycle/_lbfgs_block/_seed_zeros/_peak_window. After one initial run_cycle to confirm the plateau, enter: while time.process_time() < deadline - 1.6: pick a move uniformly from (m1) pick a random contiguous window of width w = int(U(0.02,0.15)*N), h_try = best with h_try[win] *= exp(sigma*z), sigma=0.05, z~N(0,1); (m2) compute the exact gradient g at best, rank its 66% zeros by g descending, open the top k in {16,64,256} at amplitude 1e-3*mean; (m3) pad P in {1000,3000} cells of height 1e-3*mean at one randomly chosen end, then _rescale; (m4) add a half-sine bump of amplitude 0.02*mean over a random 10% window. Then repair: ht = _lbfgs_block(h_try, touched_index_set +- 64 halo, 150, deadline-1.0, beta=1e7); ht = _lbfgs_block(ht, _peak_window(ht, pad_frac=0.15, extra=128), 80, deadline-1.0, beta=0.0); if R_of(ht) > bestR + 1e-13: accept (best, bestR = ht, R). Print every 5 hops: 'hop i acc a bestR=%.7f'. Do not accept equal scores (avoid drift). Use the remaining time on a final run_cycle + _lbfgs_all_pos(400, beta=0).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941274-0.941277 with at least 3 accepted hops. Tell: the printed number of accepted hops (target >=3/20) and whether band01 rises above 14.96%; if 0 of 20 hops is accepted even with tight (1e-13) acceptance, the plateau is confirmed tight and the next test must be global, not local.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is an exact 2x staircase (h[2i]=h[2i+1]) on its 104992 grid. Any plain linear-interpolation upsample reproduces a staircase exactly, which is a symmetric saddle: the even/odd difference direction is a *degenerate* coordinate where the first-order gradient vanishes, so L-BFGS cannot move along it — exactly why F925, F929 and p1038 reverted unchanged. Seeding a small smooth *antisymmetric* even/odd split gives that direction nonzero curvature and lets the optimizer actually use the sub-cell degrees of freedom.
experiments.change: Start from p1036's module unchanged. New phase before run_cycle: build h2 of length 2N by h2[2i] = h[i]*(1+d[i]), h2[2i+1] = h[i]*(1-d[i]), where d is a band-limited zero-mean perturbation: d = 0.03 * (sin(2*pi*f1*i/N + p1) + 0.6*sin(2*pi*f2*i/N + p2)) with f1 ~ U(3,12), f2 ~ U(20,60), p uniform, and clip h2 >= 0; _rescale. Then run run_cycle(h2, R_of(h2), deadline-2.0) with maxiter 600/300 and the beta-softmax window ladder at N=209984 (drop the ladder rungs whose windows exceed 40k free vars to keep each pass under ~2 s), then _lbfgs_all_pos(400, beta=0) at the doubled grid, then a final sharp _lbfgs_all_pos(300, beta=0). If the best doubled-grid R exceeds bestR + 1e-13, keep it; else merge back by 0.5*(h2[:m:2]+h2[1:m:2]) and re-polish on the original grid. Print '2x antisym R=%.7f N=%d argmax=%.3f' and the even/odd relative spread np.std(h2[0::2]/np.maximum(h2[1::2],1e-30)-1) at the end.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941275-0.941280 (the largest expected gain of the three).
