plan.analysis: The record hill H2 is saturated: the last 30 generations produced +1e-6 total, and every local scheme (hop ports, beta ladders, clipped-L2, band-lift surrogates, stair-breaking, grid lifts) returns the start unchanged on this construction. What still has not been tried is (a) genuinely discrete, mass-moving edits of the comb itself (cell-phase translations/mirror/swap of blocks, which no current move makes), and (b) a non-gradient map: spectrally inverting a deliberately flattened autocorrelation back to an f, which is the exact inverse of g=f*f rather than another penalty. I bet those two directions are where any remaining information about H2's ceiling lies. Slot 3 continues T85 (D8 flip) with a measured gain-per-second bandit over phases instead of fixed time fractions.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a spiky comb (67% zeros, max/mean 182) whose fine structure is fixed by the exact cell phase of each spike; every existing move (window perturbation, gradient-ranked zero opening, end padding, sine bump) is smooth or boundary-only, so no move has ever tried a discrete re-phasing of a whole block. Shifting / mirroring / swapping a contiguous block of cells changes inter-spike phases and comb period locally at zero cost; a repair on the two junction windows should recover most of the loss and can leave a better phase arrangement.
experiments.change: Use p1052's module verbatim (R_of, _fun_grad, _fun_grad_beta, _lbfgs_all_pos, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window, _rescale, _refine_knots, run_cycle). Set deadline = t0 + 0.93*budget. (1) One run_cycle to confirm the plateau. (2) Discrete hop loop while process_time() < deadline-1.8: pick a move uniformly — (a) SHIFT: lo ~ U{0..N-w}, w = int(U(0.05,0.35)*N), s = choice(±1,±2,±3); build h_try from best with the slice [lo,lo+w) moved by s cells, filling vacated cells with 0 and truncating at the array bounds; if s>0 the block moves right, else left; (b) MIRROR: reverse the contents of a random block [lo,lo+w) in place; (c) SWAP: two disjoint blocks of equal width w=int(U(0.05,0.2)*N) exchanged. (3) Repair: free = concatenation of windows [lo-128, lo+128] and [lo+w-128, lo+w+128] clipped to [0,N-1] (for SWAP include all four junctions); ht = _lbfgs_block(h_try, free, 200, deadline-1.2, beta=1e7); then ht = _lbfgs_block(ht, _peak_window(ht, pad_frac=0.15, extra=128), 100, deadline-1.2, beta=0.0); then ht = _refine_knots(ht, 150, deadline-1.2). Accept only if R_of(ht) > bestR + 1e-13 (never accept equals). Print every hop: 'hop k move=SHIFT/MIRROR/SWAP s=%d R=%.7f acc=%d bestR=%.7f'. (4) Final run_cycle and, if time remains, _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 400, deadline, beta=0).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941276-0.941280 with at least 1 accepted discrete move in ~20-30 hops. Tell: which move class is ever accepted and whether pure SHIFT (cell re-phasing) is rejected — if all SHIFTs are rejected while MIRROR/SWAP sometimes help, the comb's phase is rigid but its spike ordering is not; if nothing is accepted even at 1e-13, H2's fine structure is a strict local optimum under discrete mass transport and the next main-line test must be a different construction family.

experiments.hypothesis: All valley-flattening attempts so far (clipped-L2, q-power, top-band, q-homotopy) perturb f directly through a penalty in h-space, so the max term keeps fighting the L2 term. The exact inverse of g=f*f is available spectrally: if g is positive definite, f = IFFT(sqrt(FFT(g))) reproduces g exactly, and clipping only the negative spectral lobes gives an f whose autoconvolution has a far flatter top. Applying this to the record's own f*f, with the band [0.90,1.00]*max raised to max, produces a genuinely new candidate that no gradient scheme can reach.
experiments.change: Base p1052; import np.fft. Set deadline = t0 + 0.93*budget. (1) Compute Lf = knots(best) (length N+1), mx = Lf.max(). For c in [0.985, 0.95, 0.90] and for each: build target T = Lf.copy(); T[(T>=c*mx)] = mx; then smooth T once with a 3-point kernel [0.25,0.5,0.25] (reflect at ends), keeping T[0]=T[-1]=0; compute G = np.fft.rfft(T); Gc = np.maximum(G, 1e-10*G.max()); f0 = np.fft.irfft(np.sqrt(Gc), n=T.size); f0 = np.clip(f0, 0, None); if f0.size > 1: f0 = f0[:-1] (drop the last duplicate sample); f0 = _rescale(f0); print 'invert c=%.3f R_raw=%.7f N=%d' % (c, R_of(f0), f0.size). (2) Polish f0 with the record's ladder, guarded by time checks: _lbfgs_all_pos(f0, 250, deadline-0.5, beta=0); then the beta-softmax peak ladder for (frac,extra,beta) in [(0.05,64,1e7),(0.15,128,1e8),(0.40,256,1e8)] using _lbfgs_block(best_c, _peak_window(...), 250, deadline-0.5, beta); then _refine_knots(300). Keep the c with the highest post-polish R and print 'c=%.3f R_final=%.7f'. (3) If the best post-polish candidate beats the given start, spend the remaining time on run_cycle from it; otherwise spend the remainder on one run_cycle from the given start so the result is never worse than the start.
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.941280 (or, as a fallback, a clearly different but equal-R shape with flatter top band: band01 rising from 14.97% to >20% at the same R). Tell: R_raw of the spectrally inverted f before any polish (if R_raw is already >0.85 the inverse map is faithful and its ceiling is informative; if R_raw is ~0.6 the flattening target is infeasible for non-negative f), and whether the polished result exceeds 0.941274.

experiments.hypothesis: T85's flip of D8: the fixed 60 s split among polish/ladder/hop phases is arbitrary and phase productivity on this hill differs strongly between near-tied configurations. Measuring each phase's actual gain per CPU-second on the current basin and then spending the remaining budget on the empirically best phases (with epsilon exploration) should extract more than the fixed schedule, even if individual phases are unchanged.
experiments.change: Start from p1003's construction and its helpers (R_of, _fun_grad, _fun_grad_beta, _lbfgs_all_pos, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window, _rescale, _refine_knots). deadline = t0 + 0.93*budget. Define five phase functions, each taking (h, end) and returning h: P1 = _lbfgs_all_pos(h, 200, end, beta=0); P2 = _lbfgs_all_pos(h, 200, end, beta=1e6); P3 = _lbfgs_block(h, _peak_window(h,pad_frac=0.15,extra=128), 250, end, beta=1e7); P4 = _lbfgs_block(h, _peak_window(h,pad_frac=0.40,extra=256), 250, end, beta=1e8); P5 = _refine_knots(h, 200, end). (1) Calibration: for each phase run it once on a copy of best with end = now+4s, record dR = R_after - R_before and dt = process_time() delta; store rate[k] = max(dR,0)/max(dt,1e-9) with prior 1e-12; keep any improving output as the new best. (2) Epoch loop while process_time() < deadline-1.0: with prob 0.2 pick a uniformly random phase, else pick argmax rate[k]*(1 + 0.1*log(1+count[k])); run it on the current best with end = min(now+4s, deadline-0.8), update rate[k] by 0.5*old + 0.5*observed gain/second, count[k]+=1; accept the output only if R > bestR + 1e-13. (3) Final: one P1 with maxiter 300 and then 25 short stochastic hops (random 2-15% window times exp(0.05*normal)) repaired by P3, accept-only. Print after calibration and every 3 epochs: 'phase k count rate acc bestR=%.7f'.
experiments.prediction: Aim >0.941267 (T85's own best, p1003) and ideally 0.941272+; secondary aim is a measured ranking of phase productivity. Tell: which phase (P1-P5) ends with the highest gain/second and whether the bandit schedule beats a single fixed cycle of the same total length on the same start — if all rates decay to the prior within the first two epochs, the hill is uniformly saturated and D8 adaptation cannot pay on this construction.

info.open_why: p1043 is the record's base and p1050/F933/F937/F943/F947 are the most recent structural findings on the record's hill (degeneracy, staircase, 4x refinement, upsampling) that determine whether the next main-line move should attack the staircase degeneracy or the peak-valley structure.

plan.analysis: The record (0.941275) is a 67%-zero spiky comb, an exact 2x staircase, and sits at the fixed point of run_cycle: block shifts, mirrors, swaps, smooth/noise hops, spectral inversion, prune/regrow, clipped-L2 plateau flattening, coarse ladders and x2/x4 grid lifts all returned the start or +1e-6 over ~15 generations. Two things are still underused. (1) Single-cell spike placement has never been searched, and a mass-conserving move leaves ||f*f||_1 invariant so candidates are O(N) to score exactly — thousands can be screened instead of ~50 L-BFGS hops; it also breaks the (known-flat) staircase direction. (2) Support/tail growth is the only mechanism that has reliably paid, ~1-3e-6 per round, and prior rounds used small pads. Third lever: run_cycle still wastes ~15% of its time in _refine_knots, which F954/F1060 show never helps.

experiments.hypothesis: The comb's only remaining free parameters are spike positions. A single-cell translation preserving mass keeps ||f*f||_1 and ||f*f||_inf's scale fixed, so each candidate is one exact O(N) evaluation — thousands can be screened where block/hop moves could afford ~50 — and small moves break the exact 2x staircase, sliding along a direction already known to be flat before exposing new slope.
experiments.change: Base p1064 (keep its helpers verbatim), deadline = t0 + 0.94*budget. (1) One run_cycle to confirm the plateau. (2) S = np.flatnonzero(best > 0). Loop while process_time() < deadline - 3: draw a batch of 64 candidates, each a = random element of S with m = best[a], delta in {+/-1,+/-2,+/-3}, destination b = a+delta (skip if outside [0,N-1]); build h_try = best.copy(); h_try[a] -= m; h_try[b] += m; score with R_of (exact). (3) If the best candidate in the batch has R > bestR + 1e-12: adopt it, then run a short repair _lbfgs_block(h, indices [a-64, a+delta+64] clipped, maxiter=40, beta=0.0) and re-score; keep the repaired version only if it does not lose R. (4) Every 200 batches (or every 5 s) run a consolidating _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 150, beta=0.0) plus one _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(best, pad_frac=0.3, extra=256), maxiter=100, beta=0.0. (5) Finish with run_cycle and a final _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 400, beta=0.0). Print every 20 batches: batches, trials, accepted, largest accepted DeltaR, bestR.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941277-0.941280. Tell: accepted/trials and the largest accepted single-cell DeltaR. Any acceptance (even 1 per few hundred) says positions are a live degree of freedom and the search keeps climbing; zero acceptances over >10k exact trials says the comb's cell positions are rigid at N=104992 and only resolution/support (slot 2) can help.

experiments.hypothesis: Support/tail growth is the only mechanism that has reliably paid on this line (each round +1e-6 to +3e-6: F862, F865, F877, F896, F1010, F1014, F1019), but every round used tiny pads (4-8k cells at 1e-3*mean or short geometric tails). Three larger rounds with properly decaying tails should compound instead of saturating.
experiments.change: Base p1064, deadline = t0 + 0.94*budget. (1) One run_cycle. (2) Loop over rounds (P, tail_target_ratio) = (6000, 4e-3), (12000, 2e-3), (24000, 1e-3): let P be the stated cell count per side, hL = max of best over its first 32 nonzero cells' region, hR = same at the right edge; build h_new of length N+2P with the old h at offset P, left tail h_new[P-k] = hL * rL**k for k=1..P with rL = (tail_target_ratio)**(1.0/P), right tail h_new[N+P-1+k] = hR * rR**k with the same r; _rescale. (3) Polish: _lbfgs_block on np.arange(0, P+2000) with beta=1e7 then beta=0 (maxiter 150 each); the mirror window [N+P-2000, N+2P-1] likewise; then _lbfgs_all_pos(h, 300, beta=0), one _lbfgs_block on _peak_window(h, pad_frac=0.3, extra=256) at beta=1e8 then 0, then a run_cycle. (4) Accept the round only if R_of improves on bestR (else discard and keep best); print after each round: round, P, R, N, zero %, band01. If time is short, break and go to the final polish. (5) Finish with run_cycle and _lbfgs_all_pos(400).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941277-0.941280 with N growing to about 153k-177k. Tell: whether round 2 and 3 each still gain ~1e-6 on their own start, or collapse back — the latter would say the edge/tail structure is saturated and the remaining deficit is interior.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is at the fixed point of run_cycle, which still spends ~15% of its time in _refine_knots — a knot-space random walk that F954/F1060 show never improves. Fully densifying (all 67% zeros -> 1e-6*mean) changes the parameterisation from a spiky comb to a smooth vector with a far better-conditioned gradient, and a long refine-free global L-BFGS lets mass relocate globally instead of locally.
experiments.change: Base p1064, deadline = t0 + 0.94*budget. (1) Delete every _refine_knots call in run_cycle and in the hop loop (leave the function defined, unused) and put a second _lbfgs_all_pos(best, 400, beta=0.0) where it was. (2) One run_cycle to confirm. (3) Loop until process_time() >= deadline - 1.5: (i) hp = best.copy(); hp[hp <= 0] = 1e-6*mean(best[best>0]); _rescale(hp); (ii) hp = _lbfgs_all_pos(hp, 1500, beta=0.0); (iii) for beta in [1e4,1e5,1e6,1e7]: hp = _lbfgs_all_pos(hp, 200, beta=beta); (iv) hp = _lbfgs_block(hp, _peak_window(hp, tol=0.99, pad_frac=0.3, extra=256), 250, beta=1e8) then the same window at beta=0; (v) hp = _lbfgs_all_pos(hp, 300, beta=0.0); accept only if R_of(hp) > bestR + 1e-13. Print each iteration: iter, R, zero %, band01, band1. (4) Finish with one run_cycle and _lbfgs_all_pos(400).

plan.analysis: H2's comb is saturated: over the last ~20 generations every move class (local/discrete/split-merge hops, support extension in all flavours, resolution up/down, staircase projection, split-amplitude sweep, flattening objectives, zero densification) returned ≤1e-6. The record 0.941276 is a fixed point of run_cycle. So the remaining upside must come from move classes never tried on this basin. Three bets: (1) long-range mass transfer between distant spikes — every hop so far was local (±3 cells or adjacent merge), so the comb's global height envelope has never been perturbed discretely; (2) rank-prune-and-regrow, which worked on the earlier 0.941253 basin (F848) but was never tried at 67% zeros; (3) a D3 flip — population + crossover over spike heights, which no H2 program has ever done. All three are cheap enough to run alongside full polishing.

experiments.hypothesis: Every hop on H2 has been local: ±1-3 cell translations (F955), adjacent split/merge (F966), block SHIFT/MIRROR/SWAP (F949). None moved mass between spikes far apart, so the comb's global height envelope is only ever touched by smooth L-BFGS steps that stay in the same basin. A discrete long-range transfer changes the envelope at zero cost and the repair only has to fix two windows.

plan.analysis: The record is pinned on H2's 67%-zero comb, and every local move (translations, split/merge, long-range transfers, prune/regrow, population, crossover) returns +1e-6 or nothing: the comb is at a discrete fixed point of its own cell grid. All gains that ever mattered on this lineage came from changing a design decision, not from polishing harder. So this generation bets on three flips of shared decisions, each on the record's own construction: (1) D4 — free continuous sub-cell spike positions, which the exact 2x staircase currently forbids; (2) D4 alt — simultaneous coarse+fine optimization with a coupling residual, so coarse-scale mass moves are paid for at full fidelity instead of being lost in a resample; (3) a broad smooth envelope shake (D3's perturbation family, at a scale never tried) to let a different comb envelope form before re-polishing.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is an exact staircase, so every spike's phase is locked to integer cells; F949/F955 only tested whole-cell shifts. Giving each spike a continuous sub-cell center offset (and width) adds degrees of freedom that no current hill has, and re-rasterizing at the same N keeps everything comparable.
experiments.change: Keep p1081's module. After one run_cycle on the start, call a new phase: (a) segment best into runs of contiguous positive cells; each run becomes a spike (center = (start+end)/2, width = run length, height = run mean mass). (b) Rasterizer: for each spike add its total mass to cells by exact box/cell overlap (fraction of the spike's box overlapping each cell). (c) Pattern search over the spike centers' sub-cell offsets delta_i in [-0.5,0.5] and widths in [0.6,1.6]x, with step ladder 0.25,0.125,0.0625,0.03; after each accepted rasterization re-fit a +/-64 cell window with _lbfgs_block (beta=0, then beta=1e7) and evaluate R_of; accept only on improvement, keep the delta vector. (d) Also try splitting the largest spike into two sub-cell spikes. (e) Finish with run_cycle and a global _lbfgs_all_pos polish. Print the accepted delta histogram and per-phase dR.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941279-0.941281. Tell: if deltas settle at nonzero offsets and R rises above 0.941277, sub-cell phase is a real DOF; if every delta returns to 0.0, the staircase is genuinely optimal for this envelope and D4-flip should be dropped.

experiments.hypothesis: Every failed escape (F904, F907, F963) did restrict-then-refit, which throws away coarse moves on the way down. experiments.change: Keep p1081's module. New phase: c = block-sum of best into n/8 (mass-preserving); r = best - prolong(c), prolong = constant per coarse cell. Use analytic gradients: dR/dh back-propagated to c via prolong^T and to r directly. After the ladder, run one run_cycle and a global sharp polish. Print mu, dR per rung, and the final coarse-array change norm.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941278-0.941280. Tell: does any coarse rung produce a positive dR that survives mu->0? If the coarse array is unchanged in the L2 sense (<0.1% change), the comb's coarse envelope is already optimal and multi-resolution is dead on H2.

plan.analysis: H2 is the only competitive hill (0.941277); everything from scratch tops out near 0.94, and every local height/trajectory move (phase, translations, population, prune/regrow, coarse round-trips) sits at or below the 1e-6 noise floor. The only mechanisms that still pay are the structural ones: refine+halo (F867/F875), support/tail growth (F862/F865/F877), and split/merge edits (F966, the sole positive structural move of the last three generations). So I bet on three distinct structural mechanisms on p1087, each with full-budget polish cycles, aiming for dR >= 3e-6 rather than another 1e-6 grind.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is an exact 2x staircase at N=104992, so the fine grid still carries no independent information; a second refine+halo (2x prolongation to N=209984 plus boundary halo) is the only mechanism that has repeatedly bought +3e-6 (F867, F875), and it has never been applied to the 0.941277 construction.
experiments.change: Keep p1087's module verbatim (R_of, _fun_grad, _lbfgs_all_pos, _lbfgs_block, _peak_window, run_cycle). DELETE the _phase_search / population / crossover calls so the budget goes to the new phase. Then: (1) h2 = np.repeat(start, 2) (exact staircase, N=209984); (2) halo: pad 6000 cells on each end filled with eps=1e-3*h2.mean() constant, then taper the outermost 600 cells linearly to 0; _rescale; (3) _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0, 900 it); (4) run_cycle(h2); (5) if time remains, one _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=1e7, 300 it) then _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0, 400 it) then a last run_cycle pass; accept only if R improves. Print R after each step plus N, zero fraction, band01.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941280-0.941283. Tell: whether post-halo+cycle R beats 0.9412773 by >3e-6 and whether the polished fine array stays a near-staircase (then extra resolution is not the lever) or drifts to independent odd/even values with a gain (then 4x refinement is the next move).

experiments.hypothesis: Support/tail growth is the most reliable mechanism on this line (F862, F865, F877), but every attempt used a single pad size and a fixed 1e-3*mean fill with a symmetric layout. A parametric scan over asymmetric pad lengths and end-profile shapes tests whether the remaining gains come from the *tails* of f*f, which the argmax position 0.214 says are strongly asymmetric.
experiments.change: Keep p1087's module; delete _phase_search/population. New phase: S = flatnonzero(start>0); for (padL,padR) in {0,4000,8000}^2 minus (0,0), and for profile in {'eps-const','ramp-from-end','exp-decay'} build hp = concat(padL_profile, start, padR_profile) where 'ramp-from-end' = linear from the boundary value v (mean of the outermost 8 positive cells on that side) down to eps, 'exp-decay' = v*exp(-j/1500)+eps, eps = 1e-3*start.mean(); _rescale; cheap polish = _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0,250 it) then _lbfgs_block over the union of the two pad windows padded by 256 cells (beta=1e7, 120 it); record R per combo. Take the best candidate (even if unchanged) and run a full run_cycle, then if time remains one more round of tail-only growth: extend only the winning side by 3000 more cells and polish the new tail window with beta=0 and beta=1e7, then run_cycle again. Print a table of (padL,padR,profile,dR) and the final R.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941279-0.941281. Tell: the (padL,padR,profile)->dR table — if only asymmetric combos gain, tail asymmetry is the driver and the next generation should scan longer pads on that side; if no combo gains >1e-6, support growth is exhausted at this resolution.

experiments.hypothesis: Split/merge structural edits are the only non-polish move that produced a gain on the comb (F966), and they were only tried as a single trial inside p1087's failed phase search. A dedicated long accept-only hop loop over support-combinatorics moves (split, merge, birth of one new cell, death of one cell, mass transfer between adjacent spikes) with local repair and periodic full polish explores support *structure* rather than heights, which is where the record's remaining freedom is.

New phase replacing everything after one initial run_cycle: repeat until deadline-2s: draw one move — (a) split: pick positive cell a with prob ∝ h[a], set h[a]/2 and add h[a]/2 into neighbour a±1 (random side); (b) merge: add h[a] into nearest positive neighbour, zero a; (c) birth: set an interior zero cell adjacent to a positive run to mean_positive*0.5; (d) death: zero the smallest positive cell of a random run of length<=4; (e) adjacent transfer: move 50% of h[a] to a±1. Repair: _lbfgs_block over arange(minidx-96, maxidx+96) with beta=0 (100 it) then beta=1e7 (80 it), _rescale, R_of; accept only if > bestR+1e-13. Every 15 accepted or 40 rejected trials run a mini run_cycle pass (_lbfgs_all_pos beta=0 200 it, _peak_window ladder 3 rungs with beta=1e7, final sharp 150 it). Final: full run_cycle plus _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0, 400 it). Print per-mode accept counts and best dR per mode.

info.open_why: The record is stuck on H2's staircase comb; I need to see the exact base program p1081, what p1087's sub-cell phase actually did, and the findings on spike-position moves (F949, F955) and their refutations (F973, F966) to pick a genuinely new structural idea.

plan.analysis: The comb hill H2 is saturated for greedy local polish: p1092's hop loop gained +1e-6 but its own log shows death/transfer accepted 0 times, and p1090/p1091/p1094 all converged to the same 0.941277-0.941278 point from different routes, so the noise-floor gains are re-derivations, not new structure. Single-cell split/merge (F981/F966) is the only move class still accepting. Three bets: (1) same structural move class applied at half/quarter resolution, where one move changes spike count on a scale single-cell edits cannot reach in 60 s; (2) an explicit near-tied-knot penalty (D7 flip) that pushes the 15%-within-0.1% plateau up to the max instead of the softmax surrogate which only tracks the argmax; (3) the first Metropolis/annealing search on this hill (D3 flip) — every existing program is accept-only greedy.

experiments.hypothesis: F981 showed split/merge hops are the only move that still buys R, but each accepted move touches 1 cell of 104,992, so a full run buys only ~1e-6. The comb's spike count is a coarse-scale object; doing the same split/merge/birth/death hop loop on a mass-preserving pair-summed (N/2) and 4-summed (N/4) array reaches structurally different spike densities in one accepted move, and prolongation back is exact.
experiments.change: Keep p1092's module. After the initial run_cycle: for L in [2,4]: build hL by mass-preserving block-sum (np.add.reduceat over blocks of L), rescale; run a hop loop on hL for ~12 s with p1092's _draw_move/_repair but windows in half-res units (±48 cells) and beta=1e7 repair, accepting only improvements of R_of(hL); every 6 accepts or 20 rejects, take the current hL, prolongate with np.repeat(hL, L), run a short run_cycle at full resolution, and keep the result ONLY if full-R_of beats the incumbent by >1e-13. Finish with a full run_cycle plus _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0, 400). Print, per L, the number of accepted coarse moves and the coarse-to-full transfer success rate.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941280-0.941283. The tell: if coarse-level structural moves transfer (full-res R rises after prolongation), coarse spike count is a real DOF and the ladder should be extended to L=8; if every prolongated candidate is worse than the incumbent, the comb's spike count is locally saturated at all scales and structural work is finished.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f has only 15% of knots within 0.1% of the max and 28% within 1%: the plateau still has a hump, and R's numerator is exactly the sum of squared near-max knots. All existing peak handling (argmax gradient, logsumexp/beta-softmax, top-k mean, p-norm) targets the argmax value; none pushes the near-tied knots up toward a fixed target. A quadratic penalty on the near-tied set, with the target frozen at the current max inside each L-BFGS call, moves mass onto the plateau without the softmax's global coupling.
experiments.change: Add _fun_grad_band(h, mu, tol): compute num, dq, Lf as in _num_and_dq; M = Lf.max() (treated as a constant, not differentiated); B = {j: Lf[j] >= tol*M}; add value term mu*mean_B((M-Lf[j])**2)/M**2 and gradient contribution 2*mu*(M-Lf[j])/(|B|*M**2) to dq on B before the existing -dq/num term; keep the exact argmax term as in _fun_grad. Run a ladder of (tol, mu) = (0.999,1),(0.999,10),(0.995,10),(0.99,100), each with ~250 L-BFGS iters, followed by a beta=1e7 pass and a sharp beta=0 pass, accepting a rung only if exact R_of improves by >1e-13. Report band01/band1 fractions and the count of knots within 0.1%/1% of max before and after each rung.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941280-0.941284. Tell: whether band01 rises (e.g. 15.0% -> 17%) together with exact R; if band fractions rise while exact R does not, the plateau is already at its constrained optimum for this support and the D7 flip is dead on this hill (worth recording as a fact about the comb, retryable on H3/H5).

experiments.hypothesis: Every program on H2 (and every hill in the map) is accept-only greedy: a move is kept iff R strictly improves. On a hill where the best structural move buys 1e-6, greedy search cannot cross the small barriers that separate the 0.941277 point from a neighbour basin. Metropolis acceptance on R, with temperature scaled to the size of the residual improvements (1e-6..1e-5), is the one global search paradigm not yet tried on this construction.
experiments.change: Keep p1092's module. Replace the hop loop's acceptance rule with Metropolis on log R: draw a move from _draw_move (split/merge/birth/death/transfer) or a lognormal multiplicative hit (sigma=0.3) on a random width-1-3% window, repair with _lbfgs_block over the affected cells ±64 with beta=0 and 60 iters, compute dR = R_of(h2) - R_of(h); accept with prob min(1, exp(dR/T)) where T is recomputed each move as T = T0*(Tmin/T0)**(elapsed/total) with T0=5e-6, Tmin=2e-7. plan.analysis: The record hill is saturated: every polish surrogate, coarse round-trip, resolution bump, tail pad, SA/population hop and band penalty has returned ≤1e-6. experiments.hypothesis: F981 showed split/merge is the only move still buying R, but p1100's blind random hop loop accepts ~1 move per run (each worth ~1e-6) because it draws moves with no information. Rank by Δ=g·δh, greedily take the top 64 with index separation ≥4. For each candidate apply the edit, run _lbfgs_block on the union of [a-48,a+48] and the partner's window (60 it, beta=0; then 40 it, beta=1e7), take exact R_of, and accept the single best candidate only if R > bestR+1e-12 (recompute the gradient after each accepted move). info.open_why: Need the current record's exact code/plan (p1092), the split/merge hop finding F981 that still buys R, and the peak/plateau findings F949/F831/F490/F915 to design three concrete main-slot experiments that differ in mechanism rather than repeating failed upsample/anneal/band-penalty moves.

plan.analysis: H2's comb is a combinatorial local optimum: F991/F992 screened edits predicted Δ~5e-3 yet realised 0, which means the 97-cell L-BFGS repair restores the donor cell and undoes the move. That is a coder-side bug, not proof the moves are worthless. Three distinct fixes, all on p1105: (1) freeze the edited/donor cells during repair so the structural change persists, and spend the round on many cheap candidates instead of 64 expensive ones (F991 managed only one round in 56 s); (2) global multi-start search inside small windows — the one search L-BFGS never performs; (3) attack the measured deficit directly: only 15% of f*f knots lie within 0.1% of the max, so insert/transfer mass into the actual interior dips of g, with an exact one-dimensional amplitude line search and no repair at all. Each aims at 0.941282+; the tell is ≥3 accepted edits per run.

experiments.hypothesis: The screened split/transfer/birth/death edits of p1105 were all undone by `_repair_edit`, which re-optimises the donor cell for 60+40 L-BFGS iterations and restores the very mass the edit removed (pred 4.9e-3, realised 0). If the donor cell is pinned at its edited value during the first repair pass, the local optimum is recomputed under the new support structure instead of being reverted, so several structural edits per run can stick. The second bottleneck is throughput: p1105 finished only one round in 56 s, so candidates must be cheap-filtered first.
experiments.change: Keep p1105's module and `_screen`. Replace `_repair_edit` with: (i) freeze the donor (kind split: cell a pinned at its halved value; transfer/death: a pinned at 0; birth: b pinned at its birth value) by excluding those indices from the free set; (ii) `_lbfgs_block` on the union window [a-48,a+48] ∪ [b-48,b+48] minus the pinned cells, 40 it, beta=0, then 25 it beta=1e7 with the pinned cells still excluded; (iii) only then one free polish of the same window, 20 it beta=0. In `_greedy_edit_loop`: rank all candidates by first-order Δ, evaluate R_of on the raw edit (no repair, one FFT, ~3 ms) for the top 24 and keep the top 8 by raw R; repair only those 8; exact R_of on each; accept the single best if > bestR+1e-12; recompute the gradient and go again immediately (no mini_cycle unless 5 consecutive rounds reject). Reserve the last 8 s for run_cycle polish. Print per round: candidates screened, repaired, accepted, realised Δ, and a running count of accepted edits.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941282-0.941285 (2-5e-6). The tell is the accepted-edit count: p1105 accepted 0; if frozen-donor repair accepts 3+ moves and realised Δ per move stays ~1e-6, the lock was the reverted repair and the mechanism can be pushed harder next generation. If still 0 accepts with 8 repairs per round over ~10 rounds, support topology on this basin is genuinely optimal and the effort should move to a fresh construction.

experiments.hypothesis: Every escape on H2 has been a perturbation of the whole array followed by local descent, which always returns to the same basin. A window of 64-256 cells, however, is small enough that a genuine multi-start search inside it (dozens of random log-normal restarts, each polished) can find a better local configuration than the single L-BFGS path from the current point. Block-coordinate descent with real global search inside each block is a paradigm not yet used on this construction.
experiments.change: Keep p1105's module. Add a phase `_block_multistart(best,bestR,deadline,rng)`: loop until deadline-1.0 s. Draw a window: half the time uniform over the support of positive cells, half centred on a randomly chosen knot j with Lf[j] >= 0.97*max (mapped to index j//2), width w = rng.choice([64,128,256]). Free set = window indices. For k in range(8): make h2 = best with h2[free] *= exp(rng.normal(0,0.6,w)) (and with prob 0.3 set 20% of the window's positive cells to 0), clip, run `_lbfgs_block(h2, free, 20, deadline, beta=0)`, then exact R_of; track the best over the 8 restarts. If the best beats bestR+1e-12, accept it and run `_lbfgs_block(h2, free, 40, deadline, beta=1e7)` then re-check exact R before committing. Every 40 windows run `_mini_cycle`. Finish with `run_cycle` on the last 8 s. Print per 10 accepted windows: windows tried, R, best window gain.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941282-0.941286. Tell: the number of window restarts that beat the incumbent block configuration — if any window yields >2e-6 the basin is not a block-coordinate local optimum and the method should be run with larger windows next generation; if every window rejects, the basin is block-optimal at 64-256 cell scale and only global construction changes can help.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f has only 15.0% of knots within 0.1% of the max and 34.6% within 5%, so most of the 1-R deficit is interior ripple: gaps between comb peaks. A birth or small mass transfer placed exactly at a dip of g, with its amplitude chosen by an exact one-dimensional line search on R, improves the flatness directly; unlike p1105's random births it is targeted, and unlike p1105's screened edits it needs no local repair (which was what reverted the gain), so hundreds of trials fit in the budget.
experiments.change: Keep p1105's module. Add `_dip_moves(best,bestR,deadline)`: compute Lf=_knots(best), M=Lf.max(); find interior local minima d of Lf (Lf[d] <= Lf[d-1], Lf[d] <= Lf[d+1]) with Lf[d] < 0.998*M, sort ascending by Lf[d], keep the top 40. For t in 40 geometrically spaced values from 0.02*mean_pos to 3*mean_pos: form h2 = best with h2[b] -= t and h2[a] += t (clip at 0, skip if h2[b]<0), evaluate exact R_of (one FFT, ~3 ms) — no repair, no L-BFGS. Keep the single best (b,a,t) over all dips; accept if > bestR+1e-12; then run ONE local polish of [a-64,a+64] with beta=0 (40 it) and re-check exact R before committing. Loop for the whole budget, alternating this with `mini_cycle` every 30 s. Last 6 s: run_cycle. Print: dips examined, best raw Δ before polish, accepted moves, R.

plan.analysis: The record 0.941282 is an extremely mined local optimum: the last 12 generations produced ten +1e-6 steps and every gen-320 child returned its start. All programmes share L-BFGS-B on the amplitudes, a pointwise softmax/softmin surrogate for the max, and a fixed uniform grid. R = sum(g^2)/sum(g) with max g = 1, so the ideal g is a sharp 0/1 rectangle; the record's g instead has argmax at 0.205, only 34.6% of knots within 5% of max, and 66.6% zero cells — a broad, softly-sloped, asymmetric profile. I bet the remaining deficit is (i) in the *positions* of mass, which amplitude gradients reach only slowly, (ii) in second-order conditioning that L-BFGS cannot resolve, and (iii) in the shape of the target used by the flat-target projection. Three different attacks, all on p1119/p1122.

experiments.hypothesis: Every gain so far came from moving heights, never from a mass-preserving redistribution of the x-axis. Warping the axis moves the pair-sum density itself, so it can attack the record's lopsided ramp (argmax 0.205, long right tail) in a direction the amplitude gradient has not taken.
experiments.change: From p1122. Add `_warp(h, kind, alpha)`: with x_j = j/N, take a monotone map psi(t) = t + alpha*t*(1-t) (kind 'sym'), psi(t)=t+alpha*t*t ('left') or psi(t)=t-alpha*(1-t)**2 ('right'); invert it on the uniform grid by np.interp of the sorted forward map, and set h2[j] = H(psi_inv(x_{j+1})) - H(psi_inv(x_j)) with H = np.concatenate(([0.0], np.cumsum(h))) (mass-preserving, renormalised afterwards). Scan alpha in {-0.10,-0.05,-0.02,0.02,0.05,0.10} for 'sym' and alpha in {-0.4,-0.2,0.2,0.4} for the two one-sided kinds; for each candidate run _lbfgs_all_pos(150 iters, beta=0), then two _lbfgs_block peak-window passes (pad_frac 0.25 then 0.5, beta=1e7), record exact R, keep the best, then refine its alpha over {-0.01,-0.003,+0.003,+0.01} the same way. Print each candidate's raw R. Spend all remaining time in run_cycle on the winner; keep the printout short.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941284-0.941286. The tell: at least one warp whose exact R after the short polish exceeds 0.9412824, and whether the winner's band5 share moves off 34.62% or its f*f argmax off 0.205. If every warped candidate is below the record's raw R before polish, positional redistribution is already saturated on this basin.

experiments.hypothesis: Every programme on every hill uses L-BFGS-B, a quasi-Newton method whose Hessian approximation is useless on the ~35k-variable active set here; the +1e-6 returns suggest the stall is conditioning, not a true KKT point. The exact Hessian-vector product of the log-objective is a fixed sum of FFT correlations, so Newton-CG is affordable and can converge orders of magnitude deeper.
experiments.change: From p1119. Implement `_hess_vec(v, h, w, g, Q, m)` for Phi = -log(sum g^2) + 2 log(sum h) + log(g_m) with the argmax index m frozen: with g = _conv(h), Q = sum(g^2), w = -2g/Q + e_m/g_m, and hv = _conv(h, v), return 2*correlate(w, v, 'valid')[:n] - (8/Q)*correlate(hv, h, 'valid')[:n] + (16/Q**2)*dot(g, hv)*correlate(g, h, 'valid')[:n], all via fftconvolve. Verify against a finite difference of _fun_grad on a small random h (n=400) and print the max relative error. Then run Newton-CG on the free set (h>0 plus a 3-cell halo): at each of up to 20 outer iterations recompute g/Q/m, take the gradient from _fun_grad, run 40 CG iterations with a diagonal preconditioner 1/(2/Q + small), limit the step so max|v| <= 0.25*max(h), clip to >=0, rescale by _rescale, and accept only if the exact R improves (backtrack halving up to 8 times). Print ||grad||_2 restricted to the free set before and after, and R after each accepted step. Stop Newton with 20 s left and spend the rest in run_cycle.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941285+. The tell: the printed gradient norm at the record is not small (>>1e-3 relative) and at least one Newton step lowers the objective and raises exact R; a large drop in ||grad|| with no R gain would instead show the record is a genuine local optimum and the deficit is structural.

experiments.hypothesis: Because R = sum(g^2)/sum(g) with max 1, the ideal g is a sharp 0/1 rectangle, yet every flat-target attempt aimed at a 90-93% plateau spanning nearly the whole support (and returned the start). The plateau width and ramp width have never been searched as free parameters; a narrower plateau with steep ramps may fit this basin far better.
experiments.change: From p1119. Add `_fit_target(best, p, r, deadline)`: with Na = index of the last active cell and W = 2*Na, build T on the full knot grid (length n+1): 1.0 on [W*(0.5-p/2), W*(0.5+p/2)], cosine ramps of width r*W outside that interval, 0 elsewhere. Objective F(h) = sum((g/M - T)^2)/(n+1) with M = current max(_knots(best)) frozen, minimised by L-BFGS-B on h >= 0 with the exact gradient given by _backprop(2*(g/M - T)/M, h), 150 iterations, then rescale. info.open_why: The record p1119 and its recent children p1122/p1131 are the main line; F1004/F1011/F1015/F1017 are the flat-target and axis-warp failures on this exact construction, so I can see which design decisions remain untried and avoid repeats.

plan.analysis: The record p1137 (0.941283) sits on a spiky 2-cell-staircase comb; height-only L-BFGS and every global surrogate/coarse/warp/Metropolis escape have stalled. The only move that still bought R recently was continuous sub-cell run shifting (F1023, +1e-6), and discrete split/merge hops (F966/F981) also bought ~1e-6 but were often erased by repair. I am betting that exact-gradient continuous support geometry—per-run affine warp and continuous run splitting—adds degrees of freedom no height change can express, and that alternating them compounds. All three experiments use p1137 as base and preserve mass exactly.

experiments.hypothesis: p1137 optimised only rigid sub-cell shifts s_k in [-0.5,0.5] on tall runs. Allowing each tall run an affine warp (shift s_k plus stretch r_k about its centre of mass), with exact piecewise-linear re-splatting and the exact-R gradient chained through it, adds a width/phase degree of freedom that height-only L-BFGS cannot express and that rigid shifts cannot reach.
experiments.change: From p1137. Identify maximal runs of consecutive positive cells. Keep runs whose peak height >= 0.25*global max; print the count. For each kept run k with original masses m_j at integer positions j and centre c_k = sum_j j*m_j / sum m_j, define an affine map p -> c_k + (p - c_k)*r_k + s_k. Re-splat the run's masses linearly onto the grid through this map (mass-preserving; at r_k=1,s_k=0 it reproduces the run exactly); all unkept runs stay fixed. Implement `_warp(h, runs, s, r)` returning h2 and its exact derivative w.r.t. s_k and r_k given dR/dh2, validating against a finite difference for one k (print relative error). Optimise exact R via `_fun_grad` over (s_k, r_k) and all heights jointly with L-BFGS-B, bounds s_k in [-1,1], r_k in [0.8,1.25], init s=0,r=1; run 3 rounds of shifts+scales only, heights only, then joint, keeping the best exact-R warped array, and finish with `run_cycle`. Print max|s| and max|r-1| after each round.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941284-0.941286. The tell is whether max|r-1| > 0.02 or max|s| > 0.05 survives and the final R beats 0.9412824 by more than 1e-6; if all r anneal to 1 and s to 0, rigid sub-cell positions are already optimal and the affine degree of freedom is dead on this hill.

experiments.hypothesis: Discrete split/merge hops bought ~1e-6 (F966, F981) but repair re-optimised away the edited structure. experiments.change: From p1137. Select the top K runs by peak height with peak >= 0.7*global max, K capped at 32; print K. Implement `_split(h, runs, d, f)` and its exact derivative w.r.t. d_k, x_k and all heights via the chain rule, validating against a finite difference for one k (print relative error). Optimise exact R over (d_k,x_k) plus heights with L-BFGS-B, bounds d_k in [0,4], x_k free; 3 rounds of split parameters only, heights only, joint, keeping the best exact-R array, then `run_cycle`. experiments.change: From p1137. Select the top K runs by peak height with peak >= 0.7*global max, K capped at 32; print K. For each selected run k with original mass distribution m_j, create two copies scaled by f_k and 1-f_k (f_k = sigmoid(x_k), init 0.5) and shifted by -d_k/2 and +d_k/2 respectively, d_k in [0,4] cells, re-splatted linearly onto the grid and summed; at d_k=0 this reproduces the run exactly. Implement `_split(h, runs, d, f)` and its exact derivative w.r.t. d_k, x_k and all heights via the chain rule, validating against a finite difference for one k (print relative error). Optimise exact R over (d_k,x_k) plus heights with L-BFGS-B, bounds d_k in [0,4], x_k free; 3 rounds of split parameters only, heights only, joint, keeping the best exact-R array, then `run_cycle`. Print d_k and f_k for the largest few runs each round.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941284-0.941286. The tell is whether several d_k > 0.1 survive with f_k away from 0.5 and the final R beats 0.9412824 by >1e-6. If d collapses to 0 for all runs, continuous splitting is locally neutral on this hill and discrete split/merge gains were only repair noise.

experiments.hypothesis: The affine-warp and continuous-split mechanisms act on different autocorrelation features: per-run warp changes the local triangle width/phase, while splitting changes spike multiplicity and the flat-top shape. Alternating them lets the heights and the other continuous parameters co-adapt, so the sum can exceed the ~1e-6 each buys alone.
experiments.change: From p1137. Implement both parameterisations from slots 1 and 2 in one program. Loop up to 4 rounds or until 10 s remain: (a) L-BFGS on affine warp parameters (s,r) plus heights, (b) L-BFGS on split parameters (d,f) plus heights, (c) full-array L-BFGS polish with `_lbfgs_all_pos`, then a beta-softmax window polish and `run_cycle`. Always keep the best exact-R array. Rebuild run indices after each accepted structural change. Print after each round: R, number of runs, max|s|, max|r-1|, max d, and number of splits with d>0.1. If a round loses R, revert that round and continue with the other mechanism. Use the remaining budget for a final `run_cycle`.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941285-0.941287. The tell is that at least one warp parameter and one split parameter remain nonzero at the end and the alternating result beats both single-mechanism results; if one mechanism collapses, report which and keep the other, which still must beat 0.9412824 by more than 1e-6.

plan.analysis: H2 (0.941284) is a saturated comb: this generation's four children (sub-cell shift, affine warp, continuous split, 2x/3x refinement) all landed within 1e-6 of the base, and F1027-F1030 show continuous geometry, warp+split combinations and finer grids are dead on this construction. The only positive signal is F1023's re-splat (+1e-6) and p1143's split (0.941284) — both tiny, and both immediately re-polished by run_cycle, which likely erases the edited structure. So the bet is: (a) make the continuous-shape moves more expressive and stop the polish from undoing them, (b) generalise the per-run template from shift/stretch/split to a free small kernel, and (c) attack the flat-ramp deficit through the objective itself, replacing the single-argmax/softmax peak term all hills share with an explicit active-set constraint on the top knots. Every experiment starts from p1143, so a null result costs nothing.

experiments.hypothesis: p1143's continuous split moved R to 0.941284 but one split per top run plus an immediate full-array run_cycle re-flattens the edited spikes; recursive splitting (each copy split again) with only local window repair should let the split structure survive and compound, since a single split cannot represent the multi-cell sub-shape the ramp needs.
experiments.change: From p1143, reuse its exact re-splat machinery but replace the single split with a 3-way split applied twice. Round 1: for each top run (peak >= 0.7*global max, K <= 32, print K), replace its mass distribution m_j by 3 copies at separations d1,d2 in [-1.5,1.5] with mass fractions softmax(f1,f2,f3) (init d=(-0.5,0,0.5), f=(1/3,1/3,1/3)); exact piecewise-linear re-splat, FD-check one gradient, print relative error. Round 2: re-split each of the copies of the top 8 original runs into 2 more copies (K<=16). After each round do ONLY local repair: L-BFGS on the window [run_start-48, run_end+48] of each edited run, 80 iters, no global/run_cycle call. Then joint L-BFGS on all split parameters (d, f) plus all heights of the affected windows, 400 iters. Only in the final 15 s run the existing run_cycle polish. Keep the best exact-R array seen at any point (also keep the pre-polish array and return whichever scores higher). Print max|d| and count of |d|>0.05 surviving after the joint pass.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941285-0.941287. The tell: several |d|>0.05 survive the joint pass with f away from 1/3, and the pre-polish array beats the post-run_cycle array — which would prove the earlier failures were polish-erasure, not absence of a direction. If all separations anneal to 0, per-run sub-shape freedom is exhausted on H2.

experiments.hypothesis: Shift, stretch and split each buy <=1e-6 because each is a one-parameter slice of the real degree of freedom: the shape of each spike at the sub-cell level. A free 5-cell kernel per tall run (initialised as a pure delta, so the start is unchanged) spans all of them at once and lets L-BFGS discover which slice, if any, the ramp needs.
experiments.change: From p1143. Identify maximal runs of positive cells; keep runs with peak >= 0.5*global max (print count, expect O(100)). Each kept run k gets a kernel w_k in R^5, w >= 0, init (1e-4,1e-4,1,1e-4,1e-4) (near-delta, break symmetry). The run's mass distribution m_j is re-splatted onto fine cells i = round(centre_k)+(-2..+2) with weights w_k[idx] normalised to sum 1, times the run's total mass; unkept runs untouched. Write _splat(h, runs, W) -> h2 and its exact adjoint _splat_grad(h, runs, W, dRdh) -> dR/dW (piecewise linear; FD-validate one entry, print rel. err). Objective: exact R via _fun_grad on h2, chain to (all W entries, heights of kept runs) with L-BFGS-B, W >= 0. Schedule: (a) W only 200 iters, (b) heights only 200 iters, (c) joint 400 iters, repeat 3 rounds, then a final joint pass with run_cycle on the remaining budget; return the best exact-R array including the pre-run_cycle one. Print the final kernel-weight spread (sum of |w_i - mean(w)| / sum w) averaged over runs, and how many runs end with a non-delta profile.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941285-0.941286. The tell is a mean kernel spread well above zero surviving alongside a score gain > 1e-6; if every kernel relaxes back to a delta, the spikes really are single-cell-optimal and the deficit is not in spike shape.

experiments.hypothesis: Every hill handles ||f*f||_inf with an argmax gradient or a logsumexp softmax (D2/D7), which pushes mass toward one knot or a whole soft band. The record's f*f has only 15% of knots within 0.1% of the max, so what limits it is the transition band just below the peak. An explicit active-set constraint on the top knots -- pin the m largest knots at the max instead of one -- gives a fundamentally different gradient direction and should lift the ramp just under the plateau.
experiments.change: From p1143. Replace the argmax/softmax peak term with an augmented Lagrangian. Define Q(h) = num/s^2 (L2 numerator over squared mass, the parts of -log R that are smooth) and constraint c(h) = mean of the m=8 largest knots of L minus max(L) (i.e. c measures how far below the top the 8th-largest knot is; c = 0 when all top 8 are tied). Maximise log Q(h) - lambda*c(h) - (rho/2)*max(0,c... ) — specifically implement: val = -log(num) + 2*log(s) + lambda*g(h) + (rho/2)*g(h)^2 with g(h) = 1 - mean(top-8 knots)/max_knot (>=0, 0 when tied); gradient of the top-8 mean is (+1/8)/max_knot on those 8 knots, gradient of the max term is the usual single-argmax term scaled by the mean/max ratio; validate the whole gradient by finite differences on 5 random coordinates and print the relative error. rho fixed 50, lambda updated every 150 L-BFGS iterations: lambda <- max(0, lambda + 0.2*rho*g) (5 rounds max). After the ladder, take the last array, optionally run one plain exact-R run_cycle pass in the remaining 15 s, and return the better of the two by exact R. Print the tie spread (top-8 knots vs max, in %) at the end of each lambda round.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941285-0.941287. The tell is the top-8 spread shrinking from ~1e-3 to <1e-5 while R rises above 0.9412845; if lambda diverges with the spread unchanged, the single-argmax objective is not the binding constraint on H2 and the deficit is the outer ramp only.

info.open_why: The record's hill H2 is saturated by every local/parametric move tried on p1137 (warp, split, resample all failed); I need to see p1137's exact construction and code to judge whether any unexplored structural lever remains, or whether the main slots should instead push a different hill/exploration.

plan.analysis: H2's comb is saturated: 20+ generations of 1e-6 gains, and every sub-cell/run-shape degree of freedom (F1023, F1027, F1028, F1029, F1030, F1032, F1033, F1036) and every peak-constraint reformulation (F986, F1034) now returns exactly the start. F1036's 2x-refinement returning the start unchanged says resolution is not the limiter; F1033 says spike micro-shape is not either. What still has a positive hit rate on this line is support growth (F862, F865, F867, F877 each +2e-6..+3e-6) and changes to what the gradient is pointed at. I am betting on three cheap, orthogonal probes: grow the support with a toe-matched ramp (the record at N=104992 has never been extended), point the gradient at the mid-band shoulders where the loss actually lives (all prior band objectives targeted the top band), and test whether the 66.5% exact zeros are load-bearing by lifting the whole array onto a pedestal.

experiments.hypothesis: The record was last support-extended at p0969 (N=50496 -> 104992, F867); since then only heights moved. Support growth is the one mechanism that has repeatedly paid on H2 (+2e-6 to +3e-6), and it has never been tried on the current N=104992 array. Previous extension attempts used either a constant 1e-3*mean filler (F877) or repeated exponential-continuation rounds (F903, refuted); a single round whose pad is a graded continuation of the actual toe gives L-BFGS a ramp it can grow into rather than a flat shelf to delete.
experiments.change: Start from p1149 (N=104992). Find the active support [s0,s1]. Pad 8000 cells on each end (N -> 120992). Left pad h[i] = A_L * exp(-(s0-i)/60) for i<s0, where A_L = max(h[s0:s0+8]); right pad h[i] = A_R * exp(-(i-s1)/60) with A_R = max(h[s1-7:s1+1]). Then: (a) `_rescale`; (b) L-BFGS-B (bounds >=0) restricted to the free set {pad cells} U {first/last 2000 cells of the old support}, maxiter 400; (c) full-array L-BFGS 400 iters with beta=0; (d) the base's beta ladder peak-window polish (fracs 0.05/0.10/0.25/0.40, beta 1e7-1e8) plus a final sharp pass, keeping the best exact R at every step. Print s0,s1, pad mass after (c), and band01/band1 of f*f. If time remains, repeat once with pad=4000 and keep the better.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941286-0.941288. The tell is that the pad keeps nonzero mass after (c) and band01 rises above 15.05% while exact R beats 0.9412845; if the pad is driven back to ~1e-3*mean and R is unchanged, the tail is genuinely saturated and only F877-style shelves exist there.

experiments.hypothesis: With max(g)=1 and mass fixed, R = 1 - [sum g(1-g)]/mass, so the loss is carried by knots at intermediate values, not by the near-max band: the record has 15.0% of knots within 0.1% of max but only 34.6% within 5%, and the knots between 0.3 and 0.98 are exactly the ones the log-term never pushes on (the beta-softmax weight is exp(beta(L-M)) ~ 0 there, and the L2 term's weight dq is already near its floor). F915/F986/F1035 all aimed at the top band and returned the start; aiming the extra gradient at the mid band is an untried direction.
experiments.change: From p1149. Add `_fun_grad_mid(h, eta)`: same as `_fun_grad` but with an extra term pen = eta * sum_j w_j*(1 - Lf_j/M) / max(cnt,1), where w_j = 1 for 0.30*M <= Lf_j <= 0.98*M and 0 otherwise, cnt = sum w, and M treated as a constant so dLf_j += -eta*w_j/(M*max(cnt,1)); add this into gLf before `_backprop` and into val. Run a ladder eta in {0.5, 2, 8, 32}: each rung calls `_lbfgs_all_pos` with beta=0 on ~250 iters, then a sharp 150-iter pass, keeps the best exact R; then spend the rest on the base's `run_cycle`. Print per rung: eta, fraction of knots in [0.3,0.98]M, their mean value/M, and exact R after the sharp pass.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.9412855-0.941287. The tell is the mid-band mean value rising with eta on at least one rung while exact R after the sharp pass beats 0.9412845. If the mid-band mean is pinned and R falls monotonically with eta, the shoulders are forced by the support geometry and this direction is closed.

experiments.hypothesis: 66.5% of the record's heights are exactly zero and the base only ever seeds them at 1e-6*mean before re-applying a hard lower bound at 0, so 'f is a comb with exact gaps' is an assumption of the parameterisation, never a tested optimum: every accept-only edit that has to pass through an exact-zero (F966, F981) dies. Lifting the whole array by a common pedestal adds a smooth triangular component to g that raises the shoulders from below, and the pedestal amplitude is a single scalar whose optimum the exact R can find by scanning (F1031's dense seed helped on L8; that used 1e-6*mean, three orders below what a real floor would be).
experiments.change: From p1149. Let m = mean(h[h>0]). For p in {1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2}*m: h_p = h + p (every cell, including zeros), `_rescale`, then `_lbfgs_all_pos` 350 iters beta=0, a beta=1e7 softmax pass (150 iters), and a peak-window polish (fracs 0.10/0.30, 150 iters each), taking the best exact R; print p, resulting zeros fraction, and R. Then bracket the best p geometrically by factor 1/3 and 3 on each side, rerun the same short schedule on those two, and spend the remaining time running the base's `run_cycle` from the overall best array.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941286-0.941288. The tell is an interior optimum: R rising for small p, peaking, and falling at 1e-2*m, with the zeros fraction dropping from 66.5% to 40-60% and surviving the polish. If R falls monotonically from p=1e-5*m (i.e. the best is p->0), exact gaps are optimal and the comb structure is confirmed as load-bearing, which is itself a decisive fact for this hill.

plan.analysis: H2 is saturated for every continuous/polish move: pedestal (F1040), mid-band penalty (F1039), flat-top softmax and knot flattening (F1035/F1041), augmented Lagrangian peak pin (F1034), 2x densify (F1036/F1042), toe padding (F1038), sub-cell shifts and recursive splits (p1149/p1150) all bought nothing. The only moves still paying ~1e-6 are (i) raising the extreme edge cells (F896/F1019, never pushed hard), (ii) structural changes to the spike pattern, and (iii) changing the *surrogate* so coherent large-scale motion becomes visible to L-BFGS — never tried via a spatially coarse-grained g. I bet on three distinct mechanisms: a geometric end-amplification ladder (test whether the toe singularity is still the limiter), a coarse-g homotopy (new objective, annealed to exact), and a global spike-density flip (thin/split every run at once, which local hops cannot reach). Each keeps the record array and returns the best exact R ever seen.

experiments.hypothesis: F896/F1019 gained +1e-6 each time they raised the outermost active cells of the record, and the amplification was only ever nudged by a few percent. If the f*f toe is still the binding constraint, the gain keeps growing with a geometric amplification factor up to some interior optimum, possibly a large one (the record is already max/mean=182, so its edge is far from singular); if the toe is exhausted, only small A is accepted and large A loses.
experiments.change: From p1149 (N=104992). Add `_amp_end(h, side, q, A)`: let s0 = first index with h>0, s1 = last; for side L take the q outermost active cells s0..s0+q-1 (for R the mirrored ones) and multiply them by A. Add `_repair(h, side, q)`: `_lbfgs_block` on window [s0-16, s0+96] (mirrored for R; both windows for B) with 80 iters beta=0 then 50 iters beta=1e7, rescale, return. Main loop for the whole budget: each round evaluate every combo (side in {L,R,B}) x (q in {1,2,3}) x (A in {1.05,1.1,1.25,1.5,2,3,5,10,30,100,1000}) applied to the current best, exact R after repair; accept only the single best improving combo, print (side,q,A,R) for each accept, repeat. Every 5 accepts run one 50-iter global `_lbfgs_all_pos`. In the last 15 s run the base's run_cycle polish, and return whichever of {best pre-polish, post-polish} has the higher exact R (p1149 showed polish can erase structure).
experiments.prediction: Target 0.941286-0.941290. The tell is an interior optimum in A with the accepted A > 2 and band01 rising above 15.05%; if only A<=1.25 is ever accepted and large A collapses, the toe is not the limiter on this construction and this line is closed.

experiments.hypothesis: Every failure so far changed the objective with an additive penalty (F915, F986, F1035, F1039) or the variables, but the exact R only 'sees' the fine comb through a landscape whose useful directions (coherent reshaping of the whole envelope/plateau) are nearly flat in the fine variables. Block-averaging the f*f knot array before computing R makes those directions first-order visible; annealing the averaging width to 1 recovers the exact problem, so the coarse stages can be traversed non-monotonically in true R.
experiments.change: From p1149. Add `_fun_grad_coarse(h, beta, w)`: same as `_fun_grad_beta` except Lf is replaced by its moving average Lb_j = mean(Lf[j-r : j+r+1]) with r = w//2 and edge clamping, used in BOTH the quadratic numerator sum(a^2+ab+b^2)/3 and the beta-softmax max term; backprop dLb -> dLf by correlating with ones(w)/w (same-shape, edge-corrected) so the existing `_backprop`/2/sum chain is unchanged. The L1 term stays exact (sum h)^2. Run ladder w = 64,32,16,8,4,2,1; at each rung `_lbfgs_all_pos` with maxiter 300 at beta=1e7 (beta=0 at w=1), ~6-7 s per rung, never reverting, printing exact R after every rung; then the base's peak-window ladder (2 rungs) and run_cycle in the remaining ~15 s. Return the best exact-R array seen at any rung or after polish, always keeping the start as a fallback.
experiments.prediction: Target 0.941287-0.941291. Tell: exact R visibly DIPS during the coarse rungs (proving the landscape really changed) and recovers above 0.941284 once w hits 1-2; if exact R just walks back to 0.941284 at every rung the surrogate is useless here.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's spike density (effective comb period) is a global design decision that no local hop can change: single split/merge hops buy only 1e-6 (F966/F981/p1092/p1113/p1149). Flipping it everywhere at once — thinning every run to one cell (doubling effective frequency), or duplicating every run into its adjacent gap — lands in a different basin whose re-optimised R can exceed the record, and only a global flip can reach it.
experiments.change: From p1149. Decompose h into maximal positive runs. Build four candidate arrays: (T1) thin all runs — replace each run by a single cell at its center index carrying the run's total mass (height = mass); (T2) thin only runs of width >= 2, leave 1-cell runs; (S1) split every run into two 1-cell copies separated by one zero cell, each carrying mass/2; (S2) duplicate — insert a copy of every run shifted by +1 cell into its adjacent zero gap, then rescale. For each candidate: seed zeros at 1e-6*mean, run a 10 s polish (global `_lbfgs_all_pos` 300 iters beta=0, one beta=1e7 pass, peak-window ladder with pad_frac 0.15/0.30, no 2x-upsample stage), print its exact R. Then take the best of the four (even if below 0.941284) and spend the remaining ~20 s hill-climbing it with the base's dip loop + run_cycle, keeping and returning the best exact-R array ever seen (including the untouched start, so the record cannot be lost).
experiments.prediction: Target 0.941285+ on at least one variant. Tell: report each variant's R right after its first polish — if T1/T2/S1 land within 1e-3 of the record and then climb past it, the comb period was wrong; if all four stay >=5e-3 below even after the full polish, spike density is settled on this hill.

info.open_why: The record p1149 is the base for all three slots; the five most recent failures on it (pedestal, toe-padding, knot-flattening, mid-band penalty, augmented Lagrangian) tell me which escape mechanisms are exhausted on this construction so I can pick genuinely different ones.

plan.analysis: H2 (0.941284) is saturated: every local polish, mask hop, continuous shift/split, coarse-resample, flat-target projection and annealing variant has returned <= +1e-6 for ~20 generations. The only mechanisms that ever bought anything on this hill targeted the *shape* of the f*f deficit ∫g(1-g): softmin on low knots (p1116, +1e-6), interior-ripple attack (p1113, +1e-6), and the flat-target projection (F1004, +1e-6). So the surplus of 1-R lives in the shoulder of g where g(0.3-0.9) is not being pushed. All three slots therefore keep the exact-R polish as the acceptor but change *what the gradient looks at* or *what resolution the spikes live at*: (1) replace the numerator ∫g^2 by ∫g^p with p<2 so low knots get relatively more weight (a preconditioner, not a new optimum); (2) halve the physical spike width by going to 2N and thinning runs, a capability the current grid does not have; (3) reweight each knot by 1/(g(1-g)) so the gradient concentrates exactly where the deficit is. Targets are +1e-6..+5e-6 because that is the scale of every real gain on this hill.

experiments.hypothesis: R = 1 - integral g(1-g)/M, and the current gradient -dq/num weights each knot by g, so knots at g~0.5 (the shoulder, where all the deficit sits) get half the pull of knots at g~1. Maximising integral g^p with p<2 weights knots by g^(p-1), which is much flatter, so the shoulder is pulled up relative to the plateau; annealing p back to 2 ends on the true objective. This is a preconditioner no program on H2 has used.
experiments.change: From p1149 (N=104992). Add `_num_dq_p(h,p)`: knots Lf as now; on each segment [a,b] length 1 compute the exact piecewise-linear integral I_j = (b^(p+1)-a^(p+1))/((p+1)*(b-a)) when |b-a|>1e-12 else a^p, and the exact adjoint contributions to a and b (differentiate I_j; for the degenerate case use the limit). Validate against finite differences on 5 random coordinates, print max rel error (must be <1e-6). Add `_fun_grad_p(h,p)`: val = -log(num_p) + 2*p*log(s) + p*log(Lm), grad = -dq_p/num_p + 2*p/s + p*(argmax one-hot backprop), reusing `_backprop`. Keep the existing clip+rescale wrapper. Run the ladder p = (1.30, 1.50, 1.70, 1.85, 2.00): at each rung do (a) a full-array L-BFGS 150 iters with `_fun_grad_p`, (b) one `_peak_window` block L-BFGS (pad_frac 0.25, extra 128) 120 iters, evaluating exact R after each and keeping the best-ever array; if exact R never moves for two consecutive rungs, jump to p=2. Spend the last 12 s on the untouched `run_cycle` with exact R and return the best exact-R array seen (never the start unless everything is worse). Print, per rung, exact R, max|h|/mean|h|, and the fraction of knots within 1% and 5% of the max.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941286-0.941289. Tell: at p=1.3-1.5 exact R first DIPS (proving the landscape really changed) while the 5%-band fraction rises above 34.6%; if the final exact-R polish lands above 0.941284, the deficit-shoulder objective is the live direction. If band fractions and R are unchanged at every rung, the shoulder is not reachable by reweighting at this resolution.

experiments.hypothesis: Every cell at N=104992 is an indivisible quantum, so the narrowest spike is 1 cell wide and the sharpest f*f transition the comb can make is fixed by that width. At 2N a thinned spike is half as wide physically, which is a capability the current grid does not have (F1042 only upsampled; F1046 thinned at the old resolution, where thinning merely coarsens). Halving spike width sharpens g's transitions and cuts the transition mass that makes up 1-R.
experiments.change: From p1161 (N=104992, 67.2% zeros). Stage A: exact 2x staircase refinement to N=209984 (h[2i]=h[2i+1]=h_old[i]); exact R must be identical to the start - assert and print the difference. Stage B: thin each maximal positive run of the ORIGINAL array to half its length: for each original run of length k at fine cells [2s, 2s+2k-1], replace it by the same total mass spread uniformly over the centered block of m=max(1,ceil(k/2)) fine cells (linear re-splat, mass preserved), leaving zeros elsewhere; print exact R right after thinning (it may drop; record it). Stage C: polish with the full modern schedule on the fine grid: exact-R full L-BFGS 250 iters, then the beta ladder (0.05/64, 0.10/64, 0.25/128, 0.40/256, 0.60/512 with beta=1e7 window polishes), then exact-R full L-BFGS 300 iters, then `_refine_knots` 200 iters - all with deadlines checked, keeping the best exact-R array. Also keep the Stage-A (unthinned) array, polish it with the same schedule for 10 s if time remains, and return whichever of the two exact-R arrays is better. Print per stage: N, zeros%, max/mean, exact R, band01/band1/band5.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941286-0.941290. Tell: R drops on thinning but the polished fine array then exceeds the unthinned fine array AND the 104992 record, with max/mean rising above 182 - that would show the binding constraint is the spike width quantum, not the comb layout. If the thinned and unthinned branches converge to the same R below the record, spike width is not the constraint and the 2N representation is dead on this hill.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact gradient weights every knot equally in the dq term, but the deficit g(1-g) is concentrated where g is near 0.5; knots near g=1 and g=0 contribute almost nothing. Reweighting the quadratic numerator by w_j = 1/(g_j(1-g_j)+delta) turns the descent into one that moves mass only where the loss actually is, which no program has done - the softmin attempt (p1116) only penalised the low knots, not the mid-band.
experiments.change: From p1149. Add `_fun_grad_w(h, delta)`: compute Lf, a=Lf[:-1], b=Lf[1:], gmid=(a+b)/2; w_j = 1/(gmid_j*(1-gmid_j)+delta) clipped to [1, 200], then num_w = sum_j w_j*(a^2+a*b+b^2)/3, and the adjoint dq_w with the same trapezoid rule but each knot pair weighted by (w_{j-1}+w_j)/2 (edge pairs use their own w); treat w as fixed during each L-BFGS call (recompute between calls). Objective val = -log(num_w) + 2*log(s) + log(Lm), grad = -dq_w/num_w + 2/s + argmax term. FD-check the gradient and print the max rel error. Loop 4 rounds with delta in (0.02, 0.005, 0.002, 0.001): each round = 200-iter full-array L-BFGS with `_fun_grad_w`, then one 150-iter peak-window block polish (pad_frac 0.25) with the same weighted gradient, then accept only if EXACT R improved; if not, tighten delta and continue. Print per round: exact R, the weighted-band mean of g, and the count of knots with 0.3<g<0.9. Spend the last 10 s on one exact-R `run_cycle` and return the best exact-R array.

If the accepted array never changes and the mid-band knot count is flat, the shoulder is already at a constrained optimum (the transition width is set by the support edges, not by interior mass), which would rule out all deficit-reweighting objectives on H2.

experiments.hypothesis: Every time the then-current H2 record was support-extended with an edge-shaped (not constant-eps) continuation and the outer windows re-polished, it bought ~1e-6 (F862, F877, F896, F1010, F1019); p1168 (0.941285) has never been extended, and its own argmax sits at a different phase (0.350) than its ancestors, so the toe shape that limits the f*f ramp is different and the move is untested on it.
experiments.change: From p1168 (N=104992). (a) Locate the active support [i0,i1] (h > 1e-6*max); print its length and the outermost 5 cell values on each side. plan.analysis: The record (p1172, 0.941285, H2, N=104992, 21% zeros, max/mean 182) has absorbed every structural move: support extension (F1056), period flips and continuous-period rasterisation (F1046, F1057), sub-cell shifts and merge/split (F1023, F1053), gradient reweighting by g^p (F1050), 2x refinement (F1052, F1059) — all ≤1e-6. What still buys 1e-6 is plain polishing plus one small change of objective or of the relaxation pattern. So I bet on three cheap, accept-if-better mechanisms that are new *as mechanisms* on this point rather than on new representations: block coordinate relaxation on disjoint windows (global L-BFGS mixes these regions and stalls), a curvature-penalized polish that directly smooths the top ripple, and a long single-restart L-BFGS test of whether the point is iteration-limited rather than landscape-limited. Each is cheap, keeps the record as fallback, and ends in exact-R polish.

experiments.hypothesis: Global L-BFGS and wide peak-window polishes all touch the whole array at once, so a gain in one region is penalised by curvature coupling elsewhere and the run stalls. Block coordinate descent over disjoint windows lets each region relax into its own local optimum; nothing on H2 has ever done a systematic sweep of windows across the entire support (earlier block polishes were only the peak window or the outer 4000 cells).
experiments.change: Keep p1172's module. Run passes (whole sweep = one pass) until 9 s remain, printing pass number, number of accepted windows and exact R at the end of each pass. Then call `run_cycle(cur, curR, deadline-0.5)` and a final 4 s tight peak-window block polish (pad_frac 0.10, extra 128, beta=0). Return the best exact-R array seen, never a worse one.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941286-0.941287. Tell: per pass, at least 2-3 windows are accepted with deltas ~1e-7 and the cumulative delta over two passes exceeds 1e-6. If every window is rejected in pass 1, disjoint-window relaxation is already converged at this resolution and only global/structural moves remain.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's g=f*f has only 15.1% of knots within 0.1% of the max: the top is a rippled plateau, and every objective variant tried (softmax, top-band mass, softmin, g^p) reweights knots without ever penalising *ripple*. Penalising the discrete curvature of g on the plateau directly flattens the top, and annealing the penalty to zero ends on the true objective with a strictly better num.

Add `_fun_grad_curv(h, lam)`: same num/dq/argmax as `_fun_grad`, but gLf = -dq/num + onehot(1/Lm) + lam*gP/(Lm*Lm) and val = -log(num) + 2*log(s) + log(Lm) + lam*P/(Lm*Lm). Validate the adjoint against finite differences on 5 random coordinates and print max rel error (<1e-6 required). Add a variant of `_lbfgs_all_pos`/`_lbfgs_block` that takes this fg. Ladder lam = (3, 1, 0.3, 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0): at each rung run 150-iter full-array L-BFGS with the curvature objective, then one 80-iter peak-window block polish (pad_frac 0.25, extra 128) with the same objective, evaluate exact R after each and keep the best-ever array; print exact R and band01/band1 fractions per rung. Spend the last 15 s in `run_cycle` on the best exact-R array.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941286-0.941288. Tell: during lam=1..0.1 the band1 fraction rises above 28.2% (start 27.97%) while exact R stays within 1e-5 of the start; after the exact-R cycle, exceeding 0.9412855 means curvature regularization is the live direction. If band1 never exceeds 28.1% at any lam, the plateau ripple cannot be smoothed at fixed N.

plan.analysis: p1180 is a new H2 point (34.7% zeros, argmax 0.532) where exact-R long L-BFGS, window sweeps, support extension, and density flips are saturated. The real deficit is still the plateau: only 27.97% of knots lie within 1% of max. I am betting on porting two mechanisms that won on other H2-family constructions to p1180 (p1177's interior knot-level beta continuation and p1149's continuous split of top runs), plus one new objective: a hard upper hinge that flattens the top tail without the single-argmax gradient. All target +1e-6 to +3e-6.

experiments.hypothesis: p1177's knot-level beta-continuation raised R by 2e-6 on p1128 by flattening f*f through a beta-softmax ramp over interior heights; p1180's own run_cycle only beta-polishes the peak window, so its shoulders never see a soft-max pressure.

experiments.hypothesis: The exact-R gradient is dominated by one argmax knot, so L-BFGS never pays to flatten the top tail (only 27.97% of knots within 1% of max). For cap = max_knot * [0.9995, 0.998, 0.995, 0.990] and lam = [1e3, 1e4], run 120 L-BFGS iterations from the current best with nonnegativity clipping (no rescale during the capped phase), evaluate exact R, then run 120 exact-R peak-window L-BFGS iterations and keep the best exact-R array. plan.analysis: H2 at 0.941286 is saturated: long un-restarted L-BFGS (F1064), interior beta-continuation (F1068), hinge caps (F1070), fractional splits (F1069), mass-exact 2x upsample (F1073), coarse resample and curvature/band penalties (F986/F915/F1063) all moved R by <1e-6 on p1172/p1180. The record's g is effectively a trapezoid with ~15% total ramp fraction (15.06% of knots within 0.1% of max): R=(1-4b/3)/(1-b) at b=0.1498 gives 0.941286, so the only way to gain is to add degrees of freedom that sharpen the toe/tail or free the grid phase. Three untried concrete levers on this basin: (1) a non-commensurate conservative resample (factor 1.2486) which breaks the 2x staircase and inserts genuinely new boundary-mixed cells (F1073's exact 2x factor preserves the staircase exactly, so it tested nothing); (2) cell-scale toe reshaping (pad 4-32 cells, tau 0.5-4 cells) - F1056 only tested pad=4000 with tau 150-2500, i.e. broad shelves, not sharpening; (3) a continuous-position K-bump re-parametrisation which frees every spike position at once, unlike the per-run sub-cell moves of F1023/F1069.

experiments.hypothesis: The record (and its ancestors) is an exact 2x staircase, so every cell-level degree of freedom is duplicated and the whole shape is phase-locked to the N=104992 grid. F1073's 'mass-exact 2x upsample' to 209984 reproduced the staircase exactly and therefore added no new freedom; a NON-commensurate conservative resample (factor 1.2486) splits old cells unevenly, creating new intermediate heights at every old cell boundary, including the toe/tail cells that set g's 15% ramp. If the ramp is limited by grid phase rather than by the shape itself, these new cells buy R; if not, this is a clean negative answer.

Take start h (N=104992), build ht = _conservative_resample(h, 131072), rescale with _rescale (weights unchanged by V so R must be preserved), print R_of(h) vs R_of(ht) (expect equal to ~1e-6; abort and fall back to M=131072 cumulative-mass splat if the drop exceeds 1e-4). experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941287-0.941288. experiments.hypothesis: g's 15% ramp is the whole loss (R=(1-4b/3)/(1-b) at b=0.15 gives exactly 0.9413), and the ramp slope is set by the outermost active cells of f. (b) Build candidates per side independently: for side in {left,right}, for pad in {4,8,16,32}, for a in {0.5,1.0,2.0}, for tau in {0.5,0.75,1.0,2.0,4.0} (decay in cells, k=1..pad): pad_vals = a*h_edge*exp(-k/tau) (and one increasing variant a*h_edge*(1+k/pad)); prepend/append with _rescale, evaluate R_of (no polishing yet) - 2*4*3*6 = 144 cheap FFT evaluations. (d) Finish with the base run_cycle on the best array and a final tight peak-window polish; always return the best exact-R array seen, and keep going until deadline-0.5.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941287-0.941288. Tell: the pre-polish R of the winning toe is within 1e-6 of the start and the outer-1200 polish then beats the start (that is the F896 mechanism), and the printed winner shows whether the toe wants a short decay (tau ~1 cell, sharpening) or none at all.
