So two mechanisms each bought +1e-6 at gen 373 and they have never been compounded on the *new* record — F1258 showed compounding two same-value mechanisms does pay. Iterated blur (F1324) and the stride-16/8/4/2 cascade (F1327) are dead on this construction, so I avoid both. I bet on (i) compounding the two winning perturbation families, (ii) the 3:2 non-commensurate half-quotient lift (F1295/F1308, different from the failed cascade) on the 0.941438 state, and (iii) one genuinely new structural move: local support re-selection near the f*f argmax, which the frozen zero pattern (F1431) has locked out.

experiments.hypothesis: Two independent mechanisms each reached 0.941438 at gen 373: the block-multiplicative jitter sweep (F1246, p1484) and the high-beta sharpening ladder (F1326, p1483). F1258 showed that compounding two mechanisms which each stall at the same value yields a further gain. Neither has been applied on top of the other on the p1483 state.
experiments.change: Start from p1483. Loop until deadline-5.0 (max 3 rounds): (a) jitter arm — take idx=flatnonzero(best>0), split into ~max(1,nz/100) contiguous blocks, multiply each block by exp(sigma*u) with sigma drawn from {0.005,0.01,0.02} and u~N(0,1), clip>=0, _rescale, then _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,0.0), iters=250) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06,0.04), iters=300); (b) sharp arm — _polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,1e9,1e10,0.0), iters=350). Accept each arm only if R_of(cand) > bestR+1e-14, and always apply the next arm to the accepted best. Finish with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,0.0), iters=300) using remaining time.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941440-0.941443. Tell: at least one accepted jitter arm AND one accepted sharp arm on the 0.941438 state (not just at the first round); if only the first round's arm is accepted, the gains are not additive and the mechanism is one-shot per state.

experiments.hypothesis: The stride-16/8/4/2 quotient cascade is dead on p1477 (F1327), but the 3:2 non-commensurate lift built from the polished HALF-quotient gained on p1448/p1453 (F1295, F1307) and the odd/even rotation gained separately (F1308). That specific lift has never been run on the 0.941438 record.
experiments.change: Start from p1483. Loop until deadline-6.0 (max 3 cycles): c = best[0::2] (half-quotient, N/2). Polish c with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e6,1e7,0.0), iters=250) then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.15,0.10), iters=250). Build L=3*len(c) with fresh log-normal sub-cell weights (each c-cell split into 3 subcells with weights exp(0.25*N(0,1)) normalized to preserve mass), rescale, _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,1e8,0.0), iters=250) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06), iters=250), then fold back to N by cumulative-mass resampling (odd/even alternating on successive cycles: even fold takes cells (2i,2i+1) from quotient i, odd fold shifts by one cell so results land on cells (2i+1,2i+2)). Accept the folded array only if R_of > bestR+1e-14; otherwise keep best. Spend the last ~8 s on _polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,1e9,0.0), iters=300) plus a final _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=300).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941440-0.941442. Tell: an accepted lift on cycle 1 or 2, and whether the accepted lift is the even or odd fold (phase sensitivity, as F1308/F1223 predict). If every folded array loses R, the 3:2 lift is saturated on this state, unlike on p1448.

experiments.hypothesis: All jitter/blur/lift moves on this line mutate only active cells or blur the whole array, so the 67.7% exact-zero pattern is frozen (F1431). F1277 showed sparse re-selection (fill zeros, re-prune) can gain, but only as random index-space noise. A targeted version — freeing a bounded window around the f*f argmax INCLUDING its zeros — has never been tried and lets the solver choose which cells inside that window carry mass.
experiments.change: Start from p1483. Compute the f*f argmax knot index m from _knots(best); map to cell window win = [max(0,m//2-400), min(N-1, m//2+400)] (400 cells each side, includes zeros and actives). Run _lbfgs_block(best, win, 400, deadline-20, beta=1e8), then beta=1e7, then beta=0.0, each accepted only on R improvement, with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,0.0), iters=250) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06), iters=250) after each acceptance. Then prune: set any window entry below 1e-4*mean(best[best>0]) to exactly zero, _rescale, and re-polish. Repeat the whole window-free-optimise-prune step with progressively wider windows (800, 1600 cells each side) while time > deadline-6.0. Finish with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,0.0), iters=300) plus _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=300).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941439-0.941442. Tell: whether the accepted state's zero fraction moves off 67.7% (support re-selection actually happened) and whether the f*f argmax shifts from 0.214; if R rises with zero fraction unchanged, the gain is pure polish, not re-selection.

info.open_why: See the exact code and mechanism of the current record and its parent, plus the smoothing/jitter findings that produced the recent +1e-6 gains, so I can pick a genuinely different structural move rather than repeat a failed one.

plan.analysis: H2 is at 0.941438 and every in-place perturbation family tried on p1483 is saturated: compounded jitter+high-beta sharpening (F1330), 3:2 lift cascade (F1331), argmax window optimise-prune (F1332, +1e-6 only), quotient cascade 16/8/4/2 (F1327). What still pays on this line, generation after generation, is a change of grid structure followed by re-polish (F1283, F1300, F1294, F1308 all +2-4e-6), and the current base only ever uses stride 2. So slot 1 bets on a multi-stride (3/4/5/2) quotient cascade with a portfolio of fresh split weights. Slot 2 re-uses the only mechanism that moved the ball at gen 374 (window optimise-prune, p1491 +1e-6) but aimed at the near-max deficit band instead of the argmax. Slot 3 tests an untested assumption: every lift so far is folded back to N; since an exact repeat preserves R exactly, the finer array can be kept and any fine-grid gain retained.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is a ~3-periodic spiky comb, yet every lift on this base uses stride 2 only. Folding to a stride-3/4/5 quotient (which is closer to the comb's true period), polishing that coarse problem to a good optimum, and lifting back with several fresh random split-weight draws should expose new sub-cell degrees of freedom that the saturated stride-2 path cannot reach. F1283/F1294/F1307 show the lift-with-fresh-weights mechanism is the only structural move still paying; the base never uses it at strides other than 2.
experiments.change: Start from p1483. Loop until deadline-6.0 over strides k = (3,4,2,5). For each k: m = best.size//k; c = best[:m*k].reshape(m,k).mean(axis=1) (mass-preserving k-fold quotient). Polish c with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e6,1e7,0.0), iters=250) then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.15,0.10), iters=250). Build 4 lift candidates: w = exp(sigma*randn(m,k)) row-normalised to sum 1, with sigma in {0.1,0.3,0.6} plus a deterministic uniform w; h_new[i*k+j] = k*c[i]*w[i,j]. Polish each with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e6,1e7,1e8,0.0), iters=250) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06), iters=200); keep the best candidate and accept it only if R improves. If a stride's quotient polish itself improves R(c) but no lift is accepted, still continue to the next stride. Leave the base's Phase A/B and final polish phases intact, running them on the accepted best at the end.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941440-0.941442. Tell: at least one stride yields an accepted lift, and the accepted one is stride 3 or 5 rather than 2 (which would confirm the period-3 structure hypothesis); the accepted state's R moves above 0.9414390, i.e. +2e-6 or more over 0.9414385.

experiments.hypothesis: p1491's +1e-6 came from freeing a window around the f*f argmax and re-pruning. But the deficit R is 1 - int g(M-g)/(M int g): it lives where g is between roughly 0.4M and 0.9M, not at the argmax. Freeing the cells that produce the near-max band (and allowing their zeros to revive) targets the actual loss term instead of the already-tight peak.
experiments.change: Start from p1491. Loop until deadline-6.0 (max 4 rounds). Compute g = _knots(best), M = g.max(). Find knot indices with 0.35*M <= g <= 0.90*M, take the largest contiguous run [ka,kb]. Map to cells lo = max(0, ka//2 - 150), hi = min(N-1, kb//2 + 150). Run _lbfgs_block(best, np.arange(lo,hi+1), 400, beta=1e8), then beta=1e7, then beta=0, at the same window. After each beta, prune h[lo:hi+1] below 1e-4*(mean of active heights in the window), then _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,0.0), iters=200). Accept the round only if R improves; on acceptance also run a short _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06), iters=150). Alternate rounds between the lower band (0.35-0.65 M) and the upper band (0.65-0.90 M). Keep the base's other phases and finish with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,0.0), iters=250).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941439-0.941441. Tell: R exceeds 0.9414385 by >=1e-6 AND the printed near-max share (fraction of f*f knots within 5% of max) rises above 34.67%, or the zero fraction shifts locally in the band window (support re-selection happened). A flat result means the deficit band is already saturated by this window mechanism.

experiments.hypothesis: Every lift on this line (including the exact np.repeat(2) one in the base) is folded back to N, throwing away the finer parametrisation. An exact 2x repeat reproduces the same continuous f, hence exactly the same R, so the fine array is a free starting point with strictly more degrees of freedom; optimising in it and RETURNING it (never folding back) can add R that the fold-back discards. F1335 tested a 2x upsample-refine but kept the coarse array as the result.
experiments.change: Start from p1483. h2 = np.repeat(best, 2) (verify R(h2) == R(best) to 1e-12). Keep h2 as a candidate, never fold it back. Loop until deadline-5.0 (max 2 rounds): (a) window polish on h2: free fine cells in [2*m//2 - 900, 2*m//2 + 900] where m is the coarse argmax knot index, run _lbfgs_block(h2, win, 400, beta=1e8), then beta=1e7, then 0; (b) _polish_ladder(h2, betas=(1e7,1e8,0.0), iters=250) and _peak_ladder(h2, pads=(0.10,0.06), iters=200); keep h2 if R(h2) > R(best)+1e-9. If time remains after a full round, also try h3 = np.repeat(best,3) with one _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,0.0), iters=200) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06), iters=150) pass, and keep it if better. Return whichever array (coarse p1483 state, 2x or 3x) has the highest exact R.
experiments.prediction: Aim >=0.941439 with N around 210k (or 315k). Tell: the returned array has N > 104992 AND its R is at least 1e-6 above 0.941438; if the fine array's R is exactly 0.941438 the conclusion is that the extra resolution carries no exploitable freedom and future generations should stay at N=104992.

info.open_why: The record p1483 and the two winning mechanisms (high-beta sharpening F1326, block jitter F1246) plus the failed compounding attempt F1330 and the blur escape F1318/F1258 tell me which perturbation families still pay and how to combine them without repeating the failed compounding.

plan.analysis: H2 (the 3-periodic comb, N=104992, 67.8% zeros, f*f argmax at 0.204) is a saturated but still-permeable hill: every recent gain is +1e-6..+6e-6 and comes from compounding a lift/quotient or edge move, never from a single pass. Three things have not been re-tested at the 0.941439 level: (i) a warm-started compound quotient chain (previous chains restarted the quotient from scratch each round, and p1497 wastes its last ~6 s on the deficit-band phase that F1337 showed is dead); (ii) end/edge shaping of the support (all recent window work aimed at the argmax or the 0.35-0.9 M band, never at the two support toes, which set where g crosses M/2); (iii) a lean, lift-free schedule that spends nearly the whole 60 s in beta-ladder + tightening peak-window L-BFGS, the recipe that bought +8e-6 on the neighbouring p1039 basin (F1340). I bet on +2e-6 to +5e-6 total across these.

experiments.hypothesis: p1497's quotient phase restarts c=best[0::2] cold every round and its last 6 s go to the deficit-band phase that F1337 proved dead on this construction. Carrying the polished quotient across rounds (warm start) and lifting with fresh random sub-cell weights compounds the proven stride-2/stride-4 lift gains (F1300/F1306/F1307) instead of re-paying for the same polish each round.
experiments.change: Start from p1497. Delete the Phase C band rounds entirely (keep only Phases A, B and the final ladders). Replace Phase A with a warm-started chain running until cpu > deadline-8: (1) maintain c, initially best[0::2], and cR; polish c with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e6,1e7),iters=300) then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.20,0.12,0.08),iters=250), keeping c if R(c) improves; (2) lift: build hL = _rescale(np.repeat(c,2) * w) where w is a fresh log-normal array (sigma=0.25) randomised per round, then _polish_ladder(hL, betas=(1e7,0.0), iters=250) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=200); accept into best only if R improves; (3) every third round instead fold with stride 4 (c4 = best[:m*4].reshape(m,4).mean(axis=1)), polish c4, lift with 4 random log-normal sub-weights, polish, accept on improvement; (4) after any acceptance, re-seed c from the new best[0::2]. Finish with _polish_ladder((1e8,0.0)) + _peak_ladder((0.06,0.04)).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941441-0.941444. Tell: at least 2 accepted lift rounds after the first (logged as NEW BEST with origin 'lift'); if the same 0.941439 is hit within 2 rounds and never moves, the quotient route is exhausted and only the edge route (slot 2) remains.

experiments.hypothesis: R = 1 - int g(M-g)/(M int g); g(M-g) peaks at g=M/2, i.e. on the two f*f ramps whose slope is set by the outermost active cells of h. Every recent window move targeted the argmax or the 0.35-0.9 M band (F1332/F1337, both dead); the support toes themselves have not been re-optimised since the 0.94127 level (F1019/F1243/F1248 gave +1e-6 each). Freeing the toe windows *including their zeros* lets the solver decide how many cells carry mass there, which is exactly the quantity that sets the ramp slope.
experiments.change: Start from p1497. Loop until cpu > deadline-6 (max 6 rounds, alternating ends): for end L use win = arange(0,300), for end R win = arange(N-300,N); run _lbfgs_block(best, win, 400, deadline-3, beta=1e6), then beta=1e7, then beta=0.0, each accepted only on R improvement and each followed by _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,0.0),iters=200); then prune (set win entries < 1e-4*mean(best[best>0]) to 0), _rescale, re-polish, accept on improvement. info.open_why: p1491 is the direct base of the record and its window-free-optimise-prune move is the only recent mechanism still buying gains; F1332/F1337/F1341 show which window variants failed on this construction, and F1279 explains why many Phase-3 edits land on identical scores.

plan.analysis: Gen 376 closed off every local-polish route on H2 (p1502/p1497 comb, 0.941439): warm quotient chains (F1342), deficit-band windows (F1337), toe windows+extension (F1343) and the lean beta ladder (F1344) all returned the start unchanged, and near-max shares are frozen at 16.50/28.09/34.67. The only mechanism that has paid since gen 349 is a structural lift off the half-quotient (2x, 3:2, stride cascades, rotation) at ~2-5e-6 per accepted round. So I bet on three untested structural/algorithmic levers rather than more of the same polish: (1) a never-tried 5:4 non-commensurate lift from the polished half-quotient, (2) a systematic fold-back portfolio for the proven 3:2 lift — the projection back to N has always been a single, unexamined mass-resample — and (3) a D3 flip: accelerated projected gradient on the exact gradient, since L-BFGS's limited-memory quadratic model may be flattening the search.

experiments.hypothesis: Every lift on this line used ratio 2, 3:2 or a stride quotient; 3:2 is now saturated after repeated use, but a 5:4 non-commensurate lift changes the aliasing between the fine grid and the ~3-periodic spike comb, and the optimizer at the finer grid can then express a strictly different continuous shape. The half-quotient polish (F1180) plus a fresh random sub-cell weighting is what made every earlier lift pay (F1284/F1288/F1295), so keep that and only change the ratio to 5:4.
experiments.change: Start from p1502. Keep its Phase A half-quotient polish and Phase B sharpening, but delete the dead Phase C toe rounds. Replace with a loop until cpu > deadline-6 (max 4 rounds): (a) c = best[0::2]; polish c with beta ladder (1e6,1e7) and peak windows pads (0.15,0.10,0.06) for at most 6 s; (b) L = (5*c.size)//2; build the fine array by sampling the step function c at L cell centres mapped through cumulative mass, multiplied by per-fine-cell log-normal weights (sigma=0.45, clipped 0.2-5); (c) polish at L with beta (1e5,1e6,1e7,0) using _lbfgs_all_pos and peak windows pads (0.12,0.08,0.05); (d) fold back to m=c.size by binning the fine masses into m equal bins with cumulative-mass resampling, polish at m (beta 1e6,1e7,0); (e) expand m->N=2m with fresh random interlaced weights, polish at N (beta 1e7, 0, peak pads 0.08,0.05) and accept only if R_of beats the running best by >1e-14; log the ratio of accepted rounds. Finish with _polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,0,), iters=250).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941442-0.941445. Tell: at least one accepted lift round after the first (logged NEW BEST with tag 'lift54'), and the accepted R after fold-back to N strictly above 0.9414395; if every round is rejected, the 5:4 aliasing is absorbed just like the earlier 2x/3:2 lifts were.

experiments.hypothesis: The 3:2 lift works repeatedly, but every version folds the polished fine array back to N with one fixed rule (mass binning). That projection is the only unexamined step in the lift cycle: averaging/argmax/phase-shifted fold-backs produce different points at resolution N, and polishing each before choosing gives several distinct candidates per lift for the cost of one FFT polish. F1307 showed a portfolio on the lift side helps; the fold side has never been sampled.
experiments.change: Start from p1497. Keep Phases A and B. Replace Phase C (deficit-band) with: loop until cpu > deadline-6 (max 5 rounds): c = best[0::2]; polish c briefly (beta 1e6,1e7, peak pads 0.15,0.10); m=c.size, L=3*m//2. For each of two lift weightings (w_a: per-subcell log-normal sigma=0.5; w_b: Dirichlet(1) random triples normalised) build the fine array at L by distributing each c[i] over 3 consecutive fine cells, polish at L with _lbfgs_all_pos(beta in (1e6,1e7)) and one peak window (pad 0.08). For each polished fine array, produce three fold-backs to m: (i) cumulative-mass binning into m equal bins, (ii) plain sum of each group of 3, (iii) group sum with the middle subcell up-weighted by 1.5 and renormalised to the same total; polish each m-array (beta 1e6,1e7,1e5) for at most 3 s and record R at level m. Take the single best m-array, expand to N=2m with fresh random interlaced weights, polish at N (beta 1e7,0, peak pads 0.08,0.05), accept only on R improvement, and print which fold rule (i/ii/iii) won each round.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941441-0.941443. Tell: distinct fold rules win different rounds (i.e. the fold is not neutral) and at least one round is accepted with R(N) > 0.9414395; if the same rule always wins and no round is accepted, the fold is confirmed neutral and the 3:2 cycle is exhausted at this resolution.

experiments.hypothesis: Every hill in the map uses L-BFGS-B, whose limited-memory quadratic model stalls on this exact objective; F1224 and F0823 both note that the exact-R gradient is dominated by one argmax knot, so a first-order model is nearly flat in the directions that matter. An accelerated projected gradient (FISTA with Barzilai-Borwein steps and restarts) takes long, flat, correlated steps that L-BFGS cannot represent with 10 stored pairs, which is exactly the regime the record sits in.
experiments.change: Start from p1502. Keep Phases A and B, delete the Phase C toe rounds. Add a phase: run _fista_exact(best, slice_deadline) for ~22 s where _fista_exact is a projected accelerated gradient on the exact objective val(h) = -log(num)+2log(s)+log(Lmax) with the existing analytic gradient (_fun_grad), nonnegativity by clipping: y = x + momentum*(x - x_prev) with momentum 0.9, restarted to 0 whenever val increases; step t from Barzilai-Borwein (s.y/s.s) clipped to [1e-8, 1e2], with one backtracking halving if val(clip(y - t g)) > val(y); estimate the initial t as 1e2*||h||/||g|| at the start. Every 100 iterations evaluate R_of(clip(x)) and offer it (tags 'fista'), keeping the best; the phase must stop at its slice deadline, not before. Then spend all remaining time on _polish_ladder(betas=(1e7,1e6,0)) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06,0.04)) on the best-so-far.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941440-0.941442 from the FISTA phase alone (before polish). plan.analysis: The record 0.941440 is now locked to the N=104992 lattice: F1279/F1315/F1187 show orthogonal edits reproduce identical R, and the only moves still paying (~1e-6 each) are lattice-changing ones — non-commensurate lifts (F1284/F1295/F1300/F1308), dilation (F1280), interlacing (F1213). 3:2, 5:4, fold-rule portfolios, FISTA, doubling and basin-hopping have all now failed on this construction (F1348-F1352), so the lift-ratio family is saturated. Untried lattice knobs are (a) the sub-step phase of the grid itself and (b) small N changes, neither of which any program has used. On T25's H14 (0.871436) the basin is smooth (max/mean 3.95, 7.3% zeros); it has never been pushed toward the spiky regime that H2 occupies.

experiments.hypothesis: Every move so far changes cell *widths/content* (lifts, quotients, dilation) but never the alignment of the grid with the ~3-periodic comb's spike train. Resampling the same shape at a half/third-step offset gives a genuinely different discrete lattice (hence a different R), and polishing it on that lattice can land on a slightly better discretisation of the same continuous shape.

plan.analysis: The record is pinned at 0.941440 on H2, a spiky ~3-periodic comb (N=104992, 67.5% zeros, max/mean 183.5). The only mechanism still paying on this hill is the lift family: half-quotient polish then non-commensurate/commensurate upsample with fresh sub-cell weights, polish, fold back, accept (F1180, F1284, F1288, F1295, F1300, F1306, F1308) — each generation bought +1e-6 to +4e-6. Everything else is dead on this construction: grid-shift resampling (F1354), N perturbation (F1355), off-peak freeing (F1360), log-space active set (F1361), structural split/merge (F1364), 5:4 lift (F1348), resolution doubling (F1352). So I bet on three distinct lift variants not yet tried on p1522, each replacing the dead log-space Phase C: a 7:4 lift, a 3x interlaced lift with optimized per-phase weights, and a budget-rebalanced deep half-quotient plus one long 3:2 lift polish.

plan.analysis: The record is saturated: window, band, pool, log-space, argmax-keyed and quotient-starving moves all return 0.941441. F1180's quotient lift remains the only reliable engine, but only when unhindered. Rather than repeat those, I bet on (i) selecting the free set for H2 by the backprojected sensitivity of the loss integrand g(M-g), which reaches mid-level knots no beta-softmax gradient sees; (ii) on L3, the record chain's randomized asymmetric 2N split (F1410), never tried on that smooth basin; and (iii) a genuinely new hill from D8's untried random sparse spike train, escalated with the record's lift and beta-sharpening chain. Slot 1 aims at +2-4e-6 on the record; slots 2-3 are explorations judged against their own tracks.

experiments.hypothesis: The remaining deficit is the integral of g(M-g)/(M*int g), whose integrand is largest at mid-level knots (g near M/2) that beta<=1e7 softmax gradients cannot see. Choosing the free set by the convolution-backprojected sensitivity of that deficit finds cells whose perturbation most changes mid-level knots, wherever they sit, so a block L-BFGS on exact R can attack the loss where it actually lives.

plan.analysis: H2 is saturated under every window/block/free-set selector tried at N=104992 (F1384, F1385, F1390, F1376, F1378 all returned the start). The only move that has repeatedly bought >1e-6 on this line is a change of effective resolution (gen 349-352: +5e-5 from the quotient/lift discoveries; F1213, F1391, F429). Since the record's N=104992 is (per p0920/p0929) a 2x staircase, its true step-function resolution is ~52496; the lifts keep folding back to the same grid, so no program has ever *returned* an array at a genuinely finer effective resolution. Second, every optimizer on this hill is L-BFGS-B, whose limited-memory curvature is stale in this flat valley (F1224); a real Newton-CG with FFT Hessian-vector products has never been run. Third, every escape perturbation has been multiplicative or window-local (F539, F1431); mass-conserving transport dithering is untried. I bet on these three.

experiments.hypothesis: The record is an exact 2x staircase, so R is exactly invariant under the repeat and the search has effectively only been running at half resolution: every 'lift' so far (F1180, F1213, F1344, F1391, F1508) folds back to N=104992, throwing the finer degrees of freedom away. Breaking the staircase with a randomized asymmetric split and *keeping* the finer array, then polishing there, is the one lever that historically paid big on this basin (gen 349-352) and on L3 (F1391: +7e-5).
experiments.change: Start from p1554's code, keep all helpers. Add `_asym_split(h, sigma, rng, phase='even')`: n=h.size; w0=exp(sigma*rng.standard_normal(n)); w1=exp(sigma*rng.standard_normal(n)); w0/= (w0+w1)/2; w1/=(w0+w1)/2; out=empty(2n); out[0::2]=h*w0; out[1::2]=h*w1 (mass-preserving, mean weight 1). Also add `_shift_split(h)`: out[0::2]=0.5*h, out[1::2]=0.5*h but with the odd array rolled by one cell (0.5*(h + roll(h,1))) so mass sits on cell boundaries — a genuinely different function. Main body: from `best=p1554`, build three candidates c1=_asym_split(best,0.6), c2=_asym_split(best,0.25), c3=_shift_split(best), each 2N=209984; rescale, then for each: `_polish_ladder(cand, betas=(1e5,1e6,1e7,0.0), iters=200)` and `_peak_ladder(cand, pads=(0.20,0.12,0.08,0.05), iters=250)` (both already in the base file, they work at any N). Track the best by R_of (R is comparable across N). Then take the winner and, if time remains, split it once more to 419968 with sigma=0.3 plus the same ladder. Also keep a deterministic duplicate (=staircase, same R) as a control. Final 8 s: `_polish_ladder(best, betas=(1e7,1e8,1e9,0.0), iters=300)` + `_peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=250)` on whatever array is currently best, and return it (the returned N may be 209984 or 419968 — that is allowed, ≤1e6). Print after each stage: N, R, and the 0.1%/1%/5%-of-max knot shares. Use deadline=0.90*budget and check process_time before every phase.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.94145-0.94147 (≥ +1e-5 over 0.941441). Tell: the fine-grid candidate beats its staircase parent by >1e-6 already after the first split+polish, the returned N is 209984 or 419968, and the 1%/5%-of-max knot shares rise above 28.10%/34.67% (the shoulders steepen because the finer grid can resolve the ramp). If every fine candidate comes back below the parent by more than 1e-8, the effective-resolution lever is exhausted at 52496 and the discrete profile is converged.

experiments.hypothesis: Every program on every hill uses L-BFGS-B, whose two-loop recursion keeps only 10 stale curvature pairs; in this very flat valley its steps are essentially preconditioned steepest descent and it stalls (F1224, F1220, F1033). The exact objective -log R = -log num + 2 log s + log M has a cheap closed-form Hessian and Hessian-vector product (two extra FFT convolutions), so a Newton-CG can take genuinely second-order steps and escape where L-BFGS declares convergence.
experiments.change: Start from p1554's code, keep _num_and_dq/_backprop/_knots. Fix the argmax m between Newton steps. Add `_hv(v, h, m)`: (1) w1=2*conv(h,v) (length 2n-1); K1=_dq_of(w1) where _dq_of(Lv) applies the same (2a+b)/3 shift-add rule to any vector; Hnum_v = _backprop(K, v) + _backprop(K1, h) with K=dq (the existing factor-2 convention handles both convolution orders); (2) gnum=_backprop(K,h); (3) u = vector length n with u[i]=2*h[m-i] for 0<=m-i<n else 0; rev_m(v)[i]=2*v[m-i] likewise; (4) Hv = -Hnum_v/num + gnum*(gnum@v)/num**2 - (2/s**2)*(v.sum())*ones + rev_m(v)/M - u*(u@v)/M**2. Grad is the existing `_fun_grad` gradient at fixed m. Add `_ncg(h, iters_newton, deadline)`: each step, solve H p = -g with CG capped at 20 iterations, abort to p=-g*(0.01*max(h)/||g||_inf) if p@(Hp) <= 0 or ||p||_inf > 0.05*max(h); Armijo backtracking (t=1, halve up to 8 times) accepting only if both -log R decreases and R_of increases; after every accepted step recompute m=argmax(_knots(h)) and, every 4th step, run `_peak_ladder(h, pads=(0.08,0.05), iters=150)`. Schedule: 60% of the budget full-array Newton, 30% Newton restricted to a peak window (embed v on the window, project the HVP result back to the window — same `_hv`), final 10% `_polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,1e9,1e10,0.0), iters=300)` + `_peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04))`. Wrap every Newton block in try/except and fall back to the base's L-BFGS ladder on failure. Print per Newton step: F, R, ||g||_inf, CG iterations, step length, negative-curvature flag. deadline=0.90*budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941444-0.941450. Tell: ||g||_inf falls by ≥2 orders of magnitude within ~15 Newton steps (L-BFGS leaves it flat), the step length stays O(1e-3..1e-2)*max(h), and at least one 'NEW BEST' line is printed directly after a Newton step rather than after a polish ladder. If >80% of steps report negative curvature on the first CG iteration, that is itself the answer: the plateau is a saddle-flat region and the deficit is not gradient-reachable at this N.

experiments.hypothesis: Every escape perturbation on H2 lineage has been multiplicative (envelopes, log-normal jitter, Gaussian blur — F539, F1246, F1318, F1491) or window-local, i.e. positive and mass-changing; none has ever moved mass *between adjacent cells* at fixed total mass and fixed support. Adjacent-pair transport is orthogonal to that whole family: it changes the sub-cell phase/centre-of-mass pattern that the multiplicative moves leave invariant, and the record's deficit is exactly a ramp-shape (position) problem, not a scale problem.
experiments.change: Start from p1554's code, delete the deficit phase. Add `_transport(h, rng, amp, kind)`: (a) kind='pair': choose K=max(1,int(0.01*count_nonzero)) random indices i among active cells, d=amp*h[i]*rng.standard_normal(K), then h[i]-=d and h[i+1]+=d (or h[i-1] if i is the last cell), clip at 0; (b) kind='walk': pick one contiguous band of width int(0.1*N) at a random offset, build a zero-mean cumulative-sum random walk w (w=cumsum(randn(w))) and set h[band]+= amp*h[band]*w/ (|w|.max()+1e-12), clip; then _rescale. On every third cycle also run one 3:2 interlace lift (existing `_interlace_32` with fresh log-normal weights 0.02 at 1.5N), polish at 1.5N with betas=(1e7,0.0), fold back with `_fold_back`, then `_peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04))`. Accept-only: keep ht only if R_of(ht) > R_of(best)+1e-14, else restore; print R and cycle number each time. Finish with `_polish_ladder(betas=(1e8,1e9,1e10,0.0), iters=300)` + `_peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=250)` and return best. deadline=0.92*budget.

info.open_why: See the exact code/plan of the current record's immediate ancestors and the three most recent failed escape attempts on the record construction, so the next experiments differ concretely rather than repeating.

plan.analysis: The record (p1554, 0.941441) is saturated against single-shot moves: Newton-CG (F1397), transport dithering (F1398), asymmetric 2N/4N splits (F1396), deficit/shoulder free sets (F1385, F1390) and noise ES (F1399) all returned the start exactly. What still pays on H2 is resolution work: coarse-quotient polish and lift cycles (F1180: +7e-5 best; F1313: +23e-6 from fixing a starved half-res phase; F1437/F1453: 3:2 non-commensurate lifts +2..3e-6; F1401: +2e-6). The base spends only 15% of budget at half resolution, and every 3:2 lift so far was built from the even quotient. I bet on three variants of that lever: odd-quotient+3:2 lift, higher-ratio lifts, and a budget-rewritten half-resolution portfolio.

experiments.hypothesis: The 3:2 non-commensurate lift (+3e-6 on p1437, +2e-6 on p1453) and the stride-quotient cascade (+2e-6 on p1457) were each run only on the EVEN quotient h[0::2] (F1464 explicitly notes the cascade folds only the even quotient; F1533/F1534 use the even half-quotient). info.open_why: The record p1554 and its two most recent escape attempts (deficit-sensitivity F1390, transport F1398, asymmetric split F1396, Newton F1397) all failed on it; seeing their exact code and results tells me which structural moves are genuinely untried on the record construction.

plan.analysis: H2 is saturated: 68% zeros, max/mean 183.6, argmax oscillating 0.20-0.44 with identical f*f shares, and the last two generations produced only null results (odd 3:2 lift, 5:2/7:3/4:3 lifts, 62% half-res budget, deficit-sensitivity, fixed Newton-CG, support-only L-BFGS). Every local, quotient, jitter and multiplicative-envelope move returns the start. The one thing that still has slack is (a) a structurally different same-score state — p1564 has only 19.4% zeros and argmax 0.420, so the jitter/sharpening stack has never met that geometry — and (b) resolution growth with jittered 2x refine (F1401 gained where blind upsampling did not, and the record is an exact 2x staircase so pairing degeneracy may be binding). T86 gets its first real design: the capped inverse-sqrt edge-singular family, which reliably builds a fresh ~0.88 hill from Code Zero.

plan.analysis: The record p1566 is locally saturated: every local, lift, and NCG move returns the start. The only recent positive signals are F1413's phase-order restructure on the nearby T11 basin (p1568, +5e-6) and the fact that quotient/lift moves have historically been the largest H2 gains. I bet main slot 1 on applying F1413's front-loaded peak-ladder plus random-window block L-BFGS to the record itself; slot 2 on a half-quotient cascade on the live T11 basin p1568, where the geometry differs and a lift has not been tried. For exploration, T25's H14 is smooth and dense; none of its moves forced flatness. I bet on the proven gamma-compressed flat-target alternating projection (F690/F580) to convert H14 toward a higher, flatter basin.

experiments.hypothesis: F1413 showed that front-loading a tight peak-window beta-ladder, then alternating it with random-window block L-BFGS, buys >5e-6 on an H2 basin that other moves could not move. p1566 still spends much of its budget in half-res and NCG phases that either fail or return only +1e-7; replacing them with F1413's phase order should attack its broad near-max region (only 16.5% of knots within 0.1% of max) more effectively.

Phase A: for pad in (0.06,0.05,0.04,0.03,0.02), run _lbfgs_block on the peak window with beta=1e7 (iters 250), then again on the same window with beta=0. Phase B: repeat 6 rounds while cpu < deadline-6 s: pick a random contiguous window of length uniform in [N/20, N/6] with uniform center; run _lbfgs_block(window, 250, beta=1e6) then _lbfgs_block(window, 250, beta=0); then run _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=200); accept only if R_of increases and print round, center, length, R. Finish with _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=1e8, 400), _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0.0, 400), then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.05,0.03), iters=300). Return best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941444-0.941447. Tell: R rises above the start by more than 1e-6 immediately after Phase A (front-loaded peak ladder), and the f*f argmax moves by at least 0.01; if Phase A alone is flat and only Phase B moves R, the peak region was already saturated and random-window global moves are the operative mechanism.

experiments.hypothesis: p1568 is the only recent gain on the H2/T11 basin (+5e-6, argmax 0.209, N=84992), but F1413 only changed phase order. The half-resolution quotient polish/cascade produced the largest gains ever on the H2 lineage (F1180/F1235, +23e-6 on p1306), and it has not been tried on p1568. If p1568's fine structure has any quotient degeneracy, optimizing its half-quotient and lifting back should move it where full-resolution block moves are flat.

plan.analysis: The record has been flat at 0.941441 for ~20 generations: every lift, quotient, jitter, pool, coarsening and phase-reorder has returned the start unchanged on the 0.22-argmax comb states. But p1579 (gen 388) is a *different* point on H2: argmax at 0.496 (centred) and 41.1% zeros, not the saturated 0.223/67% comb that all the failures were tried on. So moves that were dead on the old states are legitimately untried here. I am betting that (a) the remaining deficit lives at a small set of f*f knots (shoulders/toes) whose feeding h-cells are never freed by the contiguous, argmax-centred windows used so far, and (b) on T85 (H22, 0.941267) the shrink move fails because it is a single deterministic pass — support re-selection needs restarts at the coarse level where a cell flip moves far more mass.

experiments.hypothesis: R = 1 - int g(M-g)/(M int g), so the whole loss sits on the knots where g(M-g) is large (the plateau shoulders/toes). Every window used so far is contiguous in h-space and centred on the f*f argmax, so the h-cells that actually feed those deficit knots are usually fixed and L-BFGS is pushing on a plateau whose binding knots it cannot move. Freeing exactly the deficit-feeding cells (a non-contiguous mask) should finally move them.
experiments.change: Start from p1579's code, keep all helpers. Loop while process_time() < deadline-5: (1) Lf = _knots(best); M = Lf.max(); d = Lf*(M-Lf); take the smallest set of knot indices whose cumulative d covers 90% of d.sum(); (2) map each such knot j (remember Lf = [0, conv, 0], so knot j corresponds to conv index j-1) to the h cells i and (j-1)-i for all i, take the union, dilate by +/-2 cells, clip to [0,N); (3) run _lbfgs_block(best, mask, 300, deadline, beta=b) for b in (1e6, 1e7, 1e8, 0.0), then _peak_ladder(best, deadline, pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=200); (4) accept the candidate only if R_of(cand) > R_of(best)+1e-14 and print the new R together with the deficit share carried by the masked knots (sum d[masked]/sum d). Do not exit early; keep cycling with fresh masks from the new best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941443-0.941446 (record 0.941441452). Tell: R rises above the start within the first masked round, the masked knots' deficit share falls from ~0.90, and nearmax5 (currently 0.3467) rises; if the mask is always the whole support or R never moves, the deficit is not knot-local and this line is closed at this N.

experiments.hypothesis: p1579's f*f still has only 34.67% of knots within 5% of max, so the shoulders (where g crosses M/2) are the remaining loss. All previous schedules free one window at a time or a contiguous block, so mass cannot be exchanged between the two shoulders and the centre in one step. Jointly freeing left tail + peak window + right tail, and allowing the support to grow at both ends with geometric decay (the only move that repeatedly bought ~1e-6, F1243/F1014), should extend the plateau rather than shave the peak.
experiments.change: Start from p1579's code. Compute Lf=_knots(best), M=Lf.max(); iL = first knot index with Lf>=0.5M, iR = last such index. Build mask = union of arange(0, iL+pad1) and arange(iR-pad1, N) (pad1 = max(64, N//50)) plus the pad=0.05 peak window. Run _lbfgs_block on this joint mask with beta ladder (1e5,1e6,1e7,1e8,0.0), 300 iters each; accept if R improves. Then a tail-growth round: m = max(16, N//100); append m cells at each end filled with eps*exp(-k/tau), eps = 1e-3*h.mean(), tau in (m/3, m, 3m); re-run the same joint mask optimization at the new N (rebuilding iL,iR) and accept the grown array only if R improves. Alternate the two rounds until deadline-4, then a final _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04)) and a beta=0 all-pos polish.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941443-0.941448. Tell: accepted rounds show iL moving left and iR moving right (plateau widening) and/or the half-max crossing knot values rising; gains should appear only on the tail-growth rounds, and nearmax5 should end above 0.3467. If every joint-mask round returns the start and growth always lowers R, the support really is optimal at this N.

experiments.hypothesis: T85's shrink-to-coarser-N move returned the start unchanged because it was a single deterministic shrink-and-prolong: at coarse N the basin is smooth enough that plain polish reproduces the same shape. At N/2 and N/4 a single cell flip moves far more mass, so *combinatorial* moves (zero revival, edge thickening, banded multiplicative kicks) plus restart-averaging should actually change the coarse structure, and 19.8% of p1574's cells are exact zeros so there is real support freedom to exploit.
experiments.change: Start from p1574's code. For frac in (0.5, 0.25): build c = mass-preserving rebin of best to N*frac (sum pairs for 0.5, sum quadruples for 0.25). Then run K=4 restarts at coarse resolution: for k in range(4), copy c, apply a random kick = multiply a random contiguous band of width 20-40% of the coarse array by exp(sigma*randn) with sigma in (0.05,0.10,0.20) and revive a random 15% of the zero cells at amplitude 10**uniform(-3,-1) * mean; polish each restart with _lbfgs_all_pos(cand, 300, deadline, beta=1e6), then beta=1e7, then beta=0, then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06)); keep the best coarse candidate by coarse R. Prolong that candidate back with _prolong(cand, N), run peak ladder (0.06,0.04) plus beta=1e8 and beta=0 polishes, and accept into `best` only if R_of exceeds the track start; print coarse R and prolonged R per restart. Keep best of everything found (never return worse than the start).
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.94130-0.94135 on T85 (track best 0.941267). Tell: at least one coarse restart beats its coarse start by >1e-5 at coarse R and survives prolongation with full-N R > 0.941267; the winning restart should show a zero-fraction change of at least 0.02 versus the plain shrink. If all coarse restarts lose 1e-4 or more and never recover after prolongation, coarse-level support search is dead on H22.

plan.analysis: The record is a saturated H2 comb: full-array polish and deficit masks are dead on p1579 (F1420/F1421), while F1180's half-resolution quotient polish is the strongest historical structural move and p1579 does not use it. Main bet: add a warm-started half-quotient ladder to p1579. T85/H22 is denser (19.8% zeros) and has never had the dense-basin beta-sharpening/prune/interlace recipe (F1356); its coarse-shrink path is dead (F1422). Exploration bet: flip D4 away from argmax/softmax to a hard epigraph with an auxiliary peak variable, so near-max knots all see gradient.

experiments.hypothesis: p1579 uses only peak-window and random-window full-N polishes; it has never had F1180's half-resolution quotient polish, which is the best-paying structural move on H2. Polishing c=h[0::2] doubles the effective mass per variable, exposes parity degrees of freedom, and a repeat-lift back to N can break the current full-N local optimum.
experiments.change: Start from p1579 and keep its helpers and final fallback. Insert a new quotient phase before Phase A, taking ~35% of the budget. Loop up to 4 rounds while time remains: c = best[0::2]; run _lbfgs_all_pos(c, 250, slice_deadline, beta=1e5), then beta=1e6, then beta=1e7, then beta=0; at half resolution run _lbfgs_block with _peak_window(c, pad_frac=p) for p in (0.30, 0.15, 0.08), beta=1e7 then beta=0; lift by np.repeat(c,2); run _lbfgs_all_pos(best_lifted, 200, slice_deadline, beta=0) and _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=200). Accept the lifted result only if R_of improves, print each quotient round's half-R and lifted R. Then run p1579's existing Phase A/Phase B with remaining time, using the improved best as start.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941444-0.941449. Tell: at least one quotient round reports half-resolution R above its own start and after np.repeat+full polish R exceeds 0.941441; if all lifted rounds return the same R, half-quotient is also degenerate on p1579's phase.

experiments.hypothesis: T85/H22 is a denser basin (19.8% zeros, argmax 0.315) than H2, so H2's quotient/shrink moves may not apply, but F1356's dense-basin recipe — repeated high-beta sharpening, small pruning, and interlace upsampling — lifted the structurally similar H14 basin. It has not been tried on p1574; its failed child p1582 was coarse-N restarts, a different move.
experiments.change: Start from p1574. Run 3 rounds, each with a fresh deadline slice: (1) high-beta sharpening ladder using _lbfgs_all_pos with betas (1e6,1e7,1e8,0), 200 iters each; (2) prune by setting the smallest 3% of positive heights to zero; (3) run _peak_ladder(pads=(0.08,0.05,0.03), iters=250). After round 1, if time remains, do one interlace 2x upsample: h2[2i]=h[i]*(1+eps*r_i), h2[2i+1]=h[i]*(1-eps*r_i) with eps=0.02 and r_i random ±1, then L1-normalize and run the same sharpening/prune/peak cycle. Keep the best over original N and upsampled N and return best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.94130-0.94134 on T85 (track best 0.941267). Tell: zero fraction rises and nearmax5 increases while R rises above 0.941267; if the beta ladder only reproduces p1574, H22 is saturated under dense-basin sharpening.

experiments.hypothesis: All H2 programs handle the inf-norm with the exact argmax knot or a log-sum-exp surrogate, so only the single argmax or a very peaked softmax set controls the peak term. A hard epigraph with auxiliary t >= all f*f knots gives every near-max knot a barrier gradient and lets the optimizer lower the whole top instead of chasing one knot.
experiments.change: Start from p1579 and keep its phases. Replace the exact-max/softmax peak term in one new epigraph polish phase with variables (h, u), t = max(Lf) + exp(u), initial u = log(0.02*max(Lf)). Objective F = -log(num) + 2 log(sum h) + log(t) - mu * sum_{j in J} log(max(t - Lf_j, 1e-12)), where J = knots with Lf_j >= 0.9*max(Lf). Gradient: gLf = -dq/num + mu/(t-Lf) on J (zero elsewhere), backprop to h; dF/du = (1/t - mu*sum_J 1/(t-Lf_j))*exp(u). Run L-BFGS on concatenated (h,u) with mu ladder 1e-2,1e-3,1e-4,1e-6, 150 iters each, clipping h>=0. Compare R after each mu; keep best. Then resume p1579's Phase A/B with remaining budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941443-0.941447. Tell: t settles just above the current max, several distinct near-max knots contribute barrier gradients, and R rises during the epigraph phase (not only in the final polish); if R is unchanged or falls throughout, the epigraph is not adding information beyond the softmax ladder.

info.open_why: Need the actual code/strategy of the T25 H14 best (p1577) and T85 H22 best (p1574) to plan concrete experiments, plus the key findings on what structural moves pay on H2 (F1413, F1429, F1180) and the dense-basin recipe (F1356) for the T25 climb.

plan.analysis: H2 at 0.941441 has absorbed ~30 targeted attempts in ten generations: peak-gradient reformulations (F1427 epigraph, F1432 anchor hinge), head/tail blocks (F1431), deficit masks (F1420), half-res quotient (F1426), resampling (F1435), broad-LAV (F1434) — all returned the start. So the peak term is not the blocker; only structural moves (lifts, rotations, randomized splits) have ever paid, and each paid once, ~1e-6 to 4e-6. I therefore bet on (1) a stride-3 quotient rotation, since only stride 2 was ever rotated (F1464) and the coarse quotient is where the signal lives (F1180); (2) for T87, the untried D4 alternative — pin the argmax index and differentiate through that fixed knot instead of the running argmax; (3) for a new hill, a modulated-envelope family with exact gradients, a shape no known hill occupies.

experiments.hypothesis: F1180 shows the coarse quotient carries the signal and F1464 shows rotating over the even/odd/averaged pairings buys +4e-6 at stride 2. Stride 3 has never been rotated, and polishing each residue class h[r::3] independently at 1/3 resolution moves 3x more mass per L-BFGS step than the full-N gradient can, which is exactly what a saturated 41%-zero comb needs. Recombining the three polished residues gives a genuinely new full-N state that the existing random-window loop can then repair.
experiments.change: Keep every helper and phase of p1579. Insert a new phase consuming ~45% of the budget, before Phase B: for r in (0,1,2): c = best[r::3] (length m); polish c in place with _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=1e6, 150 iters), then (beta=1e7, 150), then (beta=0.0, 150), all bounded by the phase deadline; then rebuild h_new of length N with h_new[3*i+r] = c_polished[i] for i < len(c) and the other two residues copied from best; run _lbfgs_all_pos(h_new, beta=1e6, 150), _lbfgs_all_pos(beta=0.0, 150), then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.06,0.04), iters=200); accept only if R_of strictly exceeds the current best, printing the residue index and both R values. Then continue p1579's Phase B random-window loop and the final beta/peak polish on whatever survives.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941443-0.941446. Tell: at least one residue's coarse polish raises R(c) above R_of(best[r::3]) and the recombined full-N R after the two polishes exceeds the start; if all three residues return unchanged and the recombined state is rejected, the stride-3 quotient is already at its own optimum and the comb's structure is fixed at every scale.

experiments.hypothesis: T87's diagnosis (the exact-max gradient sees one knot and the argmax flips between the two near-tied maxima at ~0.32 and ~0.50 of the support) survived F1427 and F1432, which both kept re-anchoring at the *running* argmax and penalising excess. The untried D4 alternative is to pin the peak location: choose one knot index a once, differentiate through Lf[a] as if it were the max, and let every other knot rise freely toward it. That is a smooth, well-posed objective with no hinge and no barrier, and it removes the tie-flip noise entirely.
experiments.change: Keep all helpers and phases of p1579. Add _fun_grad_pin(h, a): identical to _fun_grad but with m replaced by the fixed index a (gLf = -dq/num; gLf[a] += 1/Lf[a]; val = -log(num) + 2log(s) + log(Lf[a])). Add _lbfgs_pin(h0, a, maxiter, deadline) as an L-BFGS-B over all non-negative heights using that gradient. New phase (~40% of budget): a = argmax knot index of best; for rep in range(3): h_try = _lbfgs_pin(best, a, 300, phase_deadline); if R_of(h_try) > R_of(best): best = h_try; a = argmax knot index of best (print rep, a, R). plan.analysis: The record 0.941441 has absorbed every polish-style move: stride-3 residues, pinned argmax, 2x linear upsampling, doubled resolution, head/tail blocks all returned the start unchanged. What remains untested on H2 is the *handling of the inf-norm itself*: every hill uses a beta-softmax surrogate (D3), which smears gradient over the whole profile, yet the record has only 16.5% of knots within 0.1% of max, so softmax distortion is significant. The correct alternative is the Clarke subgradient of log(max): average 1/L_i over all knots tied with the max. That is cheap, exact, and never tried in that form. On the side tracks, T88 died from an unenforced CPU budget, not from its family; and L3's spiky asymmetric comb (max/mean 185, argmax 0.787) has never received the stride-2 half-quotient lift that is H2's single best-paying move.

experiments.hypothesis: Every H2 program handles ||f*f||_inf with a log-sum-exp surrogate (D3), and the record's top is narrow (16.5% of knots within 0.1% of max), so the softmax flattens gradient across the whole profile and blurs exactly the few knots that set the constraint. Using the exact Clarke subgradient of log(max) — 1/L_i averaged over only the knots tied with the maximum within a relative tolerance tau — keeps the objective exact while still smoothing argmax flips, which single-knot pinning (F1438) failed to do.
experiments.change: Keep all helpers of p1602. Add `_lbfgs_tie(h0, iters, deadline, tau)` copying `_lbfgs_all_pos` but with this fg (bounds [0,None), same callback/timeout guard). New phase consuming ~50% of the budget, right after the base's Phase A: for tau in (1e-12, 1e-10, 1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4): ht=_lbfgs_tie(best,300,deadline-5,tau); ht=_lbfgs_block(ht, _peak_window(ht,pad_frac=0.04,extra=128), 250, deadline-4, beta=0.0); ht=_peak_ladder(ht, deadline-3, pads=(0.05,0.03), iters=200); accept only if R_of(ht) > R_of(best)+1e-14. Print tau, K, and the R delta each pass. Spend the remaining time in the existing random-window Phase B and final full-array polish (beta 1e8 then 0). Return best.

experiments.hypothesis: F1442's modulated-envelope family was never actually tested: p1606 was killed at 85 s because the N=65536 x 32-sine-term parametrisation with per-iteration FFT backprop was too expensive and no deadline was enforced. Shrinking N to 16384 and the series to 8 terms cuts cost by ~16x, and a hard internal deadline plus an always-valid incumbent turns the experiment into a real test of whether a modulated comb can reach a new hill.
experiments.change: From Code Zero: build N=16384, t=i/(N-1). Parameter vector p = (c_1..c_8, A, log f, phi). h(p) = clip(exp(sum_k c_k sin(pi k t)) * (1 + A*cos(2*pi*f*t + phi)), 1e-12, None). Exact gradient: obtain g_h from `_backprop(-dq/num ...)` i.e. reuse `_fun_grad` on the clipped h to get d(-logR)/dh, then chain rule through h = E*(1+A cos): dE/dc_k = E*sin(pi k t); dE/dA = E*cos(...); dE/dphi = -E*A*sin(...); dE/d(log f) = -E*A*2*pi*f*t*sin(...) (f = exp(log f) kept in [5, 400]). Homotopy over A amplitude: A_fix in (0.05,0.15,0.30,0.50), each stage L-BFGS-B (maxiter 150) on (c, log f, phi) with A fixed, callback raising TimeoutError at deadline-1.5. HARD BUDGET: set model_deadline = t0 + 0.55*budget and never call an optimiser past it; also build an analytic fallback at entry (h_i = sqrt(N)(sqrt(i+1)-sqrt(i)) at N=8192) and keep it as the incumbent so a valid array is always returned. After the parametric fit, take the best h and spend the rest of the budget on: 2x asymmetric lift (h2[2i]=h*w0, h2[2i+1]=h*w1 with w log-normal sigma 0.3, folded back), then beta ladder 1e6/1e7/0 on the peak window, keeping only improvements. plan.analysis: The record has been flat at 0.941441459 for ~10 generations; every morsel costs ~1e-6. The two live tracks both just reported nulls, but their nulls are informative: T89's revival used 0.01*mean with a ±32 window (mass 100x too small to survive a full polish, and the window forbade the rest of the array from rebalancing), and T87 has now failed with two *time-varying* peak surrogates (Clarke tolerance, window-averaged max) — in both the definition of the max flips between L-BFGS iterations, so the curvature model is built on a moving objective. The untested variants are therefore: (a) revival at real mass with a full-array polish, (b) a *pinned* max set, fixed for the whole L-BFGS call, and (c) a support-width move with real mass (F1449's 1e-6 halo could do nothing). All three are structural, not finer polish.

experiments.hypothesis: The record's f*f ramp length is set by the two outermost support cells, and F1449 failed only because its halo was seeded at 1e-6*mean (128 cells of negligible mass, neither able to raise the ramp nor to be rejected fairly). Giving the support real extra mass at ~1x the boundary height, or conversely trimming the near-dead outer cells, changes the ramp geometry — a global degree of freedom no peak-window/random-window polish can reach.

Add `_trim(h, k)`: drop up to k cells from each end while h[end] < 0.002*h.max(). Keep p1610's Phase A (~10%) and its existing final polish, but compress Phase B/T so everything up to Phase S ends at 0.55*budget. New Phase S from 0.55 to 0.90 of the budget, candidates in this order: (i) _pad(best, int(0.015*N)), (ii) _pad(best, int(0.03*N)), (iii) _trim(best, int(0.02*N)). For each candidate: _lbfgs_all_pos(cand, 800, dl, beta=0.0), then _peak_ladder(cand, dl, pads=(0.06,0.03), iters=250) (beta 1e7 then 0), then _lbfgs_all_pos(cand, 400, dl, beta=0.0); accept into best only if R_of(cand) > R_of(best)+1e-12 and print the new N, argmax_frac and nearmax5. experiments.hypothesis: F1451 is not evidence that the zero set is score-irrelevant, only that a 0.01*mean revival polished inside a ±32 window cannot express a better support: the revived mass is ~100x below the smallest useful height and the window blocks the compensating motion everywhere else. Reviving at the mean active height, at zeros under the *top* band (0.9-1.0 of max) where the deficit actually sits, and then polishing the entire array with a beta ladder lets the support genuinely migrate and be judged.

Then polish the FULL array, not a window: `_lbfgs_all_pos(cand, 400, dl, beta=1e5)`, then beta=1e7 (400), then beta=0 (600), then `_peak_ladder(cand, dl, pads=(0.05,0.03), iters=200)`. Print zero_frac before/after, n_revived and the net R delta of each round.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941443-0.941446 on the track's own scale. Tell: zero fraction shifts by at least 1.5% and at least one round survives the full-array polish with a positive net delta. If both rounds return to the same R after a full polish, then the support pattern on H22 is provably tight rather than merely frozen, which is a real finding about D6.

experiments.hypothesis: T87's two failures share one mechanism: the set of knots carrying the 1/L weight is recomputed at every function evaluation, so as the argmax flips between near-tied knots the L-BFGS two-loop curvature model is fitted to a piecewise-changing gradient and can never take a coherent step. Freezing the tie set for the duration of each short L-BFGS call (and annealing the freeze tolerance outward-in) gives a smooth, honest objective within each call while still tracking the true max between calls.

plan.analysis: H22/H2 is saturated at 0.941441: every local move (tie/Clarke gradients, zero revival, head/tail blocks, support width, plateau objectives, resample lifts) returns the same value. p1610's only real jump came from an escape move, and the one escape move that ever paid on this lineage is the Gaussian spectral-smoothing phase (F1477, +3e-6) — it has never been applied to p1610's dense 18.6%-zero state, so I bet a full filter sweep (smoothing and unsharp, sigma/alpha chosen by direct R before polishing) is the cheapest live direction on the main line. plan.analysis: The record basin H22/H2 (0.941441) is now demonstrably stiff: every structural edit tried on it — exact Clarke/tie gradients (F1443, F1455), plateau objectives (F1458), zero revival in three variants (F1451, F1456, F1461), head/tail blocks (F1431), support-width ramps (F1457), 2x refine ladders (F1459, F1462), Gaussian/unsharp smoothing (F1460) — returns the start unchanged. The only repeatable gains are large-coherent-move polishes (F1117, F1180 quotient cascade) worth 1e-6..1e-5. So slot 1 bets on a low-dimensional reparametrisation that lets big coherent mass moves be taken at full N (per-block log gains with exact backprop), which no H22 program has tried. Slots 2 and 3 are track continuations: T88's smooth modulated-envelope hill stopped at 28 s of 60 and never tried spiky limits; T90 died to the CPU limit and needs a cheap, always-valid new family (mixed-radix multiplicative cascade).

experiments.hypothesis: On H22 every per-cell local move is frozen, but the mass distribution over large chunks is still free: if we reparametrise by B contiguous block log-gains x_b (h_i -> h_i*exp(x_b)) and take L-BFGS steps in x with the exact chain-rule gradient d(-logR)/dx_b = sum_{i in b} h_i * d(-logR)/dh_i, a single step moves a whole block coherently instead of being vetoed by the frozen neighbours. info.open_why: See the record program's exact code/plan, T88's base and its founding finding F1442, and the support-handling findings F1451/F1443 plus T89's base to design a non-repeating main and two exploration experiments.

plan.analysis: The record is frozen on H22 at 0.941442: per-cell moves, block log-gains, zero revival, tie/softmax peak objectives and finite-resolution upsamples all return the start unchanged, so the remaining freedom is coarse-scale mass redistribution (H22 was itself founded by shrink-polish-prolong, a mechanism its recent descendants dropped) or a walk along the exactly-flat level set. Slot 1 bets on mass-preserving coarsening with jittered re-splits; slot 3 on Metropolis acceptance of equal-R perturbations plus short polishes; slot 2 continues T28's flat-top basin where noisy interp lifts failed but exact 2x duplication (identical R, new pair-splitting freedom) was never tried.

experiments.hypothesis: Every move at full N is frozen on H22, but H22 itself was found by shrinking the array, re-optimizing where each L-BFGS step moves a large mass fraction, and prolonging back; the recent descendants (p1619-p1637) dropped that phase for zero-set and block-gain moves, so retrying it with mass-preserving block-sum coarsening and jittered re-splits is a genuinely different, coarse-scale direction.
experiments.change: Keep p1637 unchanged (all helpers, Phase A, final polish). Replace Phase G with a coarsening cycle. Add `_coarsen(h,k)`: zero-pad h to a multiple of k, reshape to (nb,k), sum along axis 1 (mass-preserving). For k in (16, 8, 4, 3), each until the phase deadline: c=_coarsen(best,k); run `_lbfgs_all_pos(c, 250, deadline, beta)` for beta in (1e6, 1e7, 0.0); then prolong: for each coarse cell i draw log-normal weights u_j (np.random.lognormal(0,0.3,k), normalized to sum 1) and set children h2[i*k+j]=c[i]*u_j, cropping back to the original N and renormalising mass; then full-N `_lbfgs_all_pos(h2, 300, dl, beta=1e8)`, `_lbfgs_all_pos(_, 400, dl, beta=0.0)` and `_peak_ladder(_, dl, pads=(0.05,0.03), iters=250)`; accept only if R_of improves by >1e-14, else discard and retry with a fresh jitter seed (up to 3 seeds per k). Print k, seed, and the delta-R after the plain polish. Reserve ~15% of the budget for the existing final polish (beta 1e8 then 0).
experiments.prediction: Target 0.941444-0.941448. Tell: at least one k prints a strictly positive delta that survives the plain polish; if every k returns exactly 0.941442 with delta-R=0, coarse-scale mass redistribution is not free on H22 either and the line is a true continuum optimum at this N.

experiments.hypothesis: H12 is a flat-top smooth basin (33% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max, 27% zeros, max/mean 27.95) whose stall is resolution, not sharpness; p1521's interlace upsample used per-cell weights 0.5+0.2*sin(random), which perturbs R before polishing and never survived. Exact 2x duplication (`np.repeat(h,2)`) gives byte-identical R as a starting point while adding one free degree of freedom per pair, so a subsequent polish can split pairs asymmetrically without the initial damage.
experiments.change: Build on p1521 (keep its helpers, beta ladder, prune, peak polish). Replace the interlace-upsample round with a doubled-grid round repeated twice: h2=np.repeat(best,2) (N doubles, R unchanged); run `_beta_ladder(h2,(1e6,1e7,1e8,0.0),250,dl)`, then peak polish `_lbfgs_block(h2, _peak_window(h2,tol=0.99,pad_frac=0.10,extra=64), 300, dl, beta=1e7)` and `_lbfgs_block(..., beta=0.0)`, then a full `_lbfgs_all_pos(h2,300,dl,beta=0.0)`; keep h2 only if R_of improves by >1e-14, otherwise fall back to best and continue the 3-round sharpening/prune loop at the current N. Spend the whole budget (loop rounds until 2 s before deadline). Print N, R, zero_frac, max/mean per round.
experiments.prediction: Target 0.8835-0.887 (from 0.881901). Tell: R rises immediately after the first doubled-grid polish while zero_frac stays near 27% and max/mean climbs toward 40+; if the doubled grid returns exactly 0.881901 with no gain, H12's flat top is resolution-saturated and the next exploration should attack the ramp shape instead.

experiments.hypothesis: Every known hill refuses stochastic perturbation on H22 and instead relies on deterministic ladders; since all gradients there are ~0, the objective has exactly flat directions, and a Metropolis walk that accepts equal-R moves can travel along that level set to points whose higher-order structure admits a better polish, which single-shot perturbations (F1374, F1461) could not reach.
experiments.change: Flip D5: keep p1637's helpers and Phase A, but replace Phases G and the peak ladder with a Metropolis plateau walk. State = best copy. Loop until 5 s before the deadline: propose a coherent perturbation, cycling randomly among (a) smooth tilt h*exp(a*cos(2*pi*m*t+phi)) with a in {1e-4,1e-3}, m in {1..8}, random phi; (b) a random contiguous block [i, i+L), L in {N/200, N/50}, multiplied by exp(a) with a in {+-1e-4, +-1e-3}; (c) a random run of 4-64 zeros raised to 0.01*mean(h). Compute r=R_of(cand); accept (state=cand, cur_r=r) if r >= cur_r (accept exact ties, i.e. flat moves), and update best if r > bestR+1e-14. Every 150 accepted moves, cheap-polish the state: `_lbfgs_all_pos(state, 60, dl, beta=1e7)` then `_lbfgs_all_pos(_, 60, dl, beta=0.0)`; if that beats bestR, set state=best=that and print the gain. End with `_lbfgs_all_pos(best,400,dl,beta=1e8)` and `_lbfgs_all_pos(best,400,dl,beta=0.0)`. Print accepted/total, cur_r, bestR every 1000 steps.

D1.everyone: minimise -log(num)+2log(sum h)+log(max knot) with exact analytic gradient (log-domain objective, linear-space heights)
alternatives: directly maximise R with a constrained/penalty formulation on ||f*f||_inf as an explicit hard constraint
optimise the ratio in a fully log-parametrised height space (log h) rather than linear h with clipping

D2.decision: how the inf-norm (peak) constraint is handled
D2.everyone: soft-max / log-sum-exp surrogate with a beta ladder (betas ~1e3-1e10) plus peak-window block polishes, never an exact hard constraint
alternatives: exact hard constraint via projected/active-set method enforcing max knot fixed at every step
multi-knot tie objective (average over all knots within tau of max) as the primary constraint rather than LSE

D3.everyone: optimise over all N entries with nonnegativity bounds, letting L-BFGS-B drive entries to exact zero (implicit sparsity), no explicit support re-selection
alternatives: explicit combinatorial support selection (greedy add/drop of nonzero cells) alternated with continuous optimisation
fixed sparse support with periodic exact-zero revival/pruning sweeps as a first-class stage

D5.everyone: rely on beta-sharpening ladder, peak-window block polishes, and coherent block-gain (log-gain per contiguous block) moves; no stochastic perturbation
alternatives: stochastic perturbations (jitter active cells, random tilts) with Metropolis/restart acceptance

plan.analysis: H22 is a hard plateau: per-cell, block-gain, coarsening, Metropolis, tie-gradient, and zero-set moves all return unchanged. The remaining hope on the main line is to change the objective geometry, not the local mover: fit a gamma-compressed flat target for g=f*f, then polish exact R. T91's Metropolis walk accepted ties but followed exact R, which is flat; continuing it needs a surrogate with actual slope, so use a blurred-g R for acceptance. L3/H8 is still climbing and has a proven randomized asymmetric 2x split move; apply it repeatedly to p1612 with beta-ladder polishing.

experiments.hypothesis: On H22 exact-R L-BFGS is frozen because the max constraint and plateau make the usable gradient tiny, but R=1 iff g=f*f is flat. Minimising ||g - M*(g/M)^gamma||^2 with gamma<1 directly lifts the low body of g while holding the peak, giving a strong descent direction that exact-R polishing can then convert into a real gain.
experiments.change: Keep p1637's helpers, Phase A and final polishes. Replace Phase G with a target-fitting phase. Compute g = _knots(best)[1:-1] and M=g.max(). For gamma in (0.75, 0.6, 0.45): build target gt = M*(clip(g/M,0,1)**gamma); zero gt outside the current support plus a small halo. Optimise h by L-BFGS-B on F(h)=sum((conv(h,h)-gt)^2)/sum(gt^2) + 1e-8*sum(h^2), with analytic gradient via _backprop of 2*(conv(h,h)-gt), bounds [0,None], 300 iters or remaining time. Then run _lbfgs_all_pos(cand,250,dl,beta=1e7), _lbfgs_all_pos(cand,350,dl,beta=0), and accept only if R_of(cand)>R_of(best)+1e-14. Print gamma, target-loss, R and delta. Spend leftover time on the base's final beta-1e8 + plain polish, hard stop 0.97*budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941446-0.941455. Tell: target loss falls substantially and at least one gamma survives the exact-R polish with a positive delta above 1e-6; if every fitted candidate polishes back to 0.941442 exactly, H22 is locally isolated under target reshaping and a new hill is required.

experiments.hypothesis: p1642's walk accepted exact-R ties but exact R is flat to machine precision on H22, so it drifted without finding a better point. A blurred-autoconvolution surrogate has genuine slope between nearby knots; walking uphill on the blurred R and periodically projecting back to exact R should convert plateau drift into a real R gain.
experiments.change: Keep p1642's Phase A and polishes. Replace its exact-R Metropolis acceptance with a surrogate walk. Define g = _knots(state)[1:-1]; smooth with a Gaussian kernel sigma in {1.5,3.0,6.0} knots; compute R_blur from the smoothed g using the same knot formula. In the walk, propose p1642's three move types but accept if R_blur(cand) >= R_blur(state) (allow ties), with a short deterministic cooling: sigma cycles 6->3->1.5 every ~400 accepted moves. Every 150 accepted moves, polish exact R with _lbfgs_all_pos(state,60,dl,beta=1e7) then beta=0; update best only when exact R_of(p)>bestR+1e-14. Print sigma, R_blur, exact R, and accepted count. Keep the final beta-1e8 + plain polish.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941444-0.941450 on T91. Tell: R_blur rises smoothly and the periodic exact-R polish produces at least one new strict best; if exact R never exceeds 0.941442 despite large R_blur drift, the plateau has no accessible improving direction under smoothing and T91 should be paused.

experiments.hypothesis: p1612 just became a spiky asymmetric comb (11.4% zeros, max/mean 185), so its fine-scale structure is still responsive, but deterministic stride-2 quotient moves are exhausted. plan.analysis: H22 (0.941442) is saturated to machine precision: exact-R L-BFGS, block-gain, block-sum coarsening, gamma-target fitting, exact-R and blurred Metropolis walks all return the start unchanged. The only structural moves that ever paid on H22 were the shrink-rebuild cycle that founded it and 1-3e-6 one-shot edits. So the main slot should try the one concrete structural edit that just worked on another hill and was never run on H22: F1480's randomized asymmetric 2x split (which bought +3e-6 on L3). T91 has now failed twice at full N (F1473 exact-R ties, F1479 blurred surrogate); I bet a Metropolis walk at coarse resolution (N/8), where R actually has slope, then lifted, can escape where the full-N walk cannot. Slot 3 goes after a genuinely new hill using F293's random multiscale block-start race, which historically produced the only true new basins from Code Zero, carrying over the record chain's beta ladder and peak-window polish.

experiments.hypothesis: p1648's Phase T (gamma<1 target fitting) is dead (F1478), but a randomized asymmetric 2x split with log-normal per-pair weights (F1391/F1480) just produced +3e-6 on L3 and has never been run on H22. The randomization perturbs each pair differently so the subsequent beta/plain polish starts off the exact 2x submanifold, giving L-BFGS the degrees of freedom to redistribute mass that every deterministic lift lacks.
experiments.change: Keep p1648's helpers, Phase A and final polishes. Delete the gamma<1 target-fitting Phase T and replace it with Phase R: loop trial t=1..20 while time remains. Each trial: draw per-cell weights w0,w1 ~ LogNormal(mean 1, sigma = 0.05/0.10/0.20 cycling by t); form h2 of length 2N with h2[2i]=h[i]*w0[i], h2[2i+1]=h[i]*w1[i]; _rescale(h2); run _lbfgs_all_pos(h2, 150, dl, beta=1e7) then _lbfgs_all_pos(...,150,dl,beta=0); evaluate R_of; if strictly > bestR+1e-14, accept h=that (N doubles only on a win) and print trial, sigma, delta, N; otherwise discard and revert to the pre-trial best. Stop trials when 5 s of budget remain, then run the existing final beta-1e8 + plain polish and peak ladder on whatever best is. Hard stop at 0.97*budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941444-0.941450 on H22. Tell: at least one trial prints a strictly positive dR surviving the beta+plain polish (not just the pre-polish split), and at least one accepted trial occurs at sigma=0.05 (mild) rather than only at 0.20. If all 20 trials revert, the H22 plateau is invariant to randomized splitting too, and only a fresh hill helps.

experiments.hypothesis: T91's full-N walks (p1642 exact ties, p1650 blurred g) both failed because R is flat to machine precision at N=104992, so no proposal produces a usable slope (F1473, F1479). The fix is to walk where the landscape is not flat: coarse-average to N/8 (blocks of 8), where each coarse R evaluation changes in measurable steps, climb there with a Metropolis walk, and only lift accepted coarse improves back to full N for exact-R verification. This makes T91's change actually take effect.
experiments.change: Keep p1642's Phase A and final polishes. Replace its full-N Metropolis walk with a coarse-resolution walk. Build c = h.reshape(N//8,8).mean(axis=1) (N_c = N//8). Loop until 10 s before deadline: propose a coherent perturbation of c cycling among (a) smooth tilt c*exp(a*cos(2*pi*m*j/N_c+phi)), a in {1e-3,1e-2,5e-2}, m in {1..8}, random phi; (b) random contiguous block [i,i+L) of c multiplied by exp(a), a in {+-1e-3,+-1e-2,+-5e-2}, L in {N_c/200, N_c/50}; (c) random run of zeros in c raised to 0.1*mean(c); compute R_of(c') and accept (c=c', rc=R) if R_of(c') >= R_of(c) - 1e-9 (accept near-ties), track c_best. Every 200 accepted moves, lift c_best to full N by replicating each coarse cell 8 times with per-copy log-normal jitter (sigma 0.05), _rescale, run _lbfgs_all_pos(cand, 120, dl, beta=1e7) then _lbfgs_all_pos(cand,150,dl,beta=0); if R_of(cand) > bestR+1e-14 accept into global best, reset state to c_best, and print coarse R, lifted exact R, delta. Finish with the base's beta-1e8 + plain polish on the global best.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941444-0.941450 on T91 (from 0.941442). Tell: the coarse walk accepts many moves with visibly nonzero coarse dR (real slope, unlike the full-N walk), and at least one lifted+polished candidate survives at > 0.941442+1e-14. If no lift survives after 20 lift attempts, the plateau is a genuine isolated point at every scale and T91 is exhausted.
