info.open_why: H22 is the record hill and every recent move on it is frozen; I need the exact construction of p1637/p1642 and the precise failure modes of the block-gain, Metropolis, blurred-surrogate, and target-fitting escapes to pick a genuinely different escape for the main slot and a real follow-up for T91.

plan.analysis: H22 (0.941442) is frozen under every local, block, softmax-Clarke, jitter and randomized-split move tried (F1478, F1484, F1443, F1483, F1485). The only moves that ever paid on this lineage were resolution/quotient lifts (p1306 +2.3e-5, p1464 +3e-6, p1453 +2e-6), so slot 1 bets on a genuinely new lift geometry: polyphase (strided) sub-lattice coordinate descent at strides 32/16/8/4, which rotates the relative phases of the comb's sub-lattices — a degree of freedom the contiguous block moves (D6) cannot reach. Slot 2 retries the T92 restart with an analytic capped inverse-sqrt edge family, the only from-Code-Zero route that reliably reaches ~0.88-0.91, since p1656 returned the trivial start unchanged (pipeline failure). Slot 3 pushes H16's dense, razor-peaked basin with gamma-compressed flat-target fitting, which worked on the other smooth hills (F1416) and failed only on the spiky comb H22.

experiments.hypothesis: H22's spikes are phase-locked: every block move so far changed contiguous chunks, and every lift used contiguous ratio decompositions (2, 4, 8, 3:2). The record score's own history shows freeing sub-lattice alignment is the biggest single win on this lineage (exact 2x staircase -> free pairing gave +2.3e-5 on p1306). A polyphase (strided) coordinate move re-optimizes one residue class mod s as its own length-N/s construction and writes it back, which shifts sub-lattice phases at scale s without touching the rest of the comb.
experiments.change: Keep p1648's helpers, Phase A (front-load peak-window beta ladder) and its final polish ladder; delete Phase T (gamma<1 target fitting, dead per F1478) and the random-window Phase B. Add Phase P: rounds t=1..14 while time.process_time() < deadline-4.0. Each round: s = [32,16,32,8,16,32,4,16,32,8,32,16,32,32][t-1]; if N % s != 0, replace s by the largest divisor of N in (32,16,8,4,2); r = (t-1) % s; idx = np.arange(r, N, s); q = best[idx].copy(); polish q as a standalone construction with _lbfgs_all_pos(q, 150, dl, beta) for beta in (1e6, 1e7, 0.0) where dl = deadline-2.5; then rescale q by factor sum(best[idx])/sum(q) (mass-preserving on that residue class), set h2 = best.copy(); h2[idx] = np.clip(q,0,None); then full-array _lbfgs_all_pos(h2, 200, dl, beta=1e7) and _lbfgs_all_pos(h2, 200, dl, beta=0.0), then _peak_ladder(h2, dl, pads=(0.05,0.03), iters=150); accept only if R_of(h2) > R_of(best)+1e-14 else discard. Print 'P t=%d s=%d r=%d dR=%.3e R=%.9f' each round. Spend any remaining time in p1648's final beta=1e8 then plain full polish, and return the best array found.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.941445-0.941455 on H22 (from 0.941442). Tell: at least two rounds print a strictly positive dR (>1e-7) that survives the full-array and peak-ladder polish, and the accepted rounds visibly change zero_frac (18.8%) or argmax_frac (0.436). If every round prints dR=0 for all strides, the comb's sub-lattice phases are exhausted and H22 is closed for polyphase moves too.

experiments.hypothesis: T92's first program failed mechanically, not on its idea: it returned the N=50 trivial start unchanged, so none of its 32 block restarts ever reached the scorer. The only from-Code-Zero routes that reliably found strong new hills are the analytic capped edge-singular families (F450/F474/F715/F1410 all gained, best +0.215), which reach ~0.88-0.91 with a signature completely unlike the 67%-zero comb. Restarting T92 on that family, with an explicit assert that a real array is returned, should found a live non-comb hill.
experiments.change: Ignore `start` (treat as None). Seed: h_i = min(cap, b + A_L*(x_i)^-pL + A_R*(1-x_i)^-pR) for cell centres x_i=(i+0.5)/N, with each cell using the EXACT average of x^-p over [a,b] (for p!=1: (a^{1-p}-b^{1-p})/((p-1)(b-a)); handle |p-1|<1e-6 by log). First do a cheap race at N0=2048: draw 400 random parameter vectors with log-uniform pL,pR in [0.2,1.5], A_L,A_R in [1e-3,1e2], b in [1e-3,1], cap in [1,1e3]; keep the top 5 by R_of at N0. For each survivor: rasterise at N=8192 (exact cell averages) and run the p1648 machinery _lbfgs_all_pos(.,200,dl,beta) for beta in (1e5,1e6,1e7,0.0), then _peak_ladder(pads=(0.10,0.06,0.04), iters=200), keeping the best. Then take the overall best, 2x cumulative-mass upsample to N=16384 and repeat the beta ladder + peak ladder; if time remains, upsample once more to 32768 and polish. Accept/keep the highest R. MUST assert the returned array has size >= 8192 and sum > 0 (guard against the p1656 failure). Print R, zero_frac, max/mean, argmax_frac and nearmax1% at the end.
experiments.prediction: Aim >= 0.90 on a hill whose signature is not the H2/H22 comb (expect zero_frac under 15%, max/mean under 120, and >1% of f*f knots within 1% of max). Tell: a positive score well above the 0.666667 start and a printed signature that differs from both the comb (18.8% zeros / 183 max/mean / 16.5% nearmax) and H16 (8.7% zeros / 27 max/mean). If it lands back on ~0.88 with a dense smooth profile, the edge-singular family is the right restart seed and the track should climb it next.

experiments.hypothesis: H16 is a smooth, dense basin (8.7% zeros, max/mean 27) whose f*f is razor-peaked (only 5.94% of knots within 1% of max, 0.01% within 0.1%), so its deficit is exactly the g(M-g) integral in the top decade. Gamma-compressed flat-target alternating projection attacks that directly and gave +3.2e-4 on the other smooth basins (F1416, F1362); it failed on H22 only because a spiky comb cannot be flattened by a target. Here it has never been tried.
experiments.change: Keep p1250's helpers and its polish routines. Prepend a new Phase F that runs FIRST and then hands off to p1250's existing polish/escalation. Phase F, for gamma in (0.85, 0.70, 0.55): build g = _conv(best), M = g.max(), ratio = clip(g/M,0,1), gt = M*ratio**gamma; zero gt outside [lo,hi] where lo/hi are the min/max index of best>0 expanded by halo = max(4, int(0.01*N)); then minimise _target_loss(h, gt) (same formula as p1648's: sum((g-gt)^2)/sum(gt^2) + 1e-8*sum(h^2), gradient gLf[1:-1]=2*(g-gt)/denom, grad=_backprop(gLf,h)+2e-8*h, bounds [0,None), L-BFGS-B, jac=True, callback timeout at dl=deadline-2, maxiter 200). After each fit run _lbfgs_all_pos(cand, 200, dl, beta=1e7) then beta=0.0, then a pad-0.05 peak-window block polish at beta 1e7 then 0. Accept only if R_of(cand) > R_of(best)+1e-14; print 'F gamma=%.2f tloss=%.4e R=%.9f dR=%.3e'. Give Phase F at most 70% of the budget, then let p1250's own polish finish with whatever time is left. Always return the best array and use the full remaining budget.
experiments.prediction: Aim 0.8178-0.8200 on H16 (from 0.817366). Tell: tloss falls monotonically across the three gammas, at least one gamma gives a positive dR > 1e-5 surviving the beta+peak polish, and the nearmax-1% fraction (now 5.94%) rises while max/mean stays ~27 (i.e. the top is flattened, not sparsified). If all three gammas are rejected, H16's peak is set by its outer support cells rather than by the interior profile and the next move should be an edge/tail extension instead.
